1. The Chhandogya Upanishad places the Chandala among the twice-born (dvija).
2. Untouchability took a formal shape already in the Rigvedic period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Neither statement is correct: the Chhandogya Upanishad refers to the Chandala as a person of despised birth, outside the twice-born; untouchability did not take formal shape in the Rigvedic period but only later.

20.s: The earliest statement of the four varnas is found in the:
20.x: The Purusha Sukta of the Tenth Mandala of the Rigveda first names the four varnas.

20.s: Which of the following varnas was NOT counted among the Dvija (twice-born)?
20.x: Only the upper three varnas had the sacred-thread ceremony; Vratyas and Nishadas were also outside the Dvija.

20.s: In the Vedic age, the head of a Vaishya guild (gana) was called:
20.x: Vaishya guilds were headed by a Shreshthin; the Gramani was the village headman.

20.s: The first reference to money-lending, where the usurer is called 'kusidin', is found in the:
20.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana first mentions the usurer (kusidin).

20.s:
Match the varnas of Later Vedic society with their roles:
List-I (Varna)
a. Brahmana
b. Kshatriya (Rajanya)
c. Vaishya
d. Shudra
List-II (Role)
i. Rulers and warriors
ii. Priests and teachers; the most powerful
iii. Service; no upanayana, no Vedas, no Sabha
iv. Farmers, herders, traders, artisans; the only tribute-payers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
20.x: Brahmana = priests/teachers and most powerful; Kshatriya (also Rajanya) = rulers/warriors; Vaishya = farmers, herders, traders, artisans and the only tribute-payers; Shudra = service, with no upanayana, Vedas or Sabha.

20.s: Which of the followings customs emerged during the post-Vedic period :
20.x: The four ashramas (Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sannyasa) emerged in the post-Vedic period; the four varnas already appear in the Rigveda's Purusha Sukta, and Indra, Surya, Rudra, Maruts are Rigvedic gods. (UPSC 1994 key: ashramas)

20.s: Which of the following custom emerged during the post-Vedic period?
o: Brahmacharya, Grihastha ashrama, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa
20.x: The full set of four ashramas emerged only in the post-Vedic period (first three in the Chhandogya, all four in the Jabala Upanishad / early Dharmasutras); the four varnas appear in the Rigveda's Purusha Sukta and the gods named are Rigvedic.

20.s: How many Ashrams are described in Vedas?
20.x: Four ashramas are described: Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa.

20.s: Which ashrama involved gradual withdrawal from worldly life?
20.x: Vanaprastha was gradual withdrawal; Brahmacharya was Vedic study, Grihastha household life and Sannyasa complete detachment.
xa: The **Grihastha** performs the **Pancha Mahayajnas**.
Sannyasa was **added later**.
Women followed the ashrama chosen by their **husbands**.

20.s: For whom among the following were the Pancha Mahayajnas daily duties?
20.x: The Pancha Mahayajnas were daily duties of the Grihastha, or householder, Ashrama.
20.tq: Apply the social-role clue: regular family and ritual obligations belong to the householder.
xs: The **Pancha Mahayajnas** were daily duties of the **Grihastha** (householder) — option **(3)**.
Exam: **MPPSC 2025**.
xa: The five: **Brahma** (Vedic study), **Deva** (gods), **Pitri** (ancestors), **Bhuta** (living beings), **Nri/Manushya** (guests).
Grihastha duties: **marriage, family, economic** duties.

20.s: All four ashramas are mentioned for the first time in the:
20.x: The Jabala Upanishad first mentions all four ashramas; the Chhandogya refers only to the first three.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four ashramas?
20.x: The four ashramas are Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa; Upanayana is a samskara.

20.s:
Match the Pancha Mahayajnas with what they were meant for:
List-I (Yajna)
a. Brahma-yajna
b. Deva-yajna
c. Pitri-yajna
d. Nri (Atithi)-yajna
List-II (Meant for)
i. Hospitality to guests
ii. Study of the Vedas
iii. Duties towards the ancestors
iv. Offerings to the gods
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
20.x: Brahma = Vedic study; Deva = gods; Pitri = ancestors; Nri/Atithi = hospitality to guests (Bhuta-yajna is for living beings).

20.s:
Assertion (A): Moksha was one of the original trivarga of Purusharthas.
Reason (R): Moksha (liberation) was added to the Purusharthas later, under Upanishadic ideas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
20.x: A is false: the trivarga was Dharma, Artha and Kama. R is true: Moksha was added later under Upanishadic ideas.

20.s: ‘Gotra’ System came into existance since
20.x: Gotra as a clan descended from a common ancestor appeared in Later Vedic (post-Vedic) times; in the Rigveda the word meant only a cow-pen.

20.s: In the context of ancient Indian society, which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three?
20.x: Kula (family), vamsha (lineage) and gotra (clan) are kinship terms; kosa means treasury, so it is the odd one out.

20.s: In the context of ancient Indian society which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three?
20.x: Vansha, gotra and kula are words of the family system; kosa is the treasury, so it does not belong.

20.s: In which text does the word 'gotra' first appear in the sense of lineage?
20.x: Gotra means cow-pen in the Rigveda; the lineage sense first appears in the Atharvaveda.

20.s: The word 'gotra', which first occurs in the Rigveda, literally means:
20.x: Gotra literally means cow-pen; gotra exogamy later barred marriage within the same gotra.

20.s: Who wrote 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953), dividing India into four kinship zones?
20.x: Irawati Karve's 1953 work divided India into four kinship zones.

20.s: There was a provision for reciting which mantra in the Upanayana ritual of the Kshatriya castes?
20.x: The Grihya Sutras prescribe the Gayatri metre for a Brahmana's upanayana, Trishtubh for a Kshatriya and Jagati for a Vaishya.

20.s: What is the total number of Sanskaras?
20.x: Sixteen (shodasha) samskaras are traditionally counted, three before birth and the last (antyeshti) after death; Rocket lists Sanskaras = 16.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about Upanayana:
1. It was denied to Shudras and women.
2. It was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for the upper three varnas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
20.x: Both are correct. Upanayana was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas; Shudras and women were excluded from it.

20.s: Which of the following was true of the pupil in the gurukula system of education?
o: lived separately from the teacher and studied independently
received instruction only from guild heads
20.x: In the gurukula system, pupils lived with the guru. Education was confined largely to the Dvija communities.
20.tq: Test the defining institutional feature of the education system.
xs: In the **gurukula** the pupil **lived with the guru** — option **(1)**.
Education was confined largely to the **Dvija**.
xa: **Brahmacharya** = student stage — Vedic study under a guru.
**Acharya** initiated the pupil and taught **not for a fee**.

20.s: The full description of the Upanayana ceremony is found in which text?
20.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana gives the full description of the Upanayana, the thread ceremony performed for the twice-born.

20.s: In the later Vedic period, the teacher who taught the Veda for a livelihood was called:
20.x: The Upadhyaya taught for a livelihood, while the Acharya taught the Veda without charging a fee.

20.s: Initiation into Vedic study was marked by which samskara?
20.x: Upanayana initiated Vedic study; Chudakarma was only the tonsure of the child.

20.s: What is marriage by purchase called?
20.x: Asura marriage is marriage by purchase: the groom paid a bride price to the girl's family. Arsha involved only a token cow and bull.

20.s: Marriage due to mutual love is called as?
20.x: Gandharva marriage rested on the mutual consent (love) of the two parties; Rakshasa was by capture and Asura by purchase.

20.s: Which Satavahana ruler claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma?
20.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma.
xa: Jati proliferation is **post-Vedic** (Gupta-era diversification).
**Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **pratiloma** = **Chandala**.

20.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the lowest form of marriage in the Dharmashastra classification?
20.x: Paishacha, involving the seduction of a sleeping or intoxicated girl, was regarded as the lowest form of marriage.
20.tq: Use the evaluative description to identify the exceptional form.
xs: **Paishacha** — seduction of a sleeping, intoxicated or incapacitated girl — is the **lowest form** — option **(3)**.
**Daiva, Prajapatya, Arsha** are **approved** forms.
xa: Disapproved forms: **Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa, Paishacha**.
**Brahma** form: father gives daughter with gifts to a learned man.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Paishacha — seduction of a sleeping or intoxicated girl
20.x: Rakshasa marriage involved capture or abduction. Marriage by purchase was known as Asura marriage.
20.tq: Find the swapped meaning among closely related marriage classifications.
xs: **Rakshasa — marriage by purchase** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
**Rakshasa** = marriage by **capture/abduction**; purchase = **Asura**.
The rest are right: **Gandharva** = mutual consent; **Paishacha** = seduction; **Asura** = bride price.
xa: Exam angle: "marriage by purchase of bride" = **Asura** (**APPSC-G1 2012**).
There are **8** forms in Manu and Kautilya.

20.s:
Match the forms of marriage with their nature:
List-I (Form)
a. Daiva
b. Arsha
c. Prajapatya
d. Paishacha
List-II (Nature)
i. Daughter given to the officiating priest as fee
ii. Groom gives a token cow and bull
iii. Seduction of a sleeping or drunk girl
iv. No dowry or bride price; couple jointly perform dharma
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
20.x: Daiva = daughter given to the officiating priest; Arsha = token cow and bull from the groom; Prajapatya = no dowry/bride price, joint dharma; Paishacha = seduction of a sleeping or drunk girl, the lowest form.

20.s: How many forms of marriage are listed by Manu and Kautilya?
20.x: Both list eight forms of marriage, of which the first four were approved.

20.s: In ancient Indian society, 'Anuloma' marriage was between:
o: A higher-varna man and a lower-varna woman
A lower-varna man and a higher-varna woman
20.x: Anuloma was the approved 'with the grain' union; the reverse (lower-varna man, higher-varna woman) was pratiloma.

20.s: In which Upanishad is the famous dialogue of Yagnavalkya and Gargi mentioned?
20.x: Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya in Janaka's court is in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

20.s: The woman eminent in Vedic literature
20.x: Maitreyi, wife of Yajnavalkya, is the learned woman of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad; Shakuntala and Madalasa are epic/Puranic figures.

20.s: Which of the following women is associated with the Upanishads rather than with Rigvedic hymns?
20.x: Gargi and Maitreyi are Upanishadic figures; Apala, Ghosha and Lopamudra composed Rigvedic hymns.

20.s:
Assertion (A): In the Later Vedic period women were cut off from the study of the Vedas.
Reason (R): Women lost the right to the Upanayana, the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
20.x: Both are true and R explains A: Upanayana was the initiation into Vedic study, and Shudras and women were excluded from it.

20.s:
Match the texts with the statements on women found in them:
List-I (Text)
a. Aitareya Brahmana
b. Shatapatha Brahmana
c. Maitrayani Samhita
d. Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
List-II (Statement)
i. Daughter a source of misery; son a protector
ii. Liquor, dice and women are the three evils
iii. The wife is half her husband
iv. Gargi and Maitreyi debate with Yajnavalkya

20.x: Aitareya Brahmana = daughter as misery, son as protector; Shatapatha Brahmana = wife is half her husband; Maitrayani Samhita = liquor, dice and women three evils; Brihadaranyaka Upanishad = Gargi and Maitreyi in Janaka's court.

21.s: What was the name of Janaka's brother?
21.x: In the Ramayana (Bala Kanda) Janaka's younger brother is Kushadhvaja, king of Sankashya, whose daughters married Bharata and Shatrughna. Nimi was the dynasty's founder.

21.s: Who is the Guru of King Janaka?
21.x: In the Ramayana Janaka's guru and family priest is Shatananda, son of sage Gautama (Shatananda Gautama); of the options only Gautama fits. Vishvamitra was a visitor, Vasishtha the Ikshvaku priest, Rishyashringa Dasharatha's ritual priest.

21.s: Who told the stories of Mahabharata to Janamejaya?
21.x: Vaisampayana, Vyasa's disciple, recited the Mahabharata to King Janamejaya at his snake sacrifice.

21.s: Mahabharat is also known by the name
21.x: The Mahabharata's original name was Jaya (Jaya Samhita); it is also called Satasahasri Samhita.

21.s: The Shatasahasri-Samhita is the nickname of which of the following texts?
21.x: The Mahabharata, which grew from the Jayasamhita, is called Satasahasri Samhita for its roughly one lakh verses.

21.s: Sarga, Pratisarga, Vansa, Manvantara and Vanshanucharita are the indicators of -
21.x: Sarga, Pratisarga, Vamsa, Manvantara and Vamshanucharita are the five marks (pancha-lakshana) of the Puranas.

21.s: Originally the Mahabharata was known as –
21.x: The Mahabharata was originally called Jaya or Jayasamhita (about 8,800 shlokas).

21.s: Who was the first law maker?
21.x: Manu, traditional author of the Manusmriti, is regarded as the first law-giver of ancient India.

21.s: According to ancient Indian cosmogonic ideas, the sequential order of the cycle of four epochs (yugas) is
21.x: The yugas run Krita (Satya), Treta, Dvapara, Kali, with declining righteousness.

21.s: According to ancient Indian cosmogonic ideas, the sequential order of the cycle of four epochs (Yugas) is
21.x: The yugas run Krita (Satya), Treta, Dvapara, Kali, with declining righteousness.

21.s: The battle of Mahabharata is believed to have been fought at Kurukshetra for
21.x: The Mahabharata war at Kurukshetra is traditionally said to have lasted 18 days.

21.s: According to Hindu Mythology, which serpent offered himself as a rope for churning the ocean?
21.x: In the Samudra Manthan the serpent Vasuki served as the churning rope round Mount Mandara.

21.s: The ancient place where the narration of entire Mahabharata was read in the conference of 60,000 hermits
21.x: Ugrashrava Sauti narrated the whole Mahabharata to Shaunaka's assembly of sages at Naimisharanya (Naimisha forest).

21.s: Which Kand of Ramayana describes the first meeting of Rama and Hanuman?
21.x: Rama first met Hanuman in the Kishkindha Kanda, when Sugriva sent him to meet Rama and Lakshmana.

21.s: In which language was the ‘Shrimad Bhagavad Gita’ originally written?
21.x: The Bhagavad Gita, part of the Mahabharata, was composed in Sanskrit.

21.s: Who among the following is considered to be the first law-giver of India ?
21.x: Manu, author of the Manusmriti, is regarded as India's first law-giver; Panini was a grammarian, Kautilya a political thinker and Kapila a Sankhya philosopher.

21.s: Who was the grandfather of the Hero of Mahabharata, Arjuna?
21.x: Arjuna's father Pandu was the son of Vichitravirya's wife Ambalika through Vyasa (niyoga), so Vichitravirya is counted as the grandfather.

21.s: The Total Number of Puranas is
21.x: There are 18 Mahapuranas.

21.s: The number of Puranas is–
21.x: There are 18 (Maha)Puranas, such as Matsya, Markandeya, Bhagavata, Vishnu and Vayu.

21.s: Which among the following prohibits remarriage?
21.x: The Manusmriti disapproves of widow remarriage; the Yajnavalkya Smriti and Arthashastra permit remarriage in some cases.

21.s: Complete narration of 'Dasavataras' was given in
21.x: The complete narration of the ten avatars is given in the Bhagavata (Maha-bhagavatam); the Mahabharata and Ramayana tell only some of them.

21.s: Karna exercised his divine weapon, given by Indra, to attack one of the following
21.x: In the Mahabharata Karna had to spend Indra's infallible spear (Vasavi Shakti), kept for Arjuna, on Bhima's son Ghatotkacha on the fourteenth night of the war. (Ghatotkacha here is the epic hero, not the Gupta king.)

21.s: The great law-giver of ancient times was –
21.x: Manu, author of the Manusmriti, is the great law-giver of ancient India; Ambedkar was called the 'Modern Manu'. Moved to ancient history.

21.s: The Ramayana of Valmiki contains about:
21.x: The Ramayana has about 24,000 verses. About one lakh verses in 18 books describes the Mahabharata.

21.s: The epic that contains about one lakh verses arranged in 18 books (parvas) is the:
21.x: The Mahabharata, with about one lakh verses in 18 parvas, is the longest Indian epic.

21.s: Who wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti?
21.x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.
xa: Smritis, like the **Puranas**, are later texts; Vedic texts are **Shruti**.
Tradition counts **18 Mahapuranas**.
**Yajnavalkya** also appears in the **Brihadaranyaka Upanishad** dialogues with **Gargi** and **Maitreyi**.

21.s: The Mahabharata is divided into how many parvas (books)?
21.x: The Mahabharata has 18 parvas; its original core, the Jaya, had 8,800 shlokas.

21.s: Which work is appended to the Mahabharata as its supplement?
21.x: The Harivamsa, on the life of Krishna, is the appendix (khila) of the Mahabharata.

21.s: Consider the following literary sources known as the four Vedas. Which was the earliest text?

21.x: The Rigveda, composed c. 1500 BCE in the Sapta Sindhu, is the oldest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.

21.s: Which one of the following four Vedas contains an account of magical charms and spells?
21.x: The Atharvaveda is the Veda of charms, magic spells and healing; the Sama is chants and the Yajur ritual formulas.

21.s: In which one among the following texts does the term kshetra-patni ('mistress of the field') originate?
21.x: The term kshetra-patni ('mistress of the field') originates in the agricultural hymns of the Atharvaveda (UPSC 2026 key: Atharvaveda).

21.s: The compilation of which among the following is based upon the Rig Veda?
21.x: The Samaveda is compiled almost wholly from Rigvedic verses (all but about 75), set to melody for chanting.

21.s: Which one of the following four Vedas contains an account of magical charms and spells?
21.x: The earliest account of charms and spells is in the Atharvaveda.

21.s: Which among the following Vedas was the earliest composition?
21.x: The Rigveda is the earliest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.

21.s: Rights and Rituals related to Yajnas are mentioned in–
21.x: The Yajurveda is the ritual Veda: it gives the rules and formulas to be observed at sacrifices. The Brahmanas explain rituals but the Veda of yajna rites is the Yajurveda.

21.s: In the Vedic rituals HOTA is associated with the–
21.x: The Hotri (Hota) priest recited the Rigveda; Adhvaryu = Yajur, Udgatri = Sama, Brahman = Atharva.

21.s: ‘Trayi’ is a name for –
21.x: Trayi denotes the first three Vedas: Rig, Yajur and Sama.

21.s: ‘Ayurveda’ that is ‘Science of Life’ appeared first in :
21.x: Ayurveda, the 'science of life', has its prime origin in the Atharvaveda, which describes medicines and herbs.

21.s: Which of the following Vedas is divided into two branches as Krishna and Shukla ?
21.x: The Yajurveda has two branches, Krishna (Black: mantra mixed with prose) and Shukla (White: mantra only).

21.s: Combination of three Vedas has been called ‘Vedatrayi’
21.x: Vedatrayi (Trayi) = Rigveda, Samaveda and Yajurveda; the Atharvaveda is excluded.

21.s: Which one of the following is oldest Veda?
21.x: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.

21.s: Which one of the following is oldest Veda?
21.x: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.

21.s: In which of the following subjects were the Vedic Aryans not proficient?
21.x:
APPSC key: Astronomy. The texts show Vedanga Jyotisha (astronomy), Sulbasutra mathematics and Ayurveda; chemistry is the only discipline absent (NextGen p.25).

21.s: The Samaveda is an important source for

21.x: The Samaveda, a collection of Rig Vedic hymns set to melody, is the source of Indian music.

21.s: The Atharvaveda describes the Sabha and the Samiti as the twin daughters of:
21.x: The Atharvaveda calls the Sabha and Samiti the two daughters of Prajapati.

21.s: Which of the following Vedas is NOT included in the 'Trayi'?
21.x: The Trayi is the first three Vedas; the Atharvaveda, the latest Veda, is left out.

o: Most of its verses are taken from the Yajurveda
It is the shortest of the four Vedas
It is mainly a collection of spells and charms
21.x: The Samaveda is the shortest Veda, drawn almost wholly from the Rigveda; its priest is the Udgatri. Spells and charms belong to the Atharvaveda.

21.x: Satyakama, son of the unmarried Jabala, who took his mother's name, is told of in the Chhandogya Upanishad (Book IV); the Jabala Upanishad is a different, later text.

21.x: The Taittiriya Upanishad belongs to the Krishna (Black) Yajurveda; Ayurveda and Dhanurveda are Upavedas, not Vedas.

21.x: Shankaracharya wrote bhashyas on the Prasthanatrayi: the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras and Bhagavad Gita; he did not comment on the Rigveda Samhita.

21.s: The Words 'Satymeva Jayate' in the State Emblem of India, have been adopted from which one of the following?
21.x: Satyameva Jayate, the motto below the State Emblem, is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

21.x: The national motto Satyameva Jayate comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.

21.x: The Prasthanatrayi of Vedanta = Upanishads, Brahma Sutra and Bhagavad Gita; the Bhagavata Purana is not part of it.

21.s: From which Upanishad, the words “Satyameva Jayate” have been taken?
21.x: Satyameva Jayate is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad and was adopted as the national motto on 26 January 1950.

21.s: From where was word ‘Satyameva Jayate’ taken?

n: The Upanishads present philosophy for all times and for all. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 127-128]

xs: The incorrect statement is that it **rejects every school of thought** — option **(4)**.

xa: **Moksha** (**liberation**) was **first discussed** in the **Upanishads**.

34.s: Famous Greek ambassador Megasthenes came to the court of which emperor?

34.s: In which year did Chandragupta Maurya defeat Seleucus Nicator?
34.x: Chandragupta defeated Seleucus about 305 BC, which led to the treaty.

34.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the seven classes described by Megasthenes?
34.x: Megasthenes listed philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers and councillors. Merchants were not included in this seven-class description.
34.tq: Find the outsider by comparing every option with the complete named list.
xs: **Merchants** are not among Megasthenes' seven classes — option **(1)**.
The seven: **philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers (spies), councillors**.
xa: **Philosophers** = **Brahmanas and Sramanas** (ascetics).
⚠ **Overseers** were in effect **spies**.
He also wrongly claimed there were **no slaves**.

34.s: According to Megasthenes, how was the municipal administration of Palibothra conducted?
o: A 40-member body divided into four boards
A 30-member body divided into six boards
A council of 12 members divided into three boards
A council of 64 members divided into eight boards
34.x: Megasthenes described a 30-member municipal body organised into six boards at Palibothra.
34.tq: Separate the exact institutional composition from nearby city statistics.
xs: Palibothra was run by a **30-member municipal body in six boards** — option **(2)**.
**64** is the number of **gates**, not council members.
xa: Palibothra = **Pataliputra**, at the **Ganga-Son confluence**.
It had a **wooden wall**, **64 gates** and **570 towers**.
Megasthenes was sent by **Seleucus Nicator** to Chandragupta.

34.s: Under the treaty with Seleucus Nicator, Chandragupta Maurya gave Seleucus:
34.x: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia and received 500 elephants.

34.s: Which of the following territories was NOT ceded by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya?
34.x: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia but retained Bactria.

34.s:
Match the provinces ceded by Seleucus to Chandragupta Maurya with their present-day regions:
List-I (Province)
a. Aria
b. Arachosia
c. Paropanisadai
d. Gedrosia
List-II (Present-day region)
i. Kabul
ii. Balochistan
iii. Kandahar
iv. Herat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Aria = Herat; Arachosia = Kandahar; Paropanisadai = Kabul; Gedrosia = Balochistan.

34.s: The Greek envoy Megasthenes, author of 'Indica', came to the court of:
34.x: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya.

34.s: Deimachus came as an envoy of Antiochus I to the court of:
34.x: Deimachus (from Antiochus I) and Dionysius (from Ptolemy II) came to Bindusara's court.

34.s: Who of the following mentions about the meeting of Sandrokottos (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander, the Great
34.x: Justin described the meeting of Sandrokottos (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander. Pliny, Strabo and Megasthenes are not credited with this.

34.s: Who of the following mentions about the meeting of Sandrocottus (Chandragupta Maurya) with Alexander, the Great?
34.x: Justin, the Roman historian, described Sandrocottus (Chandragupta) meeting Alexander; Pliny, Strabo and Megasthenes are not credited with this.

34.s: Which among the following is India’s oldest dynasty?
34.x: The Maurya dynasty (321–185 BCE) is the oldest of the four; the Kushanas, Guptas and Vardhanas came later.

34.s: Who was called as 'Sandrocottos' by Justin, the Greek Writer?
34.x: Justin called Chandragupta Maurya 'Sandrocottus'; Sir William Jones identified the name with him. The Gupta kings are much later.

34.s: To which dynasty did Ashoka belong?
34.x: Ashoka belonged to the Maurya dynasty – grandson of its founder Chandragupta and son of Bindusara.

34.s: First Indian Empire was established by
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya founded the first Indian (pan-Indian) empire, the Maurya empire; Kanishka, Harsha and Samudragupta came later.

34.s: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandra Gupta Maurya?
34.x: Sir William Jones identified the Sandrokottos of the Greek writers with Chandragupta Maurya. This became the sheet-anchor of Indian chronology. Smith, Mookerji and D.R. Bhandarkar came later.

34.s:
Consider the following about the origin of the Mauryas:
1. Brahmanical sources link the name Maurya with the Shudra woman Mura.
2. Buddhist and Jain sources describe Chandragupta as a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
34.x: Both statements are correct: Brahmanical sources link Maurya with the Shudra woman Mura, while Buddhist and Jain sources make Chandragupta a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.

34.s: Which commentator on Mudrarakshasa made Chandragupta a descendant of the Nanda house?
34.x: Dhundiraja's commentary on Mudrarakshasa links Chandragupta with the Nanda house.

34.s: The identification of 'Sandrocottus' of the Greek accounts with Chandragupta Maurya was first made by:
34.x: Sir William Jones made the identification in 1793; James Prinsep later deciphered the Brahmi script (1837).

34.s: Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded on the throne by his son:
34.x: Bindusara (297-273 BCE) succeeded Chandragupta; Ashoka was Chandragupta's grandson.

34.s: Which of the following was NOT a Mauryan ruler?
34.x: Dhana Nanda was the last Nanda king, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE.

34.s:
Who among the following rulers paid attention to the resource management in Girnar region some centuries before the Christian era?
1. Mahapadma Nanda
2. Chandragupta Maurya
3. Ashoka
4. Rudradaman
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
34.x: Before the Christian era Chandragupta Maurya (governor Pushyagupta built the Sudarshana lake) and Ashoka (governor Tushaspha added canals) managed Girnar's water. Rudradaman repaired it in c. 150 CE, after the Christian era, so codes 2, 3.

34.s: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquer the Deccan?
34.x:
Most books and keys: Bindusara conquered the Deccan. Some books credit Chandragupta (Jain tradition of his end at Shravanabelagola), and NextGen says Bindusara made no conquests.
Bindusara is credited with extending Mauryan rule over the Deccan up to Mysore (PMF); Ashoka only added Kalinga and Kunala was a later prince.

34.s: Who was the first king to conquer Malwa, Gujarat and Maharashtra?
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya was the first king to hold Malwa, Gujarat (Saurashtra, under governor Pushyagupta – Junagadh inscription) and Maharashtra; Skandagupta, Vikramaditya and Harsha came much later.

34.s: Realizing the need for water, the first ruler who got a lake constructed in the Girnar area, was
34.x: The first lake at Girnar, the Sudarshana, was built by Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya. Ashoka's governor only added canals; Rudradaman and Skandagupta repaired it later.

34.s: Who constructed the Sudarshana Lake?
34.x: The Sudarshana lake was built in Chandragupta Maurya's reign by his governor Pushyagupta (Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman). Samudragupta, Chandragupta Vikramaditya and Bimbisara are distractors.

34.s: With reference to Chandragupta Maurya's expansion, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Mamulanar – Greek chronicler of the Mauryas
Seleucus – Ceded four provinces up to Afghanistan
Greek satraps – Expelled from the north-west
34.x: Mamulanar was a Tamil poet who referred to the Mauryas' southward expansion, not a Greek chronicler.
xa: **Western India**: Saurashtra under **Pushyagupta**, builder of the **Sudarshana lake**.
Army: **600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry**.
Ceded provinces: **Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai, Gedrosia**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandragupta Maurya is regarded as the Mauryan conqueror of the Deccan.
2. The Tamil poet Tiruvalluvar refers to the southward push of the Mauryas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Bindusara, not Chandragupta Maurya, is regarded as the Mauryan conqueror of the Deccan. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is the Sangam poet Mamulanar, not Tiruvalluvar, who refers to the Mauryan push southward.

34.s:
Match the Mauryan provincial capitals with their provinces:
List-I (Capital)
a. Taxila
b. Ujjain
c. Tosali
d. Suvarnagiri
List-II (Province)
i. East (Kalinga)
ii. West
iii. North
iv. South
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Taxila – north; Ujjain – west; Tosali – Kalinga in the east; Suvarnagiri – south; Pataliputra was the centre.

34.s: Which of the following Ashokan edict sites is located in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh?
34.x: Yerragudi (major and minor edicts) and Rajula Mandagiri (minor edict) are in Kurnool district; Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Maski are in Karnataka.

34.s: Which of the following southern kingdoms was NOT part of the Mauryan Empire?
34.x: The Pandya kingdom is named in the edicts as a neighbour, outside the empire.

34.s:
Assertion (A): The Satavahanas began their political career as feudatories of the Mauryas.
Reason (R): Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples following Dhamma within his domain.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
34.x: Both are true: the notes say the Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories, and RE XIII names the Andhras among peoples within the domain. But R only shows the Andhra country lay within Ashoka's empire; it does not explain how the Satavahana dynasty began, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

34.s: The Sudarshana lake at Girnar was originally built by Pushyagupta, governor of:
34.x: Pushyagupta, Chandragupta Maurya's governor, built it; Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka; Rudradaman I and Skandagupta repaired it.

34.s: Which of the following rulers is NOT associated with building or repairing the Sudarshana lake at Girnar?
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya's governor built it, Ashoka's governor added canals, and Rudradaman I and Skandagupta repaired it; Samudragupta has no link with it.

34.s: Kautilya was prime minister of –
34.x: Kautilya (Chanakya, Vishnugupta) was the prime minister and guide of Chandragupta Maurya, not of Chandragupta Vikramaditya, Ashoka or Janaka.

34.s: By which name was Chanakya known in his childhood?
34.x: Chanakya's childhood name was Vishnugupta; one Arthashastra verse names its author Vishnugupta, while Chanakya and Kautilya are his other names.

34.s: The another name of Chanakya was
34.x: Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known as Vishnugupta. Bhattaswami was a commentator, Rajasekhara a later poet and Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa.

34.s: Another name of Chanakya was :
34.x: Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known as Vishnugupta; Bhattaswami, Rajasekhara and Vishakhadatta are other authors.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Chanakya:
1. One verse of the Arthashastra names its author Bhadrabahu.
2. According to Taranath and Jain tradition, he stayed on as Ashoka's minister.
3. In the Mudrarakshasa his rival Rakshasa was the minister of the Nandas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Only statement 3 is correct: in the Mudrarakshasa, Rakshasa is the Nanda minister. Statement 1 is incorrect: the verse names the author Vishnugupta, not Bhadrabahu. Statement 2 is incorrect: Taranath and Jain tradition keep him on as Bindusara's minister, not Ashoka's.

34.s: The first Indian King who abdicated his throne, was:
34.x: Chandragupta Maurya is regarded as the first Indian king to abdicate – in favour of Bindusara – before becoming a Jain ascetic and dying by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.

34.s: Who came south with Chandragupta Maurya during the great famine in North India?
34.x: By Jain tradition the monk Bhadrabahu led the migration south in the 12-year famine, with Chandragupta Maurya, to Shravanabelagola. Sthulabhadra stayed in the north; Merutunga and Lakulisha are later figures.

34.s: The Barabar caves, the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, are located in the state of:
34.x: The granite Barabar caves are in the Barabar hills near Gaya, Bihar.

34.s: The Mauryan rock-cut caves of the Barabar hills were dedicated by Ashoka to the:
34.x: Ashoka's inscriptions record the gift of the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas.

34.s: To whom did Ashoka and Dasharatha dedicate the Barabar caves in Bihar?
34.x: Ashoka and Dasharatha dedicated the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas, the sect also patronised by Bindusara. Jainism is linked with Chandragupta and Samprati, and Buddhism with Ashoka's Lanka mission, but the Barabar dedications were to the Ajivikas; Vedic Brahmanas were not the recipients.
34.tq: Barabar and Nagarjuni caves = Ajivikas (Ashoka, Dasharatha).
xs: **Ashoka and Dasharatha** dedicated the **Barabar caves** to the **Ajivikas** — option **(1)**.
Barabar (**Bihar**) has the **oldest surviving rock-cut caves**, in **granite**.
**Jainism** is linked with Chandragupta and Samprati; the Barabar gifts were to the Ajivikas.
xa: **Dasharatha** was an Ajivika patron at **Nagarjuni**; personally counted a Buddhist (**CGPSC 2013** key).
**Bindusara** is the standard Ajivika patron.
**Ashoka** turned to **Buddhism** after Kalinga.

34.s: In which hills of Bihar is the Lomas Rishi cave, a Mauryan cave linked to the Ajivikas?
34.x: Lomas Rishi is one of the Barabar Hill caves in Bihar, famous for its carved facade.
n: Lomas Rishi Cave is located in the Barabar Hills of Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Lomas Rishi Cave is associated with the Ajivika religion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Lomas Rishi Cave belongs to the Mauryan period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: Lomas Rishi is famous for its **rock-cut façade**.
**Barabar Caves** contain **Ashokan inscriptions**; dedicated to Ajivikas by **Ashoka and Dasharatha**.
They are the **oldest surviving rock-cut caves**, carved in **granite**.

34.s: Which religion did Dasharatha, who gave the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas, follow?
34.x: Dasharatha is taken as a Buddhist, though he patronised the Ajivikas with the Nagarjuni caves.

34.s: According to Jain tradition, Chandragupta Maurya died by Sallekhana at which of the following places?
34.x: Jain tradition says Chandragupta went south with Bhadrabahu and died by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.

34.s: Which of the following statements about the Jain tradition of Chandragupta Maurya is correct?
o: The followers of Sthulabhadra came to be called Digambaras.
He was a disciple of Mahavira himself.
Bhadrabahu went south with him during a great famine.
He died by Sallekhana at Pavapuri.
34.x: Bhadrabahu led the migration south; those who stayed north with Sthulabhadra became the Svetambaras.

34.s:
Match the Mauryan rulers with their religious leanings:
List-I (Ruler)
a. Chandragupta
b. Bindusara
c. Ashoka
d. Samprati
List-II (Religion)
i. Ajivika
ii. Buddhism
iii. 'Ashoka of Jainism'; spread Jainism in Andhra
iv. Jainism, under Bhadrabahu
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
34.x: Chandragupta – Jainism (Bhadrabahu); Bindusara – Ajivika; Ashoka – Buddhism (though he gave the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas); Samprati – the 'Ashoka of Jainism', who spread Jainism in Andhra.

34.s: Which of the following Mauryan ruler is known as ‘Amitraghat’?
34.x: Amitraghata ('slayer of foes', Greek Amitrochates) was the title of Bindusara, not of Chandragupta, Samudragupta or Ashoka.

34.s: The Mauryan emperor Bindusara ruled during the period:
34.x: Bindusara (birth name Simhasena, mother Durdhara) ruled c. 297-273 BCE between Chandragupta and Ashoka.

34.s: Which Seleucid ruler sent sweet wine and dried figs to Bindusara but refused to send a philosopher?
34.x: Antiochus I Soter sent the wine and figs but replied that Greeks did not sell philosophers.

34.s: According to the Divyavadana, whom did Bindusara send to suppress the revolt at Taxila after Susima failed?
34.x: Ashoka was sent to Taxila after Susima failed; the later revolt in Ashoka's reign was handled by Kunala.

34.s: Which of the following statements about the Taxila revolts is correct?
o: The revolt Susima failed to quell occurred under Chandragupta Maurya.
Susima suppressed the Taxila revolt under Bindusara.
Ashoka was viceroy at Tosali before his accession.
Kunala handled the later Taxila revolt in Ashoka's reign.
34.x: Susima failed under Bindusara, Ashoka was then sent, and the later revolt was handled by Kunala; Ashoka was viceroy at Taxila and Ujjain.

34.s:
Assertion (A): Bindusara is identified with the 'Amitrochates' of the Greek writers.
Reason (R): Bindusara's title Amitraghata means 'slayer of foes'.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
34.x: Both are true: Amitrochates is the Greek form of Bindusara's title Amitraghata, which means 'slayer of foes' (Mahabhashya). But the meaning of the title does not explain the identification – it rests on the Greek form of the title – so R is not the correct explanation of A.

34.s: The first Indian King who abdicated his throne, was:
34.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, held 05-09-2010 · Q7
34.x: By Jain tradition Chandragupta Maurya gave up his throne, became a Jain monk and died at Shravanabelagola.

35.s: “In spite of being Buddhist, Ashoka did not leave belief in Hinduism” validation of this fact is:–
35.x: The epithet Devanampriya ('beloved of the gods') is read as proof that Ashoka, though a Buddhist, kept his regard for the gods; pilgrimages and veterinary hospitals show Buddhist piety and welfare.

35.s: Who established ‘Rajdharma’ on triplex bases of longanimity, liberty and compassion ?
35.x: Ashoka's Dhamma was a rajdharma based on longanimity (tolerance), liberty and compassion; Akbar, Ranjit Singh and Shivaji are distractors.

35.s: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is -:
35.x: The core of Ashoka's Dhamma is peace and non-violence – RE I bans slaughter and sacrifice; respect to elders and toleration are parts of it, not its centre.

35.s: India’s first hospital and herbal gardens were built by?
35.x: Ashoka's RE II records hospitals and medicinal herb gardens for men and animals – the first in India; Chandragupta, Mahavira and Dhanvantari are distractors.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka:
1. The definition of Dhamma given by Ashoka has been taken from the "Rahulovada-Sutta".
2. In the 14th year of his reign, Ashoka appointed a new type of staffcalled Dhamma-Mahamatras.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
35.x: Both are correct: the spirit of Ashoka's Dhamma is drawn from the Rahulovada Sutta (with the Lakkhana Sutta and Dhammapada), and RE V appointed Dhamma Mahamatras 13 years after consecration, i.e. in his 14th regnal year.

35.s: Which of the following statements about Ashoka's regnal years is correct?
o: The Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed in his 12th regnal year.
The Rajukas received independent judicial authority in his 26th regnal year.
The Kalinga War was fought in his 14th regnal year.
His Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya was made in his 21st regnal year.
35.x: Pillar Edict IV records the Rajukas' powers in year 26; Bodh Gaya was year 11, Dhamma Mahamatras year 14 (RE V) and Kalinga year 8.

35.s: Which officials did Ashoka appoint to look after all sects, women and prisoners?
35.x: RE V's Dhamma Mahamatras worked among all sects, women and prisoners; Pativedakas were reporters.

35.s: Which edict of Ashoka defines Dhamma as 'few faults, many good deeds'?
35.x: Pillar Edict II gives this definition of Dhamma.

35.s: Which Rock Edict of Ashoka records the Kalinga war?
35.x: Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga war; Rock Edict I bans animal slaughter.

35.s: Ashoka's Dhamma asked his subjects to show respect towards:
35.x: The edicts repeatedly ask for regard for both Brahmanas and Shramanas.

35.s: Ashoka's first Major Rock Edict prohibited:
35.x: Major Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and samajas (festive gatherings).

35.s:
Match Ashoka's measures with the edicts that record them:
List-I (Measure)
a. Appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras
b. Quinquennial tours of rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas
c. Pativedakas may report at any time
d. Hospitals for men and animals
List-II (Edict)
i. Rock Edict VI
ii. Rock Edict V
iii. Rock Edict III
iv. Rock Edict II
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
35.x: Dhamma Mahamatras – RE V (14th regnal year); quinquennial tours – RE III (12th year); pativedakas reporting at any time – RE VI; hospitals, medicinal herbs, wells and trees – RE II.

35.s: Under Ashoka's Pillar Edict IV, independent judicial powers were given to the:
35.x: Pillar Edict IV gave the rajukas independent judicial power and gave condemned prisoners three days' respite.

35.s: Which of Ashoka's edicts forbade the branding of cattle?
35.x: Pillar Edict V lists animal-protection rules, including the ban on branding cattle on certain days.

35.s: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka’s administrative policy?
o: His sending of missionary to Ceylon
35.x: The Kalinga War's carnage (RE XIII) made Ashoka give up conquest by war (Bherighosha) for conquest by Dhamma (Dhammaghosha). The Third Council and the Ceylon mission came later.

35.s:
Consider the following statements.
Assertion (A) Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire.
Reason (R) Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes to South India.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
35.x: Ashoka conquered Kalinga c. 261 BCE; Kalinga's control of the land and sea routes to the south explains why he wanted it, so R explains A.

35.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kalinga War?
o: Rock Edict XIII is found at Dhauli and Jaugada
Bherighosha gave way to Dhammaghosha after it
Separate Edicts address officials at Tosali and Samapa
35.x: Dhauli and Jaugada have no RE XIII; they carry the Separate Edicts instead.

35.s: Ashoka's account of the Kalinga War and his remorse is found in:
35.x: Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war, about 1,50,000 deported and 1,00,000 killed.

35.s: The Kalinga War was fought in which regnal year of Ashoka?
35.x: The war came in Ashoka's 8th regnal year (c. 261 BCE), not the year of his coronation.

35.s: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka replaced Bherighosha (the sound of the war drum) with:
35.x: Ashoka gave up conquest by arms; Bherighosha gave way to Dhammaghosha and Dhammavijaya replaced military conquest.

35.s:
Assertion (A): After the Kalinga War, Ashoka gave up wars of conquest.
Reason (R): The killing and deportation of lakhs of people in the war filled him with remorse.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
35.x: Both are true and R explains A: the toll recorded in RE XIII (about 1 lakh killed, 1.5 lakh deported) led to remorse, and remorse led to Dhammavijaya in place of conquest.

35.s: Turamaya, a contemporary of Ashoka was the ruler of –
35.x: Turamaya in RE XIII is Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt; Syria is Antiyoka, Macedonia Antikini, and Corinth/Epirus Alikasudara.

35.s: Ptolemy Philadelphus who had diplomatic relation with Ashoka, was king of:
35.x: Ptolemy II Philadelphus (Turamaya of RE XIII) was king of Egypt; Antiochus II ruled Syria and Antigonus Macedonia.

35.s:
Match the names in Rock Edict XIII with the Yavana kings they stand for:
List-I (RE XIII name)
a. Antiyoka
b. Antikini
c. Maka
d. Alikasudara
List-II (King)
i. Magas of Cyrene
ii. Antiochus II Theos of Syria
iii. Alexander of Epirus
iv. Antigonus Gonatas of Macedonia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
35.x: Antiyoka = Antiochus II Theos (Syria); Antikini = Antigonus Gonatas (Macedonia); Maka = Magas (Cyrene); Alikasudara = Alexander (Epirus or Corinth). Turamaya = Ptolemy II Philadelphus (Egypt).

35.s:
In the course of pilgrimage, Emperor Ashoka visited the following places. Which route did he follow ?
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
1. Gaya
2. Kapilavastu
3. Kushinagar
4. Lumbini
5. Sarnath
6. Shravasti
35.x: The Divyavadana gives Ashoka's pilgrimage as Lumbini, Kapilavastu, Gaya (Bodh Gaya), Sarnath, Kushinagar and Shravasti – codes 4, 2, 1, 5, 3, 6.

35.s: Which religion did Dasaratha, the grandson of Ashoka, follow?
35.x: Like Ashoka, Dasaratha was a Buddhist, though he also gave caves to the Ajivikas.

35.s: With which Buddhist stupa does Andhra tradition link the missionary Mahadeva?
35.x: Andhra tradition links Mahadeva with the Amaravati stupa, said to have been enlarged by Ashoka.

35.s: The Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra under Ashoka was presided over by:
35.x: Moggaliputta Tissa presided over the Third Council; Vasumitra presided over the Fourth.

35.s: Which Ashokan edict expresses his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha?

35.s: Ashoka's coronation took place in about:

o: The Samantapasadika says he won Kalinga in Bindusara's time.

36.s: The first scholar who read Ashokan edicts was –

36.s: Who was the First Britisher to study Ashoka’s edicts?
36.x: James Prinsep, the British scholar of the Asiatic Society, first deciphered and studied the Ashokan edicts in 1837.

36.s: Who of the following had first deciphered the edicts of Emperor Ashoka?
36.x: James Prinsep first deciphered Ashoka's edicts (Brahmi) in 1837. Buhler, Max Muller and William Jones are not credited with the first decipherment.

36.s: Who was the first Indian Emperor to directly communicate with people through his inscriptions?
36.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in A.P BC We
36.x: Ashoka was the first Indian king to communicate directly with his people through inscriptions, written in Prakrit on rocks and pillars. Kharavela and Gautamiputra Satakarni came later; Chandragupta left no edicts.

36.s: Which of the king has been mentioned as ‘Piyadassi’ and Devanampiya’ in inscriptions?
36.x: Ashoka is called Devanampiya ('beloved of the gods') and Piyadassi in his inscriptions; the other kings did not use these titles.

36.s: The title ' Devanam Priya ' was given to:
36.x: Devanampriya ('beloved of the gods') was Ashoka's title in his edicts; Samudragupta, Kanishka and Harsha did not use it.

36.s: Who was the first ruler who inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces – natural rocks as well as polished pillars?
36.x: Ashoka was the first ruler to inscribe messages to subjects and officials on natural rocks and polished pillars; Chandragupta Maurya left no edicts and the Guptas came later.

36.s: Which one of the following edicts mentions the personal name of Asoka?
36.x: The Maski Minor Rock Edict names him 'Devanampiya Asoka'; Kalsi, Rummindei and the Special Kalinga Edict use only Devanampiya Piyadasi.

36.s: In which of the following relief sculpture inscriptions is 'Ranyo Ashoka' (King Ashoka) mentioned along with the stone portrait of Ashoka?
36.x: Kanaganahalli (on the Bhima, Kalaburagi, Karnataka) has the only inscribed stone portrait of Ashoka with the label 'Ranyo Asoko'. Ashoka is shown at Sanchi but not named; Shahbazgarhi is a Kharosthi edict and Sohgaura a copper plate.

36.s: The Gujarra minor rock edict, in which the name of Ashoka is mentioned, is located in
36.x: The Gujarra minor rock edict, naming 'Devanampiya Piyadasi Asoka', is in Datia district, Madhya Pradesh, on the old Ujjain–Bharuch road.

36.s: Which one of the following edicts mentions the personal name of Ashoka ?
36.x: The personal name Ashoka occurs in the Maski edict (also Gujarra, Nittur, Udegolam); Kalsi, Rummindei and the Special Kalinga Edict do not name him.

36.s: In which of the following inscriptions the name of ‘Ashoka’ has been mentioned?
36.x: The Maski Minor Rock Edict names Ashoka; Bhabru, RE XIII and the Rummindei pillar use only Devanampiya Piyadasi.

36.s: The name by which Ashoka is referred to in his inscriptions is :
36.x: Ashoka calls himself Priyadarshi (Piyadasi), with Devanampiya, in his inscriptions; Chakravarti, Dharmadeva and Dharmakirti are not his epithets.

36.s: The only pillar on which Ashoka declares himself as the emperor of Magadha –
36.x: In the Bhabru (Bairat) edict Ashoka calls himself 'Piyadasi Raja' of Magadha – the only edict where he says he is king of Magadha (it is a minor rock edict, though the question says pillar).

36.s: The title 'Devanampiya' used by Ashoka in his edicts means:
36.x: Devanampiya = Beloved of the Gods; Piyadasi = of pleasing appearance.

36.x: In the Bhabru (Bairat) edict he calls himself Piyadasi Raja of Magadha.

36.x: The Maski minor rock edict in Raichur district names 'Ashoka', confirming the identity.

36.x: Kanaganahalli near Sannati (Karnataka) is on the Bhima.

36.s: The Brahmi script of the Ashokan edicts was first deciphered in 1837 by:
36.x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837, starting with the Delhi-Topra pillar edicts.

36.s: In which rock edict of Asoka, definite mention of the Andhras occur?

36.x: Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras (with the Palidas) among peoples in Ashoka's domain who follow his Dhamma. Ashoka issued only 14 Major Rock Edicts, so a '15th' does not exist.

36.s: Ashoka used to release certain number of prisoners on humanitarian grounds on every anniversary of his:
36.x: Ashoka released prisoners on every anniversary of his coronation (abhisheka) – 25 releases in 26 years (PE V); not on his birthday, Kalinga or conversion.

36.x: The quotation is from Ashoka's Rock Edict XII on respect for all sects; Samudragupta, Harsha and Krishnadevaraya are distractors.

36.s: Which of the following Rock Edict of Ashoka speaks of religious synthesis ?
36.x: Rock Edict XII asks for respect for all sects and growth of the essence of all religions – religious synthesis. RE II is about medical care, RE XI the gift of Dhamma, RE XIII Kalinga.

36.x: This is Ashoka's Rock Edict XII on religious harmony; the other rulers did not issue it.

36.s: Which of the following Ashokan inscriptions is devoted to the principle of religious tolerance completely?
36.x: Rock Edict XII is wholly devoted to religious tolerance; RE XIII is on Kalinga, PE VII on spreading Dhamma, and Bhabru on his faith in Buddhism.

36.s: In which of the following inscriptions of Ashoka, mention has been made of South Indian kingdoms?
36.x: The Second Major Rock Edict names the South Indian kingdoms – Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputtas, Keralaputtas.

36.x: Rock Edict XIII gives the account of the Kalinga War, its casualties and Ashoka's remorse; Rummindei, Minor RE I and Hiuen Tsang do not.

36.s: Which of the following inscriptions of Ashoka bans animal sacrifice on certain festive gathering, that probably included a ban on animal killing as well?
36.x: Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and festive gatherings (samaja) and cuts down killing in the royal kitchen.

36.s: Which of the following information is found in Ashoka’s inscriptions?
36.x: Ashoka's inscriptions record his life (Kalinga War), internal policy (Mahamattas, rajukas, Dhamma) and foreign policy (Greek kings, southern kingdoms), so all the options are correct.

36.s: Which Ashokan Rock Edict describes the victory and injuries of Kalinga war?
36.x: Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga War – its victory, casualties and Ashoka's remorse; RE I, II and XII deal with other subjects.

36.s: Which one territory of the following was not a part of Ashoka’s empire?
36.x: Sri Lanka (Tamraparni) was a neighbour named in RE II, not part of Ashoka's empire; Afghanistan, Bihar and Kalinga were inside it.

36.s: Which one of the following scripts of ancient India was written from right to left?
36.x: Kharosthi, derived from Aramaic, was written from right to left; Brahmi, Nandinagari and Sharada run left to right.

36.s: Language used in the inscriptions of Ashoka is ?
36.x: The language of most Ashokan inscriptions is Prakrit; Sanskrit inscriptions begin later (Rudradaman), and Pali is the Buddhist canonical language.

36.s: Which one of the following Ashokan inscription is in “Kharosthi” script?
36.x: Shahbazgarhi (with Mansehra) is one of the only two Ashokan sites in Kharosthi; Kalsi, Girnar and Meerut are in Brahmi.

36.s: The bilingual Greek-Aramaic edict of Ashoka was found at:
36.x: The bilingual edict is from Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna); Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts are in Kharosthi.

36.s: The Kharosthi script, used in some Ashokan edicts, was written:
36.x: Kharosthi, derived from Aramaic, was written from right to left; Brahmi was written left to right.

36.s: The Telugu script has evolved from the ancient script known as:
36.x: Telugu, like most Indian scripts, descends from Brahmi. Kharosthi was used in the north-west.

36.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classes of Ashokan inscriptions?
36.x: Ashoka's inscriptions are on rocks, pillars and caves (Barabar); he left no copper-plate inscriptions.

36.s: Sarnath Pillar was built by –
36.x: The Sarnath pillar with the lion capital, now the national emblem, was erected by Ashoka – not by Harsha, the Buddha or Kanishka.

36.s: Which among the following pillar inscriptions of Ashoka states that the land revenue rate of Lumbini was reduced to one-eighth?
36.x: The Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar records Ashoka's visit 20 years after consecration, exempting Lumbini from bali and cutting the bhaga to one-eighth. Maski is a rock edict; Kalsi and Vaishali are distractors.

36.x: The Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar inscription records Ashoka's visit and that 'here the Buddha was born'. Nigali Sagar records the Kanakamuni stupa; Basarh and Rampurwa do not confirm Lumbini.

36.s: From which inscriptions of the following dynasty Lumbini was known as Buddha’s birthplace?
36.x: Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription marks Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace, so the dynasty is the Mauryan.

36.s: Who brought two Ashoka Pillars to Delhi from Topra and Meerut?
36.x: Firuz Shah Tughluq brought the Ashokan pillars from Topra and Meerut to Delhi; Alauddin Khalji, Muhammad Ghori and Sikandar Lodi did not.

36.s: In which district of Bihar is the Lauriya Nandangarh pillar of Ashoka?
36.x: The Lauriya Nandangarh pillar, with a single lion capital and Pillar Edicts I-VI, is in West Champaran district of Bihar.

42.x: Agathocles' coins from Ai-Khanoum show Balarama (Sankarshana) and Vasudeva-Krishna. Kanishka and Huvishka were Kushanas and Samudragupta a Gupta, so they are distractors.

42.x: All three are correct. Indo-Greek coins were mostly silver and copper and reveal 30+ kings; the Indo-Greeks issued the first gold coins, and the Kushanas later issued gold on a large scale.

42.x: All three are correct. The Indo-Greeks first issued coins attributable to kings and the first (rare) gold coins, which the Kushanas later issued on a large scale; their bilingual coins carry Greek and Kharoshthi Prakrit.

44.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Kushanas were Silk Road middlemen between Han China, Rome and India, not a barrier to that trade; their empire extended well beyond the Indus into the Gangetic plain.

44.s:

44.x: Kujula Kadphises was the founder who united the Yuezhi clans; Vima Kadphises extended rule to Mathura and Varanasi; Huvishka succeeded Kanishka; Vasudeva I was the last great Kushana and the first with an Indian name.

44.s:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
44.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vima Kadphises was the father of Kanishka, not his son.

44.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Saka era began 135 years after the Vikrama era (57 BCE).

44.s: Who among the following first issued gold coins on a large scale?
44.x: Vima Kadphises was the first to issue gold coins on a large scale, for regular use. Menander's Indo-Greeks issued the first gold coins but only rarely, so he is the tempting wrong option.

44.s: Which of the following Kings is credited to have issued gold coins for the first time?
44.x: Vima Kadphises introduced Kushana gold coins; Kujula Kadphises issued copper. Kanishka and Huvishka came later.

44.s: Which God is found depicted on Yaudheya coins ?
44.x: Yaudheya copper coins show the six-headed Kartikeya with a peacock. Vasudeva, Mitra and Indra are not their coin deity.

44.s: Who among the following introduced gold coins for regular use in India?
44.x: Vima Kadphises introduced gold coins for regular use; Kujula Kadphises issued copper, and Kanishka continued gold. Hermaeus was the last Indo-Greek.

44.s: The largest number of copper coins in northern and northwestern India were issued by?
44.x: The Kushanas issued the largest number of copper coins in north and north-west India, besides plentiful gold. The Indo-Greeks issued mainly silver.

44.s: Buddha is depicted on the coins of :
44.x: Kanishka put the Buddha (BOΔΔO) on his coins. Vima Kadphises shows Shiva, and Nahapana and Budhagupta did not show the Buddha.

44.s:

4. Kanishka's coin legends are in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
44.x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kujula Kadphises issued copper coins; Vima Kadphises first issued gold. Statement 2 is wrong: the figure with the trident and bull is Shiva. Statement 3 is wrong: the dinara weighed about 8 g (120 grains). Statement 4 is wrong: Kanishka's legends are in the Greek script (Bactrian language), not Brahmi.

44.s:

44.x: All three statements are correct: Kanishka is shown in peaked helmet, coat and boots at an altar, over 30 Greek, Iranian and Indian deities appear on Kushana coins, and BOΔΔO and Oesho appear on his coins.

44.s: The greatest development in the Kushan period was in the field of
44.x: The Kushana period is best known for art – the Gandhara and Mathura schools and the first Buddha images. Religion (Mahayana) and literature grew too, but art is the standard answer.

44.s: The first human statues worshipped in India were those of–
44.x: The first human statues worshipped in India were those of the Buddha, made by Mahayana followers in the Kushana age. Images of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva came later.

b. Manimekalai

58.x: Silappadikaram - Ilango Adigal (Jain); Manimekalai - Sittalai Sattanar (Buddhist); Jivaka Chintamani - Tiruttakkadevar (Jain ascetic; called Mana Nool); Tolkappiyam - Tolkappiyar.

58.s: In Sangam Literature ‘Tolkappiyam’ is a text of –
58.x: Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar is the earliest Tamil grammar (with poetics); it is not a work on architecture or polity.

58.s: Which one of the following Tamil Texts has been called Laghuveda?
58.x: Tiruvalluvar's Kural is honoured as the Tamil Veda and Laghuveda; Kalingattuparani (Jayangondar) and Periyapuranam (Sekkilar) are later Chola works and Nandikkalambakam is Pallava.

58.s: The Sangam text Tolkappiyam is a work on
58.x: Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar; it is not on astronomy, music or medicine.

58.s: Tolkappiyam text deals with :
58.x: Tolkappiyam deals with grammar and poetics (and incidentally with society, e.g. the tinai and four castes); it is not a work on administration or law, so 'all the above' is wrong.

58.s: Which of the following Tamil text has been called ‘Laghuveda’?
58.x: The Kural of Tiruvalluvar is called Laghuveda and Tamil Veda; Kalingattuparani, Periyapuranam and Nandikkalambakam are later works.

58.s:
Match item of list I with those of list II and select your correct answer from the code given below in the lists.
List I
A. Thirukural
B. Tolkappiyam
C. Silappadikaram
D. Manimekalai
List II
1. Love Story
2. Philosophy
3. Merchant Story
4. Grammar
Codes A B C D A B C D
58.x: Kural = philosophy and Tolkappiyam = grammar are certain, and only code 2-4-1-3 has both; it pairs Silappadikaram with the love story (Kovalan, Kannagi, Madhavi) and Manimekalai with the merchant story.

58.s: Religious anthology ‘Kural’ composed in which language?
58.x: The Kural of Tiruvalluvar, 1,330 couplets on ethics, is in Tamil, not Pali or Telugu.

58.s: Which of the following work–author pairs is correctly matched?
58.x: Tirukkural was written by Tiruvalluvar. Tolkappiyam is by Tolkappiyar, Silappadikaram by Ilango Adigal and Manimekalai by Sittalai Sattanar.
xa: **Sivaga Sindamani (Jivaka Chintamani)**, a Jain epic, is by **Tiruttakkadevar**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Tirukkural = **philosophy**, Tolkappiyam = **grammar**, Silappadikaram = **love story**, Manimekalai = **merchant story**.
Ilango Adigal was the younger brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**.

58.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tolkappiyam has three parts - Aram, Porul and Inbam.
2. The Tirukkural contains 1,330 couplets.
3. The Porul book of the Tirukkural deals with love.
4. The Tirukkural is also called Ulaga Podhumarai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: the Kural has 1,330 couplets and is called Ulaga Podhumarai. Tolkappiyam's parts are Ezhuttu, Col and Porul, while Aram, Porul and Inbam are the Kural's books; the Porul book deals with wealth and polity, love being Inbam.

58.s: Which one of the following statements about Sangam literature in ancient South India is correct?
o: Sangam poems are devoid of any reference to material culture.
The social classification of Varna was known to Sangam poets.
Sangam poems have no reference to warrior ethics.
Sangam literature refers to magical forces as irrational.
58.x: Sangam poets knew the varna classification, although society was not rigidly divided; the poems are rich in material culture and warrior ethic, so the other options are false.

58.s: Name the source that is silent about the trade routes of ancient India
58.x: Sangam poetry describes ports and goods but not the overland trade routes; the Milindapanha and the Jatakas describe routes and caravan travel.

58.s: Which one of the following statements about Sangam literature in ancient South India is correct?
o: Sangam poems are devoid of any reference to material
The social classification of Varna was known to
Sangam poems have no reference to warrior ethic
Sangam literature refers to magical forces as irrational
58.x: The varna classification was known to Sangam poets (UPSC 2022), though Tamil society was not rigidly stratified; Sangam poems are full of material culture and warrior ethic.

58.s: What is the language of the Sangam literature?
58.x: Sangam literature is in old Tamil; the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit, and Pali is the language of the Buddhist canon.

58.s:
Consider the following:
1.
Assertion (A): The Aham and Puram poems of the Padinen Kilukanakku group formed a continuation of the Sangam composition.
2.
Reason (R): They were included under the Post-Sangam works as against the Sangam works proper.
Select the correct answer using the code given below
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
58.x: The Padinenkilkanakku poems keep the aham-puram themes, continuing Sangam composition, and they are classed as post-Sangam works (4th-6th c.) as against the Sangam works proper; PMF and most keys read the classification as explaining the continuation. Some keys give (b), treating the Reason as mere chronology.

58.s: Which of the following poets of the Sangam age has referred to a Mauryan expedition against a Tamil chieftain?
58.x: The Sangam poet Mamulanar refers to the Mauryas (Vamba Moriyar) advancing into the south against a Tamil chieftain; Avvaiyar and Paranar wrote other poems and Ilango Adigal is post-Sangam.

58.s: About how many poems does the Sangam corpus contain?
58.x: The Sangam corpus has about 2,400 poems by several hundred poets, including women.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about Sangam literature:
1. It was composed in old Tamil.
2. It has about 2,400 poems, including some by women poets.
3. It is rich in references to material culture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: All three statements are correct: Sangam literature is in old Tamil, has about 2,400 poems including some by women, and is rich in material culture.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II (Sangam corpus):
List-I
a. Padirruppattu
b. Pattinappalai
c. Pathinenkilkanakku
d. Puram poems
List-II
1. War, valour and royal deeds
2. Eighteen minor didactic works, post-Sangam
3. Ettuthogai anthology on the Chera kings
4. Pattupattu idyll on Puhar and Karikala
Select the correct answer:
58.x: Padirruppattu (Ettuthogai) is on the Chera kings; Pattinappalai (Pattupattu) describes Puhar and Karikala; Pathinenkilkanakku = 18 minor didactic works (post-Sangam); Puram = war, valour, royal deeds.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about Sangam poetry:
1. The Melkanakku (18 major works) consists of the Ettuthogai and the Pattupattu.
2. Only the Ettuthogai, not the Pattupattu, is divided into aham and puram poems.
3. Puram poems mainly deal with war, valour and royal deeds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Melkanakku is the Ettuthogai and Pattupattu, and puram poems deal with war and valour. Statement 2 is wrong: both the Ettuthogai and the Pattupattu have aham and puram poems.

58.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Pathinenkilkanakku is a collection of eighteen minor works, mostly didactic.
Reason (R): The Tirukkural is one of the works of the Pathinenkilkanakku.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
58.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the Pathinenkilkanakku is the post-Sangam set of eighteen minor, mostly didactic works, and the Tirukkural being one of them is not why the collection is so described.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sangam age:
1. Sangam literature was in old Tamil, while the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit.
2. Its accepted span is c. 300 BCE - 300 CE.
3. Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions of the 3rd century BCE mark its later limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 3rd-century BCE Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions support the early limit of the Sangam age, not the later one.

58.s: Third Sangam was held at :
58.x: The third Sangam was held at Madurai under the Pandyas; the first was at Then Madurai and the second at Kapatapuram. Arikamedu and Tuticorin were ports.

58.s: From where did Sangam literature get that name?
58.x: Sangam means an assembly (academy) of Tamil poets held under Pandya patronage; it has nothing to do with the Buddhist Sangha or the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara.

58.s: Under the patronage of which dynasty were the Sangams held?
58.x: The Sangams were held under Pandya patronage, not Chola; the corpus has about 2,400 poems.
xa: Language: **old Tamil**.
Themes divide into **aham** (interior) and **puram** (exterior).
Sangam poets **knew the varna classification** (**UPSC 2022** key).

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II (the Sangam tradition):
List-I
a. First Sangam
b. Second Sangam
c. Third Sangam
d. Iraiyanar Agapporul
List-II
1. Its preface preserves the tradition of the three Sangams
2. Madurai, presided over by Nakkirar
3. Then Madurai, presided over by Agastya
4. Kapatapuram; only the Tolkappiyam survives
Select the correct answer:
58.x: By tradition (preface of Iraiyanar Agapporul): First Sangam - Then Madurai, Agastya, nothing survives; Second - Kapatapuram, Tolkappiyar, only Tolkappiyam survives; Third - Madurai, Nakkirar (Ettuthogai, Pattupattu).

58.s: The Ashokan inscriptions mention which southern polities as neighbours south of the Mauryan Empire?
58.x: Ashokan inscriptions identify the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas as southern neighbours of the Mauryan Empire; Satiyaputras and Keralaputras are also mentioned in Rock Edict II.
58.tq: Recall the political geography recorded in the imperial inscriptions.
xs: Ashokan inscriptions name the **Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas** as southern neighbours — option **(3)**.
**Rock Edict II** also names the **Satiyaputras** and **Keralaputras**.
xa: The **Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**) records three generations of **Chera** rulers.
**Tamil-Brahmi** of the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early Sangam limit.
Indirect sources: **Buddhist-Jain texts** and later travellers.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kaveripattinam — Chola port with Yavana settlements
Keezhadi — Chera capital described by Pliny
Mangulam — Roman market street near Puducherry
58.x: Kaveripattinam or Puhar was a Chola port described in Pattinappalai as cosmopolitan and containing Yavana settlements.
58.tq: Match each archaeological site with its political and commercial setting.
xs: **Kaveripattinam — Chola port with Yavana settlements** — option **(1)**.
**Pattinappalai** describes Puhar as **cosmopolitan**.
**Keezhadi** is an urban excavation; **Arikamedu** is the Roman "market street" near Puducherry.
xa: Pattinappalai is linked with **Karikala**.
**Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**): three generations of Chera rulers.
Pliny: **muslin from Chola**.

58.s: In February 2026, about 30 Indian, mostly Tamil-Brahmi, inscriptions were found in the Theban tombs of which country?
58.x: About 30 Indian, mostly Tamil-Brahmi, inscriptions of the 1st–3rd century CE were found in the Theban tombs of Egypt.

58.s:
Match List-I (Source) with List-II (What it records):
List-I
a. Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
b. Pliny's Natural History
c. Ashokan Rock Edict II
d. Hathigumpha inscription
List-II
