xa: The Dnyaneshwari was written in **1290** at Nevasa.
Other Bhakti saints: **Namdev**, later **Tukaram** and **Ramdas**.
The Yadavas' mother tongue was **Marathi**.

xa: Nayakas received villages called **Nayakasthalam** in place of salary.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet who translated the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Telugu as ' Andhra Mahabharatam '.
II. He is also credited with writing ' Andhra Shabda Chintamani ', a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.
III. Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya.
101.x:
Official key: I and III (Nandampudi to Nannaya). Strictly: the Nandampudi grant names Narayana Bhattu as donee and Nannaya as its composer, so I and II (NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.20, p.33).
Statements I and II are right: Nannaya translated the Mahabharata (Andhra Mahabharatam) and is credited with Andhra Shabda Chintamani. Statement III is wrong, because Rajaraja Narendra gave Nandampudi to Narayana Bhattu and Nannaya only composed the grant (official key: I and III).

104.x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni, not Firdausi. The other three source-author pairs are correctly matched.
104.tq: Find the swapped author in a list of medieval sources.
xs: **Kitab-ul-Hind — Firdausi** is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.

104.x: Tahqiq-i-Hind (Kitab-ul-Hind) was written in Arabic by Al-Biruni (Alberuni) c. 1030. Megasthenes wrote Indica; Herodotus wrote Histories.

104.x: Al-Biruni of Khwarizm came with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind). Ibn Battuta came under Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Khusrau and Ferishta were later writers.

104.s: Al-Biruni wrote his Kitab-ul-Hind in which language?
104.x: Al-Biruni of Khwarazm wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) in Arabic around 1030.

104.s: Foreign travellers' accounts of medieval India should generally be used by historians in which manner?
o: They should replace inscriptions and archaeological evidence as the primary basis of reconstruction.
They should be ignored altogether because they were written by outsiders unfamiliar with Indian languages.
They should be accepted as accurate in every detail since the travellers were neutral eyewitnesses.
They should supplement Indian texts and be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.
104.x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian textual evidence, but their statements must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
104.tq: Apply the principle of corroboration across different source types.
xs: Foreign accounts **supplement Indian texts** and must be **cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They neither replace other evidence nor are accurate in every detail; nor are they to be ignored.
xa: ⚠ Court histories have their own bias — they **glorify the patron**.
**Taj Mahal** case (**Jul 2026**): evidence that **Shah Jahan** built it includes **European travellers' accounts**.

104.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ziauddin Barani?

xs: Barani **wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His kingship theory is in **Fatawa-i-Jahandari**.
The Persian envoy to Vijayanagara was **Abdur Razzaq**; the Golconda school was founded by **Mir Hashimi**.
xa: Barani's **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers **Balban** to early **Firoz Tughlaq**.
It is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations** and Sultanate attacks on **south Indian kingdoms**.

105.x: Balban took the regnal title Ghiyasuddin Balban on his accession in 1266; his earlier name was Bahauddin.

105.x: Balban introduced the Persian festival Nauroz (Nowruz) at his court, copying Iranian kings, along with sijda and paibos. Iltutmish, Alauddin and Firuz did not.

105.s: Who among the following introduced the famous Persian festival ‘Nawruz’ in India?
105.x: Balban introduced the Persian festival Nauroz (Nowruz) at his court, copying Iranian kings, along with sijda and paibos. Iltutmish, Alauddin and Firuz did not.

105.s: Who among the following Amirs was the one publicly flogged by the orders of Sultan Balban?
105.x: Barani records that Balban had Malik Baqbaq, the amir and governor of Badaun, publicly flogged for having a servant beaten to death – an example of his 'blood and iron' justice.

105.x: Balban introduced the Persian festival Nauroz (Nowruz) at his court, copying Iranian kings, along with sijda and paibos. Iltutmish, Alauddin and Firuz did not.

It was written in Persian and deals only with Central Asia.
It was written in Hindavi and describes only Vijayanagara.
It was written in Sanskrit under the patronage of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
108.x: Rihla, also called Kitab-ul-Rehla, was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
108.tq: Use the language-and-content combination to reject swapped literary traditions.
xs: Rihla **was written in Arabic and describes the Sultanate and the Deccan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also called **Kitab-ul-Rehla**.
It was not Persian, Hindavi or Sanskrit.
xa: It records **uluq** and **dawa** couriers, the **spy system** and **sati**.
Its author, **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**, was a Moroccan born in **1304**.

108.s: In whose reign did Ibn Battuta, the first foreign traveller to Vijayanagara, visit the kingdom?
108.x: Ibn Battuta is identified in this context as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of Harihara I.
108.tq: Distinguish the earliest associated ruler from the more famous later Vijayanagara monarchs.
xs: Ibn Battuta was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** by **Harihara and Bukka**.
xa: He came to India in **1333** and served MBT as **Qazi of Delhi**.
He was sent as **envoy to China** in **1342**.

108.s: Ibn Battuta, who came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was a native of:
108.x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco and reached India in 1333.

108.s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta is correct?
o: He was made Qazi of Delhi by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
He reported that sati was completely banned.
108.x: Born at Tangiers, he reached India in 1333; he noted that sati needed the Sultan's permission.

108.s: Which medieval historian described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'?
108.x: Barani called him a mixture of opposites.

108.s: The Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi was written by:
108.x: It is Firoz Tughlaq's own account; Barani wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

108.s: During Sultanate period, 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' was related with which of the following?
108.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was MBT's department of agriculture, to bring waste land under cultivation – not the army, revenue or entertainment.

108.s: Who amongst the following established ‘Diwan-e-amirkothi’ during Delhi Sultanate?
108.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq – not Alauddin, Firoz or Iltutmish.

108.s: Which Sultan of Delhi had established a separate Agriculture Department and had planned the ‘rotation of crops’ ?
108.x: MBT created the separate agriculture department (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi), which planned better crops and crop rotation in a trial block; Iltutmish, Balban and Alauddin are not linked with it.

108.s: Which ruler established 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' department?
108.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was Muhammad bin Tughlaq's agriculture department, not Firoz's or Alauddin's.

108.s: Diwan-E-Kohi is associated with–
108.x: Diwan-i-Kohi (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi) was the agriculture department of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

108.s: How did the 'dawa' couriers of the Sultanate postal system described by Ibn Battuta travel?
108.x: Dawa were foot couriers; uluq were horse couriers.

108.s: Which rebel was Muhammad bin Tughlaq pursuing when he died at Thatta in 1351?
108.x: MBT died at Thatta on the way to Sindh, chasing the rebel Taghi after a Gujarat revolt.

108.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi – MBT's agriculture department for waste land; Taqavi (sondhar) – loans for seeds and wells; Swarga-dwari – famine-relief camp near Kannauj; Uluq – horse couriers every four miles (dawa – foot couriers).

108.s: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Alauddin Khalji first set up a separate Ariz's department
Balban introduced the branding system of horses of military
Muhammad bin Tughlaq was succeeded by his uncle to the Delhi throne
Firuz Tughlaq set up a separate department of slaves
108.x: Firoz set up the Diwan-i-Bandagan, a separate department of slaves. Horse branding was Alauddin's, the Ariz department Balban's, and MBT was succeeded by his cousin Firoz, not an uncle.

108.s: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statement is correct?
o: Alauddin Khilji first set up a separate Ariz’s department.
Balban introduced the branding system of horses for his military.
Muhammad-bin-Tughluq was succeeded by his uncle to the throne.
Firuz Shah Tughlaq set up a separate department of slaves.
108.x: Firoz set up the Diwan-i-Bandagan for slaves. Dagh was Alauddin's, the Ariz department Balban's, and Firoz was MBT's cousin.

108.s: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani did not serve under which of the following rulers?
108.x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa for Alauddin (1305) and later served MBT and Firoz; he lived long after Iltutmish (d. 1236).

108.s: For whom did Ain-ul-Mulk Multani win Malwa in 1305?
108.x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa for Alauddin in 1305 and later served MBT and Firoz.

108.s: With whom is the Dahsala system associated?
108.x: Todar Mal devised the Dahsala; Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.
n: Akbar is associated with Din-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Akbar is associated with Mansabdari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Akbar is associated with Sulh-i-kul. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Akbarnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Ain-i-Akbari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Todar Mal is associated with the Dahsala system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Jizya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Zinda Pir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Deccan policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Todar Mal is associated with revenue reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]

**Shah Jahan** — **Taj Mahal**, Mughal architecture.
**Shivaji** — title **Chhatrapati**, **Ashtapradhan**.

108.s:

c. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq

108.x: Balban – Zil-i-Ilahi, sijda, paibos; Alauddin – dagh, huliya, Siri; Ghiyasuddin – Tughlaqabad; Firoz – canals and public works.

108.s: Which Sultan of Delhi made a rule that, in any given year, the land revenue can be increased only nominally, viz one-tenth or one-eleventh of the fixed revenue?
108.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq allowed any increase in land revenue of only about one-tenth (one-eleventh) a year. Alauddin had raised it to half; Balban and Firoz are not linked to this rule.

108.s: Which technique was used in times of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq for measurement of Khalisa land?
108.x:
Printed key: Kankut. Moreland and IGNOU: Ghiyasuddin replaced measurement by crop-sharing (batai); galla-bakhshi is another name for sharing, so batai is keyed.
Ghiyasuddin dropped Alauddin's measurement (masahat) and assessed khalisa land by sharing the actual crop (batai / hukm-i-hasil). The printed key Kankut is wrong: kankut is estimation of the standing crop, not sharing.

108.s: Whom did Ghazi Malik kill to become Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320?
108.x: Ghazi Malik, earlier governor of Punjab, killed Khusrau Shah and became Sultan in 1320.
xa: He built the **Tughlaqabad** fort.
He was the **first Sultan to start irrigation/canal works**.

108.s: Where did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq die in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed?
108.x: He died at Afghanpur in 1325 (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan); he had built Tughlaqabad.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** suspects a plot by **Juna Khan**.
Cities of Delhi: **Siri** — **Alauddin Khalji**; **Tughlaqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

108.s: After its capture by the Tughlaqs in 1323, Warangal was renamed:
108.x: Warangal became Sultanpur; Daulatabad was the renamed Devagiri.

108.s: Which of the following statements about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is correct?
o: Prataparudra II died in the Godavari while being taken to Delhi.
He was Governor of Punjab under Balban.
He limited any increase in land revenue to about one-tenth in a year.
108.x: He was Alauddin's governor, Warangal became Sultanpur, and Prataparudra II died in the Narmada.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq replaced Alauddin's measurement on khalisa land with sharing of the crop (batai).
Reason (R): Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
108.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the shift from measurement to crop-sharing was a revenue choice; digging canals is a separate measure.

108.s: The Hindu king that has given shelter to Bahauddin Gurshasp who revolted against Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq in A.D.1326.
108.x: Bahauddin Gurshasp, MBT's cousin, revolted in 1326 and fled to Kampila Deva of Kampili; MBT then took Kampili and captured Harihara and Bukka. The Reddi and Musunuri chiefs rose only later.

108.s: Around which year did the Reddis expel the Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra?
108.x: Coastal Andhra was freed around 1325, before the Madurai Sultanate (1335), Vijayanagara (1336) and the Bahmani kingdom (1347).
xa: **Kapaya Nayaka** recaptured Warangal also in **1336**.
These break-aways followed MBT's **badly carried out** schemes.

108.s: Under whose guidance did Harihara and Bukka found Vijayanagara?
108.x: Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited Vijayanagara in **Harihara I's** reign.
⚠ In **1336** Kapaya Nayaka also recaptured **Warangal**.

108.s: For understanding which of the following are the Vilasa copper plate of Prolaya Nayaka and Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam important?
o: The conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions
The revenue system of the Bahmani kingdom
The maritime trade policy of the Madurai Sultanate
The succession disputes among the Mughal emperors
108.x: The Vilasa copper plate and Madhura Vijayam describe the conditions prevailing under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions.
108.tq: Associate each source with the historical situation it records, not with a later administrative theme.
xs: They describe **conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Vilasa copper plate** is **Prolaya Nayaka's**; **Madhura Vijayam** is **Gangadevi's**.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka led the fight to free Andhra (**Vilasa** grant, c. **1330**).
**Kapaya Nayaka** then **recaptured Warangal in 1336**.

108.s: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in the year:
108.x: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336; the Bahmani kingdom followed in 1347.

108.s: Who recaptured Warangal from the Tughlaqs in 1336?
108.x: Kapaya Nayaka, successor of Prolaya Nayaka, recaptured Warangal in 1336.

108.s: Madhura Vijayam, which describes the conquest of the Madurai Sultanate, was written by:
108.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam.

108.s: Which Telugu Brahmin convert became the wazir of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Malik Maqbul (Khan-i-Jahan), originally Jagannatha Pandit, became Firoz Shah's wazir.

108.s: Who was the last ruler of the Tughluq dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
108.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah (1394-1412) was the last Tughlaq; Nusrat Shah was only his rival at Firozabad.

108.s: Who took Delhi in 1414, ending the Tughlaq period?
108.x: Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414, closing the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

108.s: Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of:
108.x: Timur's invasion came in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq, after Firoz's death; Khizr Khan later founded the Sayyid dynasty.

108.s: The Sayyid dynasty of Delhi was founded by:
108.x: Khizr Khan, Timur's nominee, founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414, ending the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

108.s: Which Sultan of Delhi made the iqtas hereditary?
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the iqtas hereditary; Alauddin had kept them under strict control.

108.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Token currency was introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Firoz abolished about 24 taxes and kept the four Islamic ones.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

108.x: Firoz led two unsuccessful expeditions to Bengal against Haji Iliyas; Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.

109.s: The Mughal Empire in India was founded by:

109.x: After Panipat (1526) Babur took Delhi and Agra with the Lodi treasure.

109.s: The reason for Babur’s victory over Ibrahim Lodi was-
109.x:
Some printed keys: skilled commandant. Most books: artillery.
Babur's field artillery and muskets (Ustad Ali Quli, Mustafa), which Ibrahim lacked, are the usual reason for the victory; "skilled commandant" is too general. The same question elsewhere in the app is keyed artillery.

109.s: The main reason for Babur’s victory in the battle of Panipat was –
109.x: Babur won with a much smaller army through skilled warfare (tulughma, araba and artillery together); the Afghans' internal disputes were only a background cause.

109.s: Whom did Babur defeat in the first battle of Panipat?
109.x: Babur defeated and killed Ibrahim Lodi at First Panipat; Rana Sanga was beaten at Khanwa.

109.s: At which of the following battles was artillery used for the first time by one of the two armies?
109.x: First Panipat (1526) was the first Indian battle where one side (Babur) used field artillery.

109.s: The reason of Babur’s victory over Ibrahim Lodi was
109.x:
Some printed keys: skilled commandant. Most books: artillery.
Artillery: Babur's field guns and muskets were decisive at Panipat. A copy of this question in the app was keyed "skilled commandant".

109.s: In which year did Babur defeat Sultan Ibrahim Lodi at the battle of Panipat?
109.x: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat on 21 April 1526.

109.s: Babur attacked India in the year
109.x: Babur's decisive invasion came in 1526 (First Panipat); 1527 is Khanwa. He had raided the north-west from 1519.

109.s: What was Babur's flanking manoeuvre at the First Battle of Panipat called?
109.x: Tulughma was the flanking manoeuvre; Araba carts chained together formed the defensive line.
xa: Field **artillery** and **muskets** were the decisive factor.
Gunners: **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**.
Date: **21 April 1526**; older notes say **20 April**.

109.s: Who was the only Sultan of Delhi to die on the battlefield?
109.x: Ibrahim Lodi was killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat.

109.x: Fought on 21 April 1526; 1556 was the Second Battle and 1761 the Third.

109.s: Who was the ruler of the Delhi when Portuguese made their entry into India?
109.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
109.x: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, in Sikandar Lodi's reign (1489-1517); Ibrahim came in 1517.

109.s: Who was the founder of the City of Agra?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted the capital there.

109.s: Which ruler founded the city of Agra?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504; Akbar and Shah Jahan only built there.

109.s: Which one of the following Sultans is known for having abolished the tax on grains?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains along with other taxes and trade restrictions.

109.s: Which medieval Sultan has the credit of founding the city of Agra and making it the capital of the Sultanate?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra and made it the capital of the Sultanate.

109.s: Agra city was founded by :
109.x: Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504, not by Bahlul, Balban or Firoz.

109.s: Who among the following composed poems with the pen name ‘Gulrukhi’?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian poetry as Gulrukhi.

109.s: Which of the following Sultans founded a town where now stands Agra?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded the town that is now Agra (1504).

109.s: With whom is the Gaz-i-Sikandari, a yard used to measure land, associated?
109.x: Gaz-i-Sikandari was Sikandar Lodi's land-measuring yard; he also abolished several taxes and used audits and spies.
xa: **Sikandar Lodi** reigned **1489-1517** and founded **Agra (1504)**.
Pen name: **Gulrukhi** (Persian poetry).
Buildings: **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.

109.tq: Combine territorial expansion statements and verify each geographical claim.
109.s: Sikandar Lodi extended his rule from Punjab to Bihar and subdued the ruler of:
109.x: Sikandar Lodi subdued Jaunpur and defeated Bengal rulers and Rajput chiefs.

109.tq: Combine territorial expansion statements and verify each geographical claim.
109.s: The city of Agra was founded in 1504 by:
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra and made it his capital.

109.s: What was the original name of Sikandar Lodi?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi was Nizam Khan, third son of Bahlol, crowned on 17 July 1489.

109.s: The 'Gaz-i-Sikandari', a yard for measuring land later used by Sher Shah and Akbar, was introduced by:
109.x: Sikandar Lodi introduced the Gaz-i-Sikandari; Akbar later introduced the Ilahi gaz.

109.s: Which of the following statements about Sikandar Lodi is correct?
o: He was the son of Ibrahim Lodi.
He had a Sanskrit work on astronomy translated into Persian.
He had a Sanskrit work on medicine translated into Persian.
109.x: Sikandar Lodi, son of Bahlol Lodi, had a medical work translated; the Ilahi gaz was Akbar's.

109.s: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498 during the reign of which Delhi Sultan?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi ruled 1489–1517, so Vasco da Gama's 1498 arrival fell in his reign.

109.s: The Moth ki Masjid in Delhi was built during the reign of:
109.x: Moth ki Masjid was built by Sikandar Lodi's minister Wazir Miyan Bhoiya.

109.s: Who was the Delhi Sultan at the time of Timur's invasion?
109.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
109.x: Timur sacked Delhi in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud (printed "Mohammad") Tughlaq, the last Tughlaq; Daulat Khan Lodi ruled only in 1413.

109.s: Which one of the following dynasties ruled over India after the invasion of Timur?
109.x: After Timur, the Tughlaqs lingered to 1412-14 and then the Sayyids (Khizr Khan, 1414) ruled Delhi; the Lodis came in 1451.

109.s: In which year did Timur Lang attack India?
109.x: Timur invaded India and sacked Delhi in December 1398.

109.s: The 14th Century Turkish conqueror of India, also known as Tamurlane, was:
109.x: Timur (Taimur, Tamerlane) was the 14th-century Turkish conqueror who sacked Delhi in 1398; Chengiz Khan (Temujin) was a 13th-century Mongol.

109.s: Which of the following was NOT an effect of Timur's invasion of India?
o: Immediate establishment of the Mughal Empire in Delhi
Break-up of the Tughlaq state into regional kingdoms
Later rise of Khizr Khan's Sayyid dynasty
109.x: The Mughal Empire was established much later, by Babur in 1526.
xa: Timur sacked **Delhi** in **December 1398**, after crossing the **Indus** and passing **Multan** and **Bhatnair**.
Regional kingdoms that emerged: **Jaunpur**, **Malwa**, **Gujarat**.
Khizr Khan founded the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.

109.s: Which of the following statements about Timur's invasion is correct?
o: Timur claimed descent from Mahmud of Ghazni.
It led directly to the founding of the Mughal Empire.
The Lodis came to power immediately after it.
It took place in 1398 during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq.
109.x: Timur sacked Delhi in December 1398; he claimed descent from Chengiz Khan and the Sayyids followed in 1414.

109.s: The dynasty that came to power in Delhi soon after Timur's invasion was the:
109.x: Khizr Khan, Timur's nominee, founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.

109.s: Who was last ruler of Lodi dynsty?
109.x: Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26) was the last Lodi and last Delhi Sultan, killed at Panipat; Bahlul founded the dynasty.

109.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Afghan rulers of Delhi?
o: Sikandar Lodi – Ibrahim Lodi – Bahlol Lodi
Sikandar Lodi – Bahlol Lodi – Ibrahim Lodi
Bahlol Lodi – Sikandar Lodi – Ibrahim Lodi
Bahlol Lodi – Ibrahim Lodi – Sikandar Lodi
109.x: Bahlol Lodi (1451-89) → Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517) → Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26).

109.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Afghan rulers to the throne of Delhi?
o: Sikandar Shah-Bahlul Khan Lodi or Lodi Ibrahim

II. Alauddin Khilji and Muhammad bin Tughluq demanded one-sixth of the agricultural produce as revenue from the peasants.
Which of the statements(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: Only I: Alauddin held discourses with the Jain Acharya Mahasena. Alauddin demanded one-half, and MBT raised it further in the Doab – not one-sixth.

113.s:
With reference to Sultan Alauddin Khilji, consider the following statements.

I. Alauddin Khilji fixed the prices of foodgrains.

II. Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan, who paid his soldiers in cash.

III. During Alauddin Khilji’s rule, the share of the land revenue to be paid by the peasant was raised to half of the produce.
Which of these statements are correct?
113.x: All three: Alauddin fixed grain prices, paid soldiers in cash and raised land revenue to half the produce.

113.s: Who gave taccavi (sondhar) loans for agriculture?
113.x: MBT set up Diwan-i-Kohi and gave taccavi (sondhar) loans.

113.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, 'Khalisa' land referred to:
o: Crown land whose revenue went to the royal treasury
113.x: Khalisa was crown land; iqta was revenue assigned to officials in place of salary and inam was religious grant land.

113.s: Which of the following cities was a Mughal imperial centre?
113.x: Agra was a Mughal imperial centre; Siri, Tughlaqabad and Jahanpanah were Sultanate cities of Alauddin, Ghiyasuddin and MBT.
n: Agra was a Mughal imperial centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal imperial capital, especially under Shah Jahan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Lahore was a Mughal political and architectural centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Akbar's fort. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Mughal administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was also known as Prayagraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal political centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]

113.s: Which one of the following was NOT founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
113.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji. Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Firozabad, Fatehabad, Hisar-Firoza and Jaunpur.
113.tq: Find the odd city-founder association within the same historical period.
xs: **Siri** was NOT founded by Firoz; it was **Alauddin Khalji's** — option **(4)**.
Firoz founded **Firozabad**, **Hisar Firoza**, **Fatehabad** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** = Ghiyasuddin; **Jahanpanah** = MBT.
**Agra (1504)** = Sikandar Lodi.

113.s: Which of the following pairs (town – founder) is INCORRECTLY matched?
113.x: Jahanpanah was founded by MBT; Alauddin built Siri.

113.s: Why was paper-making important for the Sultanate administration?
113.x: The availability of paper strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping in the Sultanate administration.
113.tq: Link a technological development to its administrative consequence.
xs: Paper-making **strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping** — option **(2)**.
It did not replace coinage: the **tanka** (silver) and **jital** (copper) remained the basic coins.
xa: Paper and the **Persian wheel** were lasting gains.
Other Turkish technologies: **glass-making**, **spinning wheel**, better **looms**.
Superior **mortar** for **arches and domes**.

113.s: Which statement regarding slaves during the Sultanate period is correct?
o: Slaves were employed only in agriculture and not traded
Ibn Battuta mentioned slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves
Slaves were absent from urban markets
Firoz Tughlaq abolished all forms of slavery
113.x: Ibn Battuta referred to slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves.
113.tq: Reject absolute statements and combine the two documented features of slavery.
xs: **Ibn Battuta** mentioned **slave markets**, and **Firoz** had a **separate department** for slaves — option **(2)**.
Firoz did not abolish slavery; slaves were traded in markets.
xa: Firoz's slave department = **Diwan-i-Bandagan**.
Firoz also ran about **36 karkhanas**.

113.s: Which social developments are associated with medieval Hindu society during the Sultanate period?
o: Widespread widow remarriage and inter-caste dining among Hindus
Royal decrees by the Sultans banning sati across the empire
Replacement of varna-based occupations by iqta administration
The continuation of caste order and the spread of sati and purdah
113.x: Hindu society retained its caste order, while sati and purdah spread during this period.
113.tq: Identify the option that preserves both social features rather than reversing them.
xs: Hindu society kept its **caste order**, while **sati and purdah spread** — option **(4)**.
So caste did not disappear and sati was not abolished.
xa: **Nobles** held iqtas; **ulema** kept religious law.
**Peasants** bore the revenue burden.

113.x: Firoz Tughlaq maintained about 36 royal karkhanas supplying the court.

113.x: Firoz took the manuscripts from Jawalamukhi at Nagarkot (Kangra) and had some translated into Persian.

114.s: The historian Barani refused to consider the state in India under Delhi Sultans as truly Islamic because:
o: the majority of the population did not follow Islam
the Muslims theologists were often disregarded
the Sultan supplemented the Muslim law by framing his own regulations
religious freedom was accorded to non‑Muslims
114.x: Barani said the state was not truly Islamic because the Sultan supplemented the sharia with his own state laws (zawabit).

114.s: The historian Barani did not consider the state in India under Delhi Sultans as truly Islamic because :
o: The majority of the population did not follow Islam
The Muslim theologists were often disregarded
The Sultan supplemented the Muslim law by framing
The religious freedom was accorded to non-Muslims
114.x: Barani said the state was not truly Islamic because the Sultan supplemented the sharia with his own state laws (zawabit).

114.s: Who were called ‘Dastar-Bandan’?
114.x: The ulema were called Dastar-bandan (turban-wearers); the Sayyids were the Kulah-daran.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate social groups:
1. The Ajlaf were lower-status Muslims.
2. The Kulah-daran were the ulema.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: 1 is correct: the Ajlaf were lower-status Muslims. 2 is wrong: the Kulah-daran were the Sayyids; the ulema were the Dastar-bandan.

114.s: Which officer of the Delhi Sultanate was in charge of religious grants and also acted as Chief Qazi?
114.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur handled religious grants and was also the Chief Qazi.

a. Dastar-bandan
b. Kulah-daran
c. Ashraf
d. Ajlaf

114.x: Dastar-bandan – ulema; kulah-daran – Sayyids; ashraf – Turks, Persians, Afghans of foreign descent; ajlaf – lower-status Indian convert Muslims.

114.x: Barani wrote the Fatawa-i-Jahandari on statecraft (and the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi); the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is by Minhaj-us-Siraj.

114.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur managed religious grants and affairs; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief judge.

114.s: Which Sultan of Delhi had levied ‘Jizya’ on Brahmins?
114.x: Firuz Tughlaq was the first to levy jizya on Brahmins, who had been exempt earlier.

114.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Leaned on Sufis against the ulema
Firoz Tughlaq — Followed the ulema’s advice
Sikandar Lodi — Tolerant ruler who gave non-Muslims important posts
114.x: Sikandar Lodi was orthodox; he destroyed temples at Mathura, broke the Jwalamukhi images at Nagarkot and imposed jizya. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
114.tq: Find the one reversed ruler–policy association.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi – tolerant ruler** is wrong: he was **orthodox** — option **(3)**.
He destroyed **Mathura** temples, broke the **Jwalamukhi** images at **Nagarkot** and imposed **jizya**.
The rest are correct: **MBT** leaned on Sufis; **Firoz** followed the ulema; **Iltutmish** gave non-Muslims posts.
xa: **Jalaluddin Khalji** = first Sultan benevolent to Hindus.
⚠ **Alauddin** = ulema shut out; **Firoz** = ulema followed.

114.s: Which Sultan leaned on the Sufis against the ulema and visited the Ajmer shrine?
114.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq leaned on the Sufis against the ulema; Firoz, by contrast, followed the ulema.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (Sultan – religious approach)?
o: Alauddin Khalji – followed the counsel of the ulema
Jalaluddin Khalji – first Sultan benevolent to Hindus
Muhammad bin Tughlaq – leaned on the Sufis
114.x: Alauddin kept the ulema out of state affairs; it was Firoz Tughlaq who followed the ulema.

114.s: Which of the following was NOT exempt from jizya under the Sultans?
114.x: Women, children, the old and the disabled were exempt; jizya fell on other non-Muslims in place of military service.

114.s: The Delhi Sultan who imposed jizya even on Brahmins, who had earlier been exempt, was:
114.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq extended jizya to Brahmins. Women, children and the old remained exempt.

114.s: Under the Delhi Sultans, which of the following was NOT generally exempt from jizya?
114.x: Jizya fell on adult non-Muslim men; women, children and the old were exempt. Sikandar Lodi also imposed it.

114.s: The Sultan who told Qazi Mughisuddin that he ordered whatever was good for the state was:
114.x: Alauddin Khalji's reply to Qazi Mughisuddin shows his view that state interest came before the ulema.

114.s: Which of the following statements about the Delhi Sultans is correct?
o: Hindu gods were worshipped in the palace under Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Sultan benevolent to Hindus
Firoz Shah Tughlaq leaned on the Sufis against the ulema
Balban told Qazi Mughisuddin that he ordered whatever was good for the state
114.x: Palace worship was under Khusrau Shah; the reply to Mughisuddin was Alauddin's; it was Muhammad bin Tughlaq who leaned on the Sufis.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

A is false, but R is true

114.s: The Sultan who destroyed the temples of Mathura and broke the images of Nagarkot was:
114.x: Sikandar Lodi destroyed the Mathura temples and the Nagarkot images.

114.s: Which of the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate is correct?
o: Temple destruction under the Sultans had only religious motives
Firoz Tughlaq sought recognition from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt
The Abbasid Caliphate of Baghdad was still standing in Firoz Tughlaq's time
Ibrahim Lodi destroyed the temples of Mathura
114.x: Baghdad fell in 1258, so Firoz looked to the Caliph in Egypt; Sikandar Lodi destroyed the Mathura temples, and temple destruction also served political ends.

114.s: Which of the following Sultans had most number of slaves in his court?
114.x: Firuz Tughlaq had about 1,80,000 slaves and a separate department (Diwan-i-Bandagan) for them.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women in the Sultanate period?
o: Chand Bibi ruled the Delhi Sultanate
Jauhar was performed at Chittor in 1303
114.x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar and never ruled Delhi; Razia was the only woman ruler of Delhi.

114.s: Which traveller recorded the practice of sati in the Sultanate period?
114.x: Ibn Battuta recorded sati in the 14th century; Al-Biruni came earlier, with Mahmud of Ghazni.

114.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Purdah was unknown in the Sultanate period.
Al-Biruni recorded sati in the Sultanate period.
Purdah spread among upper-class women of north India from the 13th century.
The jauhar at Ranthambhor took place in 1303.
114.x: Purdah spread from the 13th century. Ranthambhor's jauhar was in 1301 (Chittor 1303); Ibn Battuta recorded sati.

o: Alauddin Khalji's third market dealt in horses, slaves and cattle
Slavery was unknown in the Vijayanagara empire

114.s:

2. The social liberation theory explains conversions only partially, as caste-like ranks survived among converts.

114.x: Both statements are correct: political patronage and social liberation are each only partial explanations, since caste-like ranks persisted among converts.

114.s: In which of the following did the Bhakti movement have its indigenous roots?
114.x: The Bhakti movement had indigenous roots in the Alvars and Nayanars; Islam only reinforced its egalitarian and anti-ritual tendencies.
xa: Islam shaped later Bhakti's **egalitarianism** (**Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas**).
Khanqahs and dargahs drew **Hindus and Muslims** alike.

114.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Arthashastra – Compared by Al-Biruni with the Sufi idea of divine love
Amritakund – Translated into Arabic and Persian
Al-Biruni – Parallel between the Sufi idea of the soul and Patanjali's Yoga Sutra
114.x: Al-Biruni compared the Sufi idea of divine love with the Gita, not the Arthashastra; the other pairs are correct.
xa: **Nizamuddin Auliya** was struck by **Nath-yogic** body theory.
Amritakund = a **Hatha-yoga** text.

114.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Raja Man Singh of Gwalior — Man Kautuhal
114.x: Dalail-i-Firozshahi was associated with Sanskrit texts translated during Firoz Tughlaq's reign, not with Baba Farid. Pir Bhodan, Raja Man Singh and Jayasi are correctly matched.
114.tq: Find the swapped author-work association among closely related cultural figures.
xs: **Baba Farid – Dalail-i-Firozshahi** is wrong: Baba Farid was a **Chishti Sufi** — option **(1)**.
The rest are correct: **Jayasi – Padmavat**; **Raja Man Singh of Gwalior – Man Kautuhal**; **Pir Bhodan – Sufi musician**.
xa: Other Chishtis: **Muinuddin**, **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
Padmavat uses **human love** as metaphor for **divine love**.

114.s: Which musical instrument is credited to Amir Khusrau?
114.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with the sitar and with qawwali.

114.s: Akkanna and Madanna, called the 'Andhra Sultans', belonged to which kingdom?
114.x: Akkanna and Madanna were the 'Andhra Sultans' of Qutb Shahi Golconda under Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

114.s: Which of the following statements about religious conversion in medieval India is correct?
o: The 'sword' theory of forced mass conversion is universally accepted by historians.
Conversion was confined to the urban nobility of Delhi.
Sufi influence with agrarian expansion was a major factor in Bengal and Punjab.
Sufis played no role in the spread of Islam in India.
114.x: Historians reject the sword theory and see Sufi influence with agrarian expansion as key in Bengal and Punjab.

114.x: The Chishtis used Hindavi to reach ordinary people, an important aspect of syncretism in the Sultanate period.

114.s: In the Deccan kingdoms, the foreign Muslims (immigrants from Persia and Central Asia) were known as:
114.x: Foreign Muslims were the Afaqis (Pardesis); the local Deccani Muslims were the Dakhnis.

114.x: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) made the Bhadrachalam grants.

115.s: The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the -
115.x: The Alai Darwaza (1311) of Alauddin Khalji introduced the horse-shoe arch with a lotus-bud fringe, and has the first true dome. Balban's tomb has the first true arch, not the horse-shoe arch.

115.s: The first true arch in the Sultanate memorial could be seen in
115.x: Balban's tomb at Mehrauli shows the first true arch in India. The Alai Darwaza has the first true dome; Iltutmish's tomb and Quwwat-ul-Islam use corbelled (false) arches.

115.s: India’s first tomb constructed in the Indo-Islamic style was
115.x:
Most books and keys: Balban's tomb (first tomb in a true Indo-Islamic style, with the true arch). Strictly: the first Islamic tomb in India is Sultan Ghari (1231), built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud (app notes 1:115; ASI).
Balban's tomb (Mehrauli) is given as the first tomb in a purely Indo-Islamic style, being the first with a true arch. Humayun's tomb is Mughal; Aibak's tomb (Lahore) and Alauddin's tomb are not counted as the first.

115.s: Which among the following is ‘Octagonal tomb’?
115.x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb is octagonal (an arched verandah round the chamber) and has the first double dome. Balban's, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's and Firoz Shah's tombs are square.

115.s:
Match the following.

A. 'Lotus bud' fringe on the underside of the arch
B. Emergence of octagonal tomb
C. Use of Bodegoi in the pillar
D. Massive entrance gate with inclined walls
List II (Associated Dynasty)

2. Vijayanagara

115.s: For which of the following is the tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq at Tughlaqabad noted?

Sloping walls and a marble dome
A horseshoe arch with lotus-bud fringe

xa: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city was built by **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style is called the "**crisis period of architecture**" (Mongol threat, finances).
Qutb complex holds the **Tomb of Iltutmish**, not the Tughlaq tombs.

115.s: The domes and false arches of Tughlaq architecture show the influence of which styles?
115.x: Tughlaq domes and false arches show Syrian and Byzantine influence.
xa: The Tughlaq period is called the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Examples: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city and **Ghiyasuddin's tomb** (battered walls, **marble dome**).
First **octagonal** tomb (Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's) also dates from the **Tughlaq** period.

115.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Indian trabeate style of building?
115.x: The true arch with keystone came with Indo-Islamic architecture; the trabeate style used lintel, pillar and corbel.

115.s: Surkhi, used in Indo-Islamic buildings, was:
o: Brick dust used in lime mortar
115.x: Surkhi was brick dust mixed in lime mortar.

115.s: What is ‘Adhai Din ka Zhonpda’?
115.x: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer is a mosque built by Qutbuddin Aibak from temple material. It is not a temple, hut or tower.

115.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
115.x: Tughlaqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque is Sher Shah Suri's, the Moth Masjid dates from Sikandar Lodi's reign and the Kirti Stambha is Rana Kumbha's.

Moth Masjid was built during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]

**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** built **Jahanpanah**.

115.x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.

Tughlaq style: **sloping (battered) walls**, pointed domes, false arches.

115.s: The Qutab Minar was named after: merican

Most books and keys: named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki. Some historians: named after its builder Qutbuddin Aibak (Wikipedia, citing ASI).
The Qutb Minar is commonly held to be named after the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki; it was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish. Iltutmish and Raziya are not its namesakes.

115.s: Who amongst the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey and added the fifth storey. Aibak built the first storey and Iltutmish the next three; Sikandar Lodi only repaired it.

115.s: Who among the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey and added the fifth storey. Aibak built the first storey and Iltutmish the next three; Sikandar Lodi only repaired it.

Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:
1. Sikandar Lodi carried out repairs to it.
2. It was completed by Alauddin Khalji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: 1 is correct: Sikandar Lodi, like Firoz Tughlaq, repaired the minar. 2 is wrong: Qutbuddin Aibak began it and Iltutmish completed it; Alauddin only planned the unfinished Alai Minar.

115.s: Who built the second, third and fourth storeys of the Qutb Minar?
115.x: Aibak built the first storey (c. 1199); Iltutmish added the next three.

o: Sikandar Lodi added its fifth storey.
Qutbuddin Aibak built its first storey around 1199.

115.x: The Iron Pillar is attributed to Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

115.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments' World Heritage Site?
115.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is at Tughlaqabad; the others are in the Qutb complex (WHS 1993).

115.s: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world?
115.x: The Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur), tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, has one of the largest domes in the world (second only to St Peter's, Rome) and a whispering gallery.

115.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid

xs: **Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid** are all **Bengal** monuments — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is **Bahmani** (Bidar); (2) mixes **Jaunpur**, Daulatabad and **Bijapur**; (3) mixes **Hyderabad**, Bengal and **Mandu**.
xa: Bengal style: **brick** building, **curved roofs**.
**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

115.x: The Adina Mosque is associated with Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat. Gol Gumbaz is at Bijapur, Jami Masjid at Mandu and Chand Minar at Daulatabad.

Others are correct: **Chand Minar–Daulatabad**, **Gol Gumbaz–Bijapur**, **Jami Masjid–Mandu** (Malwa).
xa: **Gujarat** style: strong Hindu-Jain carving; **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.
⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal); **Gol Gumbaz** = Bijapur.

115.x: The Gulbarga Jama Masjid is unique for having its whole courtyard covered.

115.s: What is the name of the 16th century stepwell that the Archaeological Survey of India recently conserved in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund India?
o: More than one of the above
115.x: Rajon ki Baoli, Mehrauli (c. 1506, Daulat Khan Lodi, reign of Sikandar Lodi) was conserved by the ASI with the World Monuments Fund India (TCS Foundation funding) and reopened in May 2025. Agrasen ki Baoli and Chauki Bavdi were not this project.

Consider the following statements:

115.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
115.x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.

xs: **Golconda Fort** is known for its **acoustics** and **piped water** — option **(2)**.
A handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
Covered courtyard = **Gulbarga**; curved brick roofs = **Bengal**; propylon = **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers.
Golconda Jami Masjid gateway has fine **Nastaliq** calligraphy.

o: Muhammad Adil Shah's Gol Gumbaz, Bijapur
Ibrahim Shah Sharqi's Atala Masjid, Jaunpur

115.x: Mir Momin Astarabadi, Peshwa of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, planned the city on the Isfahan model.

115.x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 and the capital moved there in 1592.

116.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
116.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

116.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
116.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

116.s: The savant of both languages “Hindi and Persian” was –
116.x: Amir Khusrau wrote in both Persian and Hindavi (Hindi), hence 'savant of both languages'. Akbar, Tansen and Bairam Khan are Mughal-era figures.

116.s: Father of new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi or Hindustani style was :
116.x: Amir Khusrau created the Sabak-i-Hindi (Indian style) of Persian poetry. Barani was a historian, Afif and Isami chroniclers.

116.s: Who among the following was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was the first Persian poet to depict the Indian environment, praising India's land, languages and people (Nuh Sipihr). Amir Hasan, Kalim and Faizi came after or were less known for this.

116.s: Amir Khusrau, the “Parrot of India,” was born at-
116.x: Amir Khusrau was born at Patiyali (1253), near Etah (now Kasganj district), Uttar Pradesh.

116.s: Who among the following is called the ‘Sadi of India’?
116.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi (Sijzi), Khusrau's friend and compiler of Fawaid-ul-Fuad, is called the 'Sadi of India' for his ghazals. Khusrau is the 'Tuti-i-Hind'.

116.s: Which of the following is not associated with the Bhakti Movement?
116.x: Amir Khusrau was a Sufi poet (disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya), not a Bhakti saint. Vallabhacharya, Chaitanya and Guru Nanak belong to the Bhakti movement.

116.s: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of Hindi Khari Boli?
116.x: Amir Khusrau is called the father of Khari Boli for his Hindavi riddles and verses. Jayasi wrote in Awadhi; Kabir and Rahim came later.

116.s: Amir Khusrau played a pioneer role in the development of
116.x: Amir Khusrau's Hindavi verses, riddles and mukris are the earliest Khari Boli, from which Hindi and Urdu grew. Braj, Awadhi and Bhojpuri developed separately.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was court poet of
116.x: Amir Khusrau was chiefly associated with the court of Alauddin Khalji, who gave him the title Tuti-i-Hind. He died in 1325 (Firoz and Ibrahim Lodi came later; Muhammad bin Tughluq's reign had barely begun).

116.s: Who among the following called himself the ‘parrot of India’?
116.x: Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) was Amir Khusrau's title. Amir Hasan was 'Sadi of India'; Qutban and Usman were Sufi premakhyan poets.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was a –
116.x: Amir Khusrau was poet, historian (Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughluqnama) and musician (qawwali, tarana, sitar tradition).

116.s: “Every pearl in the Royal crown is the crystallised drops of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasants” … Who made this statement?
116.x: The line 'every pearl in the royal crown is the crystallised drop of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasant' is attributed to Amir Khusrau. Al-Biruni, Ibn Battuta and Badauni are not credited with it.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was born in
116.x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): Patiyali, Amir Khusrau's birthplace, is in Kasganj district (carved out of Etah in 2008), still so in Nov 2026. (When this paper was set, the answer was: Etah.) Source: https://kasganj.nic.in/
Patiyali was part of Etah district — now in Kasganj district, carved out of Etah in 2008 (kasganj.nic.in)
Khusrau was born at Patiyali, then in Etah district (now Kasganj district, UP). Agra, Barabanki and Etawah are wrong.

116.s: Who among the following witnessed the reign of Seven Sultans of Delhi?
116.x:
Most books and keys: Amir Khusrau (court poet of seven Sultans). Strictly, Nizamuddin Auliya (1238-1325) also lived under seven or more Sultans; PMF lists five Sultans Khusrau served.
Amir Khusrau (1253-1325) lived through and served the courts of about seven Delhi Sultans, from Balban's son to Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. Nizamuddin Auliya also lived through these reigns but kept away from all courts.

116.s: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Sufi saint?
116.x: Khusrau was a devoted disciple of the Chishti saint Nizamuddin Auliya.

116.s: Amir Khusrau, who called himself 'Tuti-i-Hind', is regarded as the father of which language form?
116.x: Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli; his Hindavi verses grew into Rekhta/Urdu.

116.s: Which poet of the Delhi Sultanate was called 'Sadi-i-Hind' for his ghazals?
116.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi was called the Sadi of India; Khusrau was the Parrot of India.

116.s: 'Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi' was written by
116.x: Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi on Firoz Tughlaq's reign (Barani wrote the other of the same name). Yahya Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Minhaj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Isami the Futuh-us-Salatin.

116.s: Who is the author of "Tarikh-i-Firujshahi"?
116.x:
Two options are right: both Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi. Most keys give Barani; Afif (option a) is equally correct strictly.
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is best known as Ziauddin Barani's history (to 1357); Shams Siraj Afif wrote a second work of the same title. Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin and Yazdi wrote Zafarnama (Timur), so the printed key 'Isami' is wrong.

116.s:

II. Prithviraj – Raso

III. Kitab-ul-hind

IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri

116.x: Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030) → Prithviraj Raso (traditionally late 12th c.) → Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260) → Fatawa-i-Jahandari (Barani, c. 1358). So III, II, IV, I.

2. He wrote his works under the patronage of Alauddin Khalji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Barani wrote his Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari under Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

116.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote both; the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi covers Balban to early Firoz.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Amir Khusrau?
116.x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is Barani's work on political theory.

116.s:

116.s: Which of the following musical instruments is not of Indo-Islamic origin?
116.x:
The MPPSC 2013 official key and many books give the Shehnai. PMF credits Amir Khusrau with the Sarangi; authorities are split.
The sarangi is an indigenous Indian bowed instrument; the sitar and sarod owe their origin to Persian influence and the tabla is credited to the Indo-Islamic tradition. So the sarangi is not of Indo-Islamic origin.

116.s: ‘Tabla’ was introduced by :
116.x: The tabla is traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau. Tansen and Baiju Bawra were singers; Adil Shah is unrelated.

116.s: Musical instrument sitar is the combination of:
116.x: The sitar, traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau, combines the Indian veena and the Persian tambura (setar).

116.s: Which among the following musical instruments is the finest example of Hindu-Muslim harmony in musical instruments?
116.x: The sitar, joining the Indian veena with the Iranian tambura, is the classic symbol of Hindu-Muslim musical synthesis. The veena, dholak and sarangi are indigenous.

116.s: The qaul, tarana and raga Aiman (Yaman) are credited to:
116.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with the qaul, tarana and raga Aiman, and traditionally with the tabla.

116.s: Sama and qawwali were popularised by the khanqahs of the:
116.x: The Chishti khanqahs popularised sama; the Suhrawardis were more orthodox.

116.s: The earliest Persian treatise on Indian music is:
116.x: Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise; Rag Vibodh is Somanatha's, Man Kautuhal is linked to Raja Man Singh Tomar.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT a treatise on music?
116.x: Tuzuk-i-Babri is Babur's memoir; the others are works on music.
