116.x: Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh on Alauddin Khalji's conquests. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, Minhaj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Barani the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

116.s: Who among the following was the author of Tarikh-i-Alai, which contains the details of the first few years of Sultan Alauddin Khilji?
116.x: Tarikh-i-Alai is the other name of Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh, on Alauddin's early years and conquests. Barani and Afif wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi; Yahya the Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi.

116.s:
Which of the following texts are written by Amir Khusrau ?
1. Khazain-ul-Futuh
2. Nuh Siphir
3. Miftah-ul-Futuh
4. Qiraan-us-Sadain
116.x: All four – Khazain-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Miftah-ul-Futuh and Qiran-us-Sadain – are Amir Khusrau's works.

116.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work of Amir Khusrau)
a. Miftah-ul-Futuh
b. Qiran-us-Sadain
c. Nuh Sipihr
d. Tughluqnama
List II (Subject)
i. Meeting of Bughra Khan and his son Kaiqubad
ii. Rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq
iii. Jalaluddin Khalji's campaigns
iv. Mubarak Shah's reign and praise of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
116.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. All four are works of Amir Khusrau: Miftah-ul-Futuh - Jalaluddin's campaigns; Qiran-us-Sadain - meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad; Nuh Sipihr - Mubarak Shah's reign; Tughluqnama - rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Amir Khusrau?
116.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Barani (and Afif); the other three are Amir Khusrau's.

116.s: Amir Khusrau's Ashiqa deals with the romance of Khizr Khan and:
116.x: Ashiqa is the romance of Khizr Khan and Deval Rani; Kamala Devi was Deval Rani's mother.

116.s: Who of the following has given a detailed description of the postal system found during the Sultanate period?
116.x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla describes the Sultanate postal system: horse post (ulaq) and foot runners (dawa) every third of a mile. Barani, Khusrau and Firoz Shah's own memoir do not give this account.

116.s: Medieval traveller and writer Ibn Batuta belonged to which country?
116.x: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveller, born at Tangiers (1304); he lived in India 1333-1347 under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

116.s: Which one of the following travelogues has given an insight on the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq?
o: Francois Bernier’s Travels in the Mogul Empire
116.x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla, written after his stay of 1333-1347, describes the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq, who made him Qazi of Delhi. Bernier, Manucci and Tavernier wrote on the Mughals.

116.s: In which language did Ibn Battuta write his travel account, the Rihla?
116.x: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta wrote the Rihla in Arabic.

116.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as his envoy in 1342 to:
116.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and in 1342 sent him as envoy to China.

116.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Traveller)
a. Al-Biruni
b. Marco Polo
c. Abdur Razzaq
d. Ibn Battuta
List II (Origin)
i. Morocco
ii. Venice
iii. Khwarizm (Uzbekistan)
iv. Persia - envoy of Shah Rukh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
116.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i. Al-Biruni came from Khwarizm with Mahmud of Ghazni; Marco Polo was from Venice (Motupalli, 1292); Abdur Razzaq was Shah Rukh's Persian envoy to Deva Raya II (1443); Ibn Battuta was from Morocco.

116.s: Who among the following had translated Chintamani Bhatt’s Sanskrit text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it the title ‘Tutinama’?
116.x: Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi translated Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati into Persian as Tutinama (14th c.). Khusrau, Abdur Razzak and al-Umari did not.

116.s: The term ‘Apabhramsa’ was used in medieval Sanskrit text to denote
o: early forms of some of the modern Indian language.
116.x: Apabhramsa ('corrupt speech') denotes the late Prakrit dialects that were the early forms of modern Indian languages (Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati…).

116.s: Which was the official language in the Delhi Sultanate?
116.x: Persian (Arabicised Persian mixed with Turkish) was the language of administration of the Delhi Sultanate. Arabic was the religious language; Urdu developed later in camps and bazaars.

116.s: Who translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit?
116.x: Shay Akbar made the reverse translation of Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit.

116.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work)
a. Tutinama
b. Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi
c. Kalila wa Dimna
d. Razmnama
List II (Description)
i. Persian Panchatantra
ii. Persian Mahabharata (Mughal)
iii. Based on Sanskrit texts of the Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot) temple
iv. Persian version of Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
116.x: Correct code: a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii. Tutinama (Nakhshabi) is from the Suka Saptati; Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi from the Jwalamukhi texts under Firoz Tughlaq; Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian Panchatantra; the Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata.

116.s: The official (court) language of the Delhi Sultanate was:
116.x: Persian was the language of administration; Arabic was the language of religion and theology.

116.s: The form of Hindavi/Urdu that developed in the Deccan is known as:
116.x: Dakhni (Deccani) Urdu developed under the Bahmani and the Deccan Sultanates.

116.s: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi was refused an audience by Nizamuddin Auliya?
116.x:
Most books and keys: Alauddin Khalji ('two doors' reply). The saint also avoided Jalaluddin Khalji, who tried to visit through Amir Khusrau.
Nizamuddin Auliya never went to court. When Alauddin Khalji sought a meeting, he replied that his house had two doors, and if the Sultan came in by one he would leave by the other. Jalaluddin's earlier attempt (via Khusrau) also failed; Ghiyasuddin quarrelled with him ('Hanuz Dilli dur ast').

116.s: The Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the record of the conversations of Nizamuddin Auliya, was compiled by:
116.x: Amir Hasan Sijzi recorded Nizamuddin Auliya's conversations in the Fawaid-ul-Fuad.

116.s: Which of the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya is correct?
o: He never visited the royal court though he lived through several reigns.
His conversations were recorded by Ziauddin Barani.
He belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
116.x: He was a Chishti saint buried in Delhi; Amir Hasan Sijzi recorded his talks.

116.s: Chandayan (1379), an early Awadhi premakhyan (Sufi romance), was written by:
116.x: Mulla Daud wrote Chandayan; Qutban wrote Mrigavati and Jayasi the Padmavat.

116.s: The Sufi romance Padmavat was written by:
116.x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat in Awadhi in the 16th century.

116.s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana render into Telugu?
116.x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

116.s: Errana of the Reddi period completed which parva of the Mahabharata?
116.x: Errana completed the Aranya Parva.

116.s: Who is the author of Sringara Naishadham?
116.x: Srinatha of the Reddi period wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kasi Khandam.

116.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Poet)
a. Tikkana
b. Palkuriki Somanatha
c. Gona Budda Reddy
d. Srinatha
List II (Work)
i. Kasi Khandam
ii. Ranganatha Ramayanam
iii. Nirvachanottara Ramayanam
iv. Basava Puranam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
116.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. Tikkana - Nirvachanottara Ramayanam (and 15 parvas of the Mahabharata); Palkuriki Somanatha - Basava Puranam; Gona Budda Reddy - Ranganatha Ramayanam; Srinatha - Kasi Khandam.

116.s: Addanki Gangadhara, the first to dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim ruler, dedicated 'Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam' to:
116.x: It was dedicated to Ibrahim Qutb Shah (Malki Bharama), a patron of Telugu.

116.s:
Match the following authors with their works :
a. Al-Biruni
b. Minhaj-us-Siraj
c. Ziauddin Barani
d. Ibn Battuta
I. Tariqh-i-Firoz Shahi
II. Tahqiq-i-Hind
III. The Rihla
IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
116.src: APPSC Group-I Preliminary (Screening Test) 2023, Notification 28/2022, Paper I – General Studies (GS/1G/100), held 08-01-2023 · Q28
116.x: Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind, Minhaj-us-Siraj Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Ziauddin Barani Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Ibn Battuta the Rihla.

117.s: Who shifted the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom from Gulbarga to Bidar?
117.x: Ahmad Shah I (Wali, 1422-36) annexed Warangal and moved the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. Firoz Shah was his predecessor; Muhammad Shah III's era is Mahmud Gawan's.

117.s: Who founded the Bahmani Empire?
117.x: Hasan Gangu (Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah) founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347 with Gulbarga as capital. Yusuf Adil Khan founded Bijapur; Prolaya Nayaka was a Musunuri chief.

117.s: The bone of contention between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagar kingdom was
117.x: The Raichur doab between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra was the chief bone of contention between the Bahmanis and Vijayanagara.

117.s: Who among the following founded the Bahmani kingdom in the Deccan in the 14th century A.D.?
117.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), a Tughlaq officer, revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347.

117.s: Who among the following shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
117.x: Ahmad Shah I (Wali, 1422-36) annexed Warangal and moved the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. Firoz Shah was his predecessor; Muhammad Shah III's era is Mahmud Gawan's.

117.s: In which war was gunpowder used for the first time in India?
117.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
117.x: The earliest recorded use of gunpowder weapons in India is by the Bahmani Sultan Muhammad Shah I against Vijayanagara (Bukka I), c. 1366-68 (Mudgal/Adoni). The Kakatiyas and Warangal were gone by then; Babur's Panipat (1526) only popularised field artillery.

117.s: Who founded the Bahmani Empire?
117.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

117.s:
The Bahmani kingdom was founded in
A) Hari
B) Prabhu
117.x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347; 1336 is Vijayanagara, 1325 MBT's accession.

117.s: ____ established the Bahamani Kingdom after revolting against the Delhi Sultanate.
117.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
117.x: Ala-ud-din Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu, Zafar Khan), a Tughlaq officer, revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347; Alauddin Khilji was a Delhi Sultan and Mujahid Shah a later Bahmani. (Moved to the Bahmani row.)

117.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, was renamed Hasanabad.
2. Ahmad Shah I shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Both statements are correct: Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, was renamed Hasanabad, and Ahmad Shah I moved the capital to Bidar.

117.s: The Bahmani Sultanate, the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan, was founded in 1347 by:
117.x: Hasan Gangu founded it at Gulbarga as Alauddin Bahman Shah.

117.s: Which of the following statements about the Bahmani Sultanate is correct?
o: It was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan
Alauddin Bahman Shah built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid
Firuz Shah built an observatory near Bidar
117.x: Firuz Shah's observatory was near Daulatabad, the kingdom ended in 1527, and the Gulbarga mosque was built under Muhammad Shah I.

117.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Babur was the first to use gunpowder weapons in India, at Panipat in 1526.
Reason (R): The Bahmanis under Muhammad Shah I used firearms against Vijayanagara around 1366-68.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
117.x: A is false: the first recorded use of firearms in India was by the Bahmanis (Muhammad Shah I) against Vijayanagara c. 1366-68; Babur only popularised field artillery. R is true.

117.s: The Raichur Doab, the chief bone of contention between the Bahmanis and Vijayanagara, lay between the rivers:
117.x: The Raichur Doab is the land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.

117.s: Bidriware, a blackened zinc alloy inlaid with silver, developed under the Bahmani rulers at:
117.x: Bidriware takes its name from Bidar, the later Bahmani capital.

117.s: Which one of the following places was known as ‘Shiraz of East’ during the regime of Sharqi Rulers?
117.x: Jaunpur, a great centre of learning under the Sharqis (Ibrahim Shah), was called the 'Shiraz of the East / Shiraz-i-Hind'.

117.s: Who was the last ruler of 'Jaunpur' state?
117.x: Hussain Shah Sharqi was the last ruler of Jaunpur; Bahlul Lodi took the kingdom in 1479.

117.s: Which one of the following places was called “Shiraz of India”?
117.x: Jaunpur, a great centre of learning under the Sharqis, was called 'Shiraz-i-Hind'.

117.s: The capital of Sharqi dynasty during 15th-16th century AD was?
117.x: Jaunpur was the Sharqi capital (1394-1479), founded as a kingdom by Malik Sarwar.

117.s: The main achievement of Bahlul Lodi was victory over which among the following regions?
117.x: Bahlul Lodi's chief achievement was the conquest of the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur (1479) from Hussain Shah Sharqi.

117.s: Who among the following was the last ruler of Sharqi dynasty?
117.x: Hussain Shah Sharqi was the last Sharqi ruler, defeated by Bahlul Lodi in 1479.

117.s: Who had established Jaunpur?
117.x: Firoz Shah Tughluq founded Jaunpur and named it after his cousin Muhammad bin Tughluq (Jauna Khan). Ibrahim Shah Sharqi only made it a cultural centre.

117.s: Who among the following ordered the construction of Atala mosque in Jaunpur?
117.x: The Atala Masjid at Jaunpur was begun under Firoz Tughlaq (1376) and completed by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi (1408). Bibi Raje built the Lal Darwaza mosque.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about music at the Sharqi court of Jaunpur:
1. The Sharqi court patronised Khyal.
2. The Sufi musician Pir Bodhan flourished under Husain Shah Sharqi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Both statements are correct: the Sharqi court patronised Khyal, and Pir Bodhan flourished under Husain Shah Sharqi.
117.tq: Music = Husain Shah Sharqi; buildings = Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.

117.s: Which of the following statements about the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur is correct?
o: Jaunpur was founded by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
The Atala Mosque was built by Bibi Raje.
The Lal Darwaza Mosque was built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.
Malik Sarwar made Jaunpur independent in 1394.
117.x: Malik Sarwar (Malik-us-Sharq) made it independent in 1394; Firoz Tughlaq founded Jaunpur; Ibrahim Shah built the Atala Mosque and Bibi Raje the Lal Darwaza.

117.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Jaunpur was called the 'Shiraz of India'.
Reason (R): Jaunpur was at its height as a centre of learning under Hussain Shah Sharqi.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
117.x: A is true: Jaunpur was the 'Shiraz-i-Hind' as a great centre of learning. R is false: its height was under Ibrahim Shah Sharqi (1402-40); Hussain Shah Sharqi was the last ruler, conquered by Bahlul Lodi (1479).

117.s:
Consider the following statements: The striking feature of the Jama Masjid in Kashmir completed by Zain-ul-Abidin include(s):
I. turret
II. similarity with Buddhist pagodas
III. Persian style
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin's Jama Masjid at Srinagar combines turrets, pagoda-like roofs recalling Buddhist architecture, and Persian style. So I, II and III.

117.s: Which among the following ruler abolished Jizya for first time?
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir (1420-70) abolished jizya more than a century before Akbar (1564); he also banned cow slaughter.

117.s: Ruler of Kashmir who was also known as “Akbar of Kashmir’ was-
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin (Bud Shah) is called the 'Akbar of Kashmir' for his tolerance. Sikandar was 'Butshikan'; Shamsuddin founded the Shah Mir line.

117.s: What was the original name of ruler of Kashmir Zainul-Abidin?
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin's original name was Shahi Khan; he succeeded his brother Ali Shah in 1420.

117.s: Which Sultan was reputed to be 'Akbar of Kashmir?
117.x: Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Bud Shah, 1420-70) was the 'Akbar of Kashmir'. Sikandar was 'Butshikan'.

117.s: The Sultan of Kashmir known as 'Butshikan' (idol breaker) was:
117.x: Sikandar (1389–1413) was called Butshikan and imposed jizya; Zain-ul-Abidin was tolerant.

117.s: Jonaraja continued Kalhana's Rajatarangini under the patronage of:
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin had the Rajatarangini translated into Persian and patronised Jonaraja.

117.s: Which of the following rulers got the Jantar Mahal of Mandu constructed?
117.x:
'Jantar Mahal' in the stem is a misprint for Jahaz Mahal. Most sources credit Ghiyasuddin Khalji (not offered); among the options only Mahmud Shah Khalji, his father, in whose reign it was begun, fits. The printed key 'Alauddin Khilji' is wrong.
The Jahaz (ship) Mahal of Mandu is a Khalji-Malwa palace: begun in Sultan Mahmud Shah Khalji's reign (1436-69) and completed/used by his son Ghiyasuddin Khalji. Alauddin Khalji (Delhi), Bhoj Parmar and Hoshang Shah did not build it.

117.s: Who among the following established independent Muslim rule in Malwa?
117.x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri, Firoz Tughlaq's governor, made Malwa independent in 1401 with Dhar as capital. His son Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu.

117.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Mandu is in Dhar district.

II. Hindola Mahal is in Mandu.
Select the correct answer on the basis of above statements.
117.x: Mandu lies in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, and the Hindola Mahal (swinging palace, sloping walls) is at Mandu. Both statements are true.

117.s: The ‘Jahaj-Mahal’ of Mandu was built by whom?
117.x: The Jahaz Mahal at Mandu, between the Kapur and Munj tanks, is credited to Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khalji of Malwa (1469-1500), for his harem.

117.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Ruler of Malwa)
a. Hoshang Shah
b. Mahmud Khalji
c. Ghiyasuddin Khalji
d. Baz Bahadur
List II (Association)
i. Jahaz Mahal and Hindola Mahal
ii. India's first marble tomb
iii. Romance with Rupmati
iv. Completed the Jami Masjid, Mandu; Ashrafi Mahal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
117.x: Correct code: a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii. Hoshang Shah's tomb is India's first marble tomb; Mahmud Khalji completed the Jami Masjid and built the Ashrafi Mahal; Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Jahaz and Hindola Mahals; Baz Bahadur, the last Sultan, is linked with Rupmati.

117.s: Hoshang Shah of Malwa shifted his capital from Dhar to:
117.x: Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu, home of the Hindola Mahal and Jahaz Mahal.

117.s: Who among the following rulers of medieval Gujarat surrendered Diu to Portuguese?
117.x: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, pressed by Humayun, gave Diu to the Portuguese (Treaty of Bassein 1534 / Diu 1535); he was killed by them in 1537. Mahmud Begarha fought the Portuguese with Egypt and never surrendered Diu.

117.s: Which among the following Sultan of Gujarat was killed by the Portuguese on board the ship when making a deal with them?
117.x: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat (1526-37) was killed (drowned) by the Portuguese at Diu in 1537 while negotiating on board their ship.

117.s:
Which statements is/are correct regarding the book 'Mirat-e-Sikandari'?
1. There is a description of the happiness and prosperity of the Kingdom of Sultan Mahmud Begada of Gujarat.
2. There is a description of proper arrangements for the security of trade routes.
Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code -
117.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari (Sikandar bin Muhammad) describes the prosperity of Mahmud Begarha's Gujarat and the security of its roads for traders. Both statements are correct.

117.s: The city of Ahmedabad on the Sabarmati was founded in 1411 by:
117.x: Ahmad Shah I founded Ahmedabad in 1411; Zafar Khan (Muzaffar Shah I) founded the Gujarat Sultanate in 1407.

117.s: Which Gujarat sultan captured Girnar and Champaner?
117.x: Mahmud Begarha took Girnar and Champaner and joined Egypt against the Portuguese.

117.s:
Match list-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists –
List-I (Book)
A. Mirat-e-Sikandari
B. Burhan-e-Masir
C. Riyaz-us-Salatin
D. Riyaz-ul-Insha
List-II (Context)
(1) History of Bengal
(2) History of Bahmani's Ahmad Nagar
(3) Collection of Mahmood Gawan's letters
(4) Victory of Gujarat Code –
117.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari – Gujarat (4); Burhan-i-Maasir – Bahmanis and Nizam Shahs of Ahmadnagar (2); Riyaz-us-Salatin – Bengal (1); Riyaz-ul-Insha – Mahmud Gawan's letters (3).

117.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Chronicle)
a. Mirat-i-Sikandari
b. Burhan-i-Maasir
c. Riyaz-us-Salatin
d. Riyaz-ul-Insha
List II (Subject)
i. Bahmanis and Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar
ii. Bengal
iii. Letters of Mahmud Gawan
iv. Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
117.x: Correct code: a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii. Mirat-i-Sikandari is on Gujarat (not Bengal); Burhan-i-Maasir on the Bahmanis and Nizam Shahis; Riyaz-us-Salatin on Bengal; Riyaz-ul-Insha holds Mahmud Gawan's letters.

117.s: Akbar annexed Bengal in the year:
117.x: Bengal was annexed in 1576; Gujarat in 1572-73.

117.s: Jaunpur was conquered from the Sharqis by:
117.x: Bahlul Lodi took Jaunpur around 1479.

117.s: Which one among the following was not a reform measure carried out by Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani Kingdom?
o: The Kingdom was divided into eight provinces or Tarafs.
Nobles were paid salaries and were asked to maintain contingents of horses.
A tract of land, Khalisa, was set apart for the expenses of the Tarafdar.
Lands were measured and land taxes were fixed on that basis.
117.x: Gawan set apart a khalisa tract in every province for the expenses of the Sultan, not of the tarafdar. Dividing the kingdom into eight tarafs, fixing nobles' salaries and measuring land were his reforms.

117.s: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar was built on which model?
117.x: The three-storeyed, tile-decorated madrasa followed a Persian (Herat/Samarkand) model; the Cordoba comparison belongs to the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
xa: **Bidriware** of Bidar: **14th century** under the Bahmanis; GI tag **2006**.
Mahmud Gawan's letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud Gawan:
1. He took Goa in 1472.
2. His letters are collected in the Riyaz-us-Salatin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: his letters are collected in the Riyaz-ul-Insha; the Riyaz-us-Salatin is a history of Bengal.

117.s: Mahmud Gawan was the wazir of which Bahmani Sultan?
117.x: Mahmud Gawan served Muhammad Shah III; he divided the four tarafs into eight provinces.

117.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Mahmud Gawan merged the eight tarafs into four provinces.
Mahmud Gawan crushed the Telangana revolts with Reddi help.
Mahmud Gawan was a leader of the Dakhni (local) faction.
Mahmud Gawan divided the four tarafs of the Bahmani kingdom into eight provinces.
117.x: Gawan, an Afaqi (Persian) noble, split the four tarafs into eight and used Velama help in Telangana.

117.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Bahmani kingdom broke up after the execution of Mahmud Gawan in 1481.
Reason (R): Mahmud Gawan was framed by rival nobles.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
117.x: Both are true, but R explains why Gawan was executed, not why the kingdom broke up; the break-up followed the loss of the minister under whom the kingdom had been at its height.

117.s: Who was conferred the title of ‘Gunraj Khan’?
117.x: Maladhar Basu, author of Sri Krishna Vijaya (Bengali Bhagavata), received the title 'Gunaraj Khan' from the Bengal Sultan (Rukunuddin Barbak Shah).

121.s: What was the administrative unit of the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: The question means the administrative system of the empire: the Amaranayaka (Amara-Nayankara) system, in which military governors (Nayakas) held amarams for salary and army expenses.

121.s: The Nayakas in the Vijayanagar empire were
o: Priests of large and powerful temples.
121.x: Nayakas (amaranayakas) were military chiefs who held and administered territories (amarams) in lieu of salary - not ministers, priests or ordinary cavalry.

121.s: Who were polygars of South India?
121.x: Polygars (Palegars) were amara-nayakas who administered territories and owed military service - territorial administrative and military governors; they were only forerunners of the zamindars.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagar Empire.

I. Vijaynagar was noted for its markets dealing in spices, textiles and precious stones.

II. Krishnadeva Raya’s rule was characterised by the strain within the imperial structure.

III. The amara-nayakas were military commanders who were given territories to be governed by the Rayas.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
121.x: I and III: Vijayanagara's markets dealt in spices, textiles and precious stones, and the amara-nayakas were military commanders given territories by the Rayas. II is wrong – Krishnadeva Raya's reign was one of expansion and consolidation; strain came after him (NCERT).

121.s: What was the land assigned by the Vijayanagara king to military chiefs in lieu of cash salaries called?
121.x: Amaram was land granted to military chiefs, who were known as Amaranayakas, Nayaks, Palaiyagars or Poligars. The grant substituted for direct cash payment to the chiefs.
121.tq: Use the exact administrative term rather than a similar land-revenue term.
xs: Land granted to military chiefs instead of cash salaries was the **Amaram** — option **(2)**.
Holders were **Amaranayakas / Nayakas / Poligars** (also Palaiyagars), titled **Mahamandaleshwara**.
**Manyam** = tax-free lands of the **Ayagars**; **Jagir** belongs to the **Mughal** mansabdari.
xa: They paid a fixed **annual tribute (kist / kappam)**.
Krishnadevaraya had about **200 nayankaras** (Nuniz).
**Amara gramalu** collected **Durgadayam** for the army.

121.s: What was the principal political outcome of the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system after 1565?
o: The replacement of Nayakas by hereditary village accountants and headmen under the Ayagar system
The conversion of all amarams into Mughal jagirs held by mansabdars from Delhi
The complete abolition of regional chieftaincies and direct rule from Penukonda and Chandragiri
The emergence of semi-independent and later independent Nayaka states such as Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi
121.x: After 1565, semi-independent Nayaka kingdoms emerged and some became independent, including those of Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.
121.tq: Test the result of the system through its named regional examples.
xs: After **1565**, **semi-independent** and then **independent Nayaka states** arose — **Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi** — option **(4)**.
The Nayankara gave a huge army **cheaply** but bred kingdoms that **broke away after Talikota**.
xa: Amara-nayakas also became **Palegars (Poligars)**, forerunners of the **zamindars**.
The Mughal mansabdari, by contrast, was **non-hereditary** and centrally controlled.

121.s: Who is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system?
121.x: Prataparudra II is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system. The Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system grew out of the Kakatiya system.
121.tq: Use the originator–system association and avoid substituting a later ruler.
xs: The Kakatiya Nayankara originated with **Prataparudra II** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025** key).
**Akbar** is linked to the Mughal **mansabdari**; the Vijayanagara system **grew out of** the Kakatiya one (CDX).
xa: Kakatiya nayakas held **a fort and a quarter of the land** and paid a fixed sum.
⚠ Kakatiya **75/77** vs Vijayanagara about **200**.

121.s: From whom did the Palegars or Poligars primarily originate?
121.x: The Amara-nayakas became the Palegars or Poligars when central authority weakened after the Battle of Talikota.
121.tq: Trace the origin of the later institution to its Vijayanagara military-administrative predecessor.
xs: The Palegars (Poligars) grew out of the **Amara-nayakas** — option **(3)**.
After **Talikota (1565)** weakened central authority, they became **hereditary** local rulers.
xa: They were **forerunners of the zamindars**.
In **Rayalaseema** they were suppressed by **Thomas Munro** with **Campbell**.
⚠ **Ayagars** were village functionaries; **Parupatyagars** were Nadu revenue officials.

121.s: The Palegars (Poligars), who became hereditary local rulers after Talikota, are regarded as the forerunners of whom?
121.x: The Palegars are regarded as forerunners of the zamindars; Ryotwari was introduced by Munro after suppressing them.
xa: Palegars arose from the **Amara-nayakas**.
Rayalaseema (the **Ceded Districts**) had a dense network of fortified poligar chiefs.

121.s: Which British officer, assisted by Campbell, crushed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
121.x: Thomas Munro, with his officer Campbell, crushed the Palegars and then introduced the Ryotwari system.

121.s: Police rights were sometimes sold in the Vijayanagara Empire. What was this called?
121.x: Under Padikaval, police rights were sold to individuals; Athavana was revenue and Kandachara the military department.

121.s: In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
121.x: The Pradvivaka was the chief judicial adviser to the king, interpreting Dharmashastra; not revenue, espionage or military.

121.s: Who policed the village under the Vijayanagara Kavali system?
121.x: The Talari policed the village, the Peta Kavalidaru the towns and the Kavali Daru the Sthala.
xa: The Talari had **no salary** and collected **Merulu** at harvest.
Police watched communities suspected of receiving stolen goods, e.g. the **Panchanam**.

121.s: Who policed the Sthala level under the Kavali system?
121.x: Talari policed the village, Kavali Daru the sthala and Peta Kavalidaru the towns.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara Kavali system:

2. The Kavali Daru policed the towns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Talari policed the village. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kavali Daru policed the sthala; the towns were under the Peta Kavalidaru.

121.s: In the Vijayanagara judicial system, civil cases were called:
121.x: Dhanodbhava cases were civil and Himsodbhava cases criminal; treason was punished with death.

121.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the king's position as supreme judge (with ministers like Timmarusu also trying cases) does not follow from which law book was authoritative.

121.s: While appointing 'Brahmins' as 'Karanams', Harihara I of the Vijayanagara Empire followed the appointment system of which of the following dynasties?

121.x: Harihara I appointed Brahmins as village Karanams on the Kakatiya pattern - the Sangama brothers had served the Kakatiya state, and Vijayanagara village administration (Ayagars, Karanam) continued the Kakatiya system.

121.s: Who was the repair and maintenance officer of forts in the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: The Parupatyagar, the king's officer of the nadu/sima, collected revenue and repaired and maintained forts. Gowda was a village/sthala head and Dandanayaka a commander.

121.s: The biggest administrative unit in the Vijayanagara Empire was
121.x: The Rajya or Mandala (province) was the largest unit, above Nadu, Sthala and Grama; Kottam and Kurram were smaller Chola-era units.

The village headman of the Vijayanagara empire is keyed as Gowda (Gauda), the Karnataka name of the Andhra Reddi; Chowdhary and Parupatyadar are wrong.

121.s: Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara provincial governors is correct?

They held office for life without transfer
121.x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

121.s: What title did the Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces hold?
121.x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

121.s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
121.x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

121.s: Who was the 'Kase' among the village artisans of the Vijayanagara period?
o: Potter or maker of clay pots
121.x: Kase was the mason or house-builder; Vadrangi was the carpenter, Kummari the potter and Chakali the washerman.
xa: **Kammari** = blacksmith; **Mangali** = barber.
There were **12 Ayagars** per village.

121.s: Who collected the grain gifts called 'Merulu' in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

121.s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

121.x: Saluva Narasimha ruled Chandragiri as governor; Penukonda became the capital only after Talikota.

121.s: Under the Ayagar system, each village had how many hereditary functionaries?
121.x: Each village had 12 hereditary Ayagars, among them the Kase (mason).

121.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Ayagar system?
o: They received a share of the village harvest
Ayagars were paid cash salaries by the state
121.x: Ayagars were paid through a harvest share and tax-free lands, not state salaries.

121.s: The Vijayanagara king, though supreme head of state, was expected to act within Dharma and in consultation with whom?
121.x: The king was supreme head, commander and fountain of justice, but acted within Dharma and with ministerial counsel.
xa: Burton Stein called Vijayanagara a **"segmentary state"**; Nilakanta Sastri a **"military administration"**.
The PM was the **Mahapradhana/Mahapradhani** (e.g. **Saluva Timmarusu**), heading the **pradhanis**.
As supreme judge the king sat in the **Dharmasana**.

121.s: Which historian characterised the Vijayanagara empire as a 'segmentary state'?
121.x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state, whereas Nilakanta Sastri described it as a military administration.
xa: The Nayankara gave a huge army cheaply but bred **Nayaka kingdoms** that broke away after **Talikota**.
The king was supreme head but bound by **Dharma** and ministers' counsel.

121.s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding forest tribes?
o: Crush them by force and destroy their forest strongholds
Expel them from the kingdom and clear their forests for farming
Win them over rather than merely crush them
Leave them entirely alone and avoid all contact with them
121.x: Amuktamalyada combines devotion with statecraft and advises winning over forest tribes rather than merely crushing them.
xa: "Political matters are discussed" in it (APPSC G2 **2003**).
Revenue maxim: the **bulk of revenue should go to the army**.

121.s: Which of the following is correctly stated regarding the contents of Amuktamalyada?
o: It refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns and gives political advice, but does not trace a genealogy from Bukka.
It is exclusively a manual on fort construction.
It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka but not Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns.
It contains no discussion of kingship or administration.
121.x: Amuktamalyada contains political maxims on rajaniti, kingship and administration and refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns, but it gives no genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2003).
121.tq: Discriminate between the work’s dynastic genealogy and the campaigns it does not record.

121.s: Who headed the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara?
121.x: The standing army was under the Dalavayi; Durga Dannayakas commanded forts.
xa: Nuniz put the standing army at about **50,000**.
The other wing: **Amara-nayaka levies** — **600,000** under Achyutaraya (Nuniz).

121.s: Who introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen, into the Vijayanagara military system?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen. Bukka I is associated with the first use of cannon by a Vijayanagara king.
121.tq: Separate the closely related military innovations of Bukka I and Saluva Narasimha.
xs: **Saluva Narasimha** introduced the **Samugaris** (gunmen) — option **(2)**.
**Bukka I** was the first to use **cannon**; **Devaraya II** and **Rama Raya** recruited **Muslim** troops.
xa: Firearms came with **Turkish** and **Portuguese** experts.
Horses came via **Goa, Honnavar, Bhatkal**.

121.s: What were the four types of forts in the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: The four types of forts were Giri (hill), Sthala (land), Jala (water) and Vana (forest) forts.
xa: Forts were under **Durga Dannayakas**.
Krishnadevaraya advised making **Brahmins** fort commanders.
The **Amara gramalu** collected **Durgadayam** for the army.

121.s: The first Vijayanagara king to use cannon was:
121.x: Bukka I is credited with the first use of cannon in Vijayanagara.

121.s: The standing army of Vijayanagara was commanded by the:
121.x: The Siddha (standing) army was under the Dalavayi and was paid every four months.

123.x: The Pemmasani Nayakas patronised the Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples.

123.s:
Match List I (temple) with List II (feature):
List I
a. Ontimitta Kodandarama
b. Yaganti Uma Maheswara
c. Srikalahasti

List II
i. Vayu linga

123.x: Ontimitta (Kadapa) - official Sri Rama Navami venue after 2014; Yaganti - the 'growing' Nandi; Srikalahasti - Vayu linga; Srisailam - four gateways. Hence a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

123.s: The mukha mandapam of the Mallikarjuna temple at Srisailam is credited to the Vijayanagara ruler:
123.x: Harihara II built the mukha mandapam at Srisailam.

123.s: The bronze statues of Krishnadevaraya with his queens Chinna Devi and Tirumala Devi are found at:
123.x: Krishnadevaraya's bronze statues with his queens stand in the Tirumala temple.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The great southern Rajagopuram of the Ekambaranatha temple at Kanchipuram was built by Krishnadevaraya in 1509.
Reason (R): The Ekambaranatha temple was founded by the Vijayanagara rulers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
123.x: A is true, but R is false: the Ekambaranatha temple is of Pallava origin; Krishnadevaraya only added the southern Rajagopuram.

123.s: The Indo-Saracenic style of architecture is depicted in one of the buildings of Vijayanagaram rulers. Name the Building?
123.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
123.x: The Lotus Mahal at Hampi, built by Krishnadevaraya 'in Indo-Arabic style', shows the Indo-Islamic (Indo-Saracenic) arches and domes. The Vitthala and Hazara Rama temples are Dravidian; Mahamandapa is a temple hall.

123.s: Who got the monumental Rayagopurams in front of the temples at Hampi, Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Sri Rangam, Tirupati etc constructed?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya built the Raya gopurams at Hampi, Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Srirangam, Tirupati and Kalahasti. Vidyaranya was a sage, Harihara the founder, Rajaraja a Chola.

123.s: Building 'Kalyana Mandapas' was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of
123.x: Kalyana mandapas for the divine marriage are a hallmark of Vijayanagara temples, with Raya gopurams. Chalukya, Chandela and Rashtrakuta temples do not have them.

123.s: Author of "Sangita Suryodayam"?
123.x: Sangita Suryodayam was written by Bandaru Lakshminarayana, court musician of Krishnadevaraya. Krishnadevaraya, Rama Raya and Ramabhadramba wrote other works.

123.s: Which musical instrument gained prominence during the Vijayanagara Empire?
123.x: The veena was the chief instrument of Vijayanagara court music - treatises such as Sangita Suryodaya and the Carnatic tradition of Vidyaranya's Sangita Sara centre on it. Mridangam, tambura and cymbals were accompaniments.

123.s: What is a separate goddess shrine in a Vijayanagara temple complex, as at Hazara Rama, called?
123.x: The Amman shrine is the separate goddess shrine, seen at the Hazara Rama temple.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Vijayanagara temple architecture?
o: Pillared corridors added to older temples
123.x: Vijayanagara temples are Dravidian in style; the curvilinear shikhara is a Nagara feature.

123.s: The ruins of Vijayanagara, the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, are at:
123.x: Hampi on the Tungabhadra is a World Heritage Site.

123.s: With which ruler are the Mahanavami Dibba and the Lotus (Padma) Mahal at Hampi associated?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya's building at Hampi included the Ugra Narasimha, Hanuman statue, monolithic Ganesha, Mahanavami Dibba and Lotus Mahal.
xa: He added Virupaksha's central hall and **eastern gopuram (1510)**.
He installed the **Bala Krishna** idol from **Udayagiri**.

123.s: Near which structure does the Queen's Bath (Maharani Snanavatika) at Hampi stand?
123.x: The Queen's Bath is near the Lotus Mahal, in the zenana area.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the secular structures of Hampi?
o: The Lotus Mahal shows Indo-Islamic influence
The Huzur Daftar is an Indo-Persian council chamber
The Mahanavami Dibba was built by Krishnadevaraya for Dasara
The Lotus Mahal is credited to Achyutaraya
123.x: The Lotus Mahal is credited to Krishnadevaraya, not Achyutaraya.

123.s: Sangita Suryodaya was written by a court musician of which Vijayanagara ruler?
123.x: Sangita Suryodaya was written by Lakshminarayana (Lakminatha), a court musician of Krishnadevaraya.
xa: The name is also spelt **Lakminatha** in the notes.
**Yakshaganam** entertained the court; **Tolu Bommalata** entertained the **rural people**.
**Veedhi Bhagavatham** was the forerunner of **Kuchipudi**.
123.fixed: author of Sangita Suryodaya is Bhandaru Lakshminarayana; 'Lakminatha' is a misspelling

123.s: In Vijayanagara temple architecture, the pillared hall meant for the divine marriage ceremony was the:
123.x: The kalyana mandapa was used for the celestial marriage of the deity.

123.s: The towering gateways of Vijayanagara temples that dwarfed the central shrine were called:
123.x: Raya gopurams were the huge gateway towers of the Vijayanagara style.

123.s:
Match List I (structure) with List II (description):
List I
a. Lotus Mahal
b. Huzur Daftar
c. Mahanavami Dibba
d. Raya gopurams
List II
i. Platform built by Krishnadevaraya for the Dasara festival
ii. Indo-Arabic style building, also called Chitrangi or Padma Mahal
iii. Towering gateways at Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram and Srirangam
iv. Indo-Persian council chamber with 40 pillars
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Lotus Mahal (Chitrangi / Padma Mahal) - Indo-Arabic style; Huzur Daftar - council chamber with 40 pillars; Mahanavami Dibba - Krishnadevaraya's Dasara platform; Raya gopurams - Krishnadevaraya's gateways at Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Srirangam. Hence a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Percy Brown described Vijayanagara architecture as the 'matured state of the Dravidian tradition'.
Reason (R): Vijayanagara temples carried the Dravida features of gopuras, vimanas and pillared mandapas to their most elaborate form.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
123.x: Both are true. R explains A: this elaboration of Dravida features is why Percy Brown called it the matured Dravidian state.

123.s: Inscriptions on Gutti Fort Walls in Andhra Pradesh -------- century?
123.x: The earliest inscriptions on the walls of Gooty (Gutti) fort date to the 7th century; a Bukka I record calls it the foremost of forts.

123.s: The inscriptions on the walls of Gooty fort in Andhra Pradesh date back to the ____ century.
123.x: The earliest inscriptions on the walls of Gooty (Gutti) fort date to the 7th century; a Bukka I record calls it the foremost of forts.

123.s: Which of the following is related to Penukonda fort?
123.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
123.x: Penukonda fort belongs to the Vijayanagara kingdom; it became the first Aravidu capital in 1570.

123.s: Which city was founded by Krishnadeva Raya?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya founded Nagalapura (Nagalapuram) near Hampi in honour of his mother Nagala Devi. Warangal, Udayagiri and Chandragiri were older.

123.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Udayagiri of Nellore?
o: Place where idols were looted by Mir Jumla
123.x: Udayagiri in Nellore was built by the Vijayanagara rulers, later taken by Golconda, and is associated with the Panchaloha cannon.
123.tq: Distinguish closely related forts by their unique identifying feature.
xs: **Udayagiri (Nellore)** holds the **Panchaloha cannon** — option **(4)**.
It was built by Vijayanagara and later taken by **Golconda**.
**Mir Jumla** looted **Gandikota**; the first Aravidu capital was **Penukonda**; **Gooty** was **Aliya Rama Raya's** base.
xa: ASI is conserving the **Udayagiri fort** (Apr **2026**).
The style spread in Andhra through courts at **Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Chandragiri, Vinukonda**.

123.s: Under which ruler was Chandragiri the Aravidu capital?
123.x: Chandragiri served as the Aravidu capital under Venkatapati Raya II.
123.tq: Use the ruler–capital association and distinguish it from Penukonda's earlier Aravidu role.
xs: Chandragiri was the Aravidu capital under **Venkatapati Raya II** — option **(3)**.
Its **fort and Raja Mahal** blend **Hindu** and **Indo-Saracenic** styles.
xa: Capital order after Talikota: **Penukonda (1570)** → **Chandragiri** → **Vellore (1600)**.
**Vellore** became the capital under **Venkatapati II** (**1600**).

123.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Aravidu capitals of the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Vellore was the first Aravidu capital
123.x: Penukonda (1570) was first, followed by Chandragiri and then Vellore (1600), so Vellore was the last, not the first.

123.s: Where is the Raja Mahal, a blend of Hindu and Indo-Saracenic styles?
123.x: The Chandragiri fort has the Raja Mahal blending Hindu and Indo-Saracenic styles.

123.s: Which was the first capital of the Aravidu dynasty after the battle of Talikota?
123.x: The Aravidus moved first to Penukonda (1570), then Chandragiri and later Vellore (1600).

123.s: The idols of Gandikota were looted in 1657 by:
123.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda general, took Gandikota and looted its idols.

123.x: Thimmamma Marrimanu near Kadiri (then Anantapur district) entered the Guinness Book in 1989 as the banyan with the largest canopy, spreading over about 5 acres and estimated at about 550 years old.

(Temple) — (Place)
123.src: APPSC Group-I Services Prelims (Screening Test) 2019, Notification No. 27/2018, Paper-I General Studies (GS/1G/100, Series A), held 26-05-2019 · Q3
123.x: The Virupaksha temple is at Hampi in Karnataka (another is at Pattadakal), not Thiruvananthapuram. The other three pairs are correct.

124.s: To the delight of the public, besides Yakshagana, what was the other form of art available for entertainment in rural Andhra under Vijayanagara rule?
124.x: Yakshaganam entertained the court and elites; the leather shadow-puppet play Tolu Bommalata was the chief entertainment of rural Andhra under Vijayanagara. Harikatha and Burrakatha became popular later.

124.s: 'Jakkula Purandhri' is a character of which of the following folk art?
124.x: Jakkula Purandhri is a stock character of the Yakshaganam, performed by the Jakkula community. Perini, Oggu Katha and puppetry have no such role.

124.s: In the entertainments of the Vijayanagara kings, apart from Yakshaganam, which art form entertained the common rural people of Andhra?
124.x: Yakshaganam entertained the court and elites; the leather shadow-puppet play Tolu Bommalata was the chief entertainment of rural Andhra under Vijayanagara. Harikatha and Burrakatha became popular later.

124.s: 'Lavani' Dance is from the state of
124.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
124.x: Lavani is the folk dance-song form of Maharashtra (with the dholki), often part of Tamasha folk theatre – a culture fact, not geography.

124.s: What role did folk performance traditions mainly play in the Andhra Movement?
o: Carry a distinct Telugu cultural consciousness to villages
Entertain the Qutb Shahi court and its Persian-speaking nobility
Replace written Telugu literature with oral tradition alone
Preserve classical Sanskrit ritual drama in temple settings
124.x: Folk performance was living proof of a distinct Telugu culture and helped carry that cultural identity to the villages during the Andhra Movement.
xa: The **Praja Natya Mandali** used folk plays for **socialist/communist ideals**.
Sunkara Satyanarayana's Burrakathas include **Alluri Sitaramaraju** and **Veeresalingam**.
AP plans an **annual Telugu Mahotsavam** to revive these forms.

124.s: Which statement about the Yakshaganam of Andhra is correct?
o: It is a shepherd ballad sung to the Oggu drum.
It is performed in Telugu with elaborate costumes and Puranic stories.
It is a solo philosophical discourse.
It is performed only in Sanskrit, without costumes.
124.x: Andhra Yakshaganam is performed in Telugu, uses elaborate costumes and presents epic or Puranic stories.
xa: **Sugreeva Vijayam** by **Kandukuri Rudra Kavi** is the **first published Yakshaganam in Telugu**.
**Koravanji** is the ancient precursor of Yakshagana.
Under Vijayanagara, Yakshaganam entertained **royal courts/elite**; under the Qutb Shahis it became **folk theatre**.

124.s: Which is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam?
124.x: Sugreeva Vijayam of Kandukuri Rudrakavi is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam.

124.s: The Telugu Yakshaganam was traditionally performed by the:
124.x: The Jakkula community performed Yakshaganam; Koravanji was its precursor.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Veedhi Natakam (Veedhi Bhagavatam), the street dance-drama of Andhra, is regarded as the forerunner of Kuchipudi.
Reason (R): Under the Qutb Shahis, Yakshaganam became folk theatre and Kuchipudi flourished.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
124.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: Kuchipudi's descent from the Veedhi Natakam is a matter of form; its flourishing under the Qutb Shahis is a later development.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about folk artists and their honours:
1. Adibhatla Narayana Dasu bears the title Burrakatha Pitamaha.
2. Sheikh Nazar bears the title Harikatha Pitamaha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is the Harikatha Pitamaha. Statement 2 is wrong: Sheikh Nazar is the Burrakatha Pitamaha.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about folk forms of Andhra Pradesh:
1. In June 2025, Tholu Bommalata and Burrakatha were flagged as close to extinction.
2. Lack of patronage and youth disinterest are causes of their decline.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
124.x: Both statements are correct: in June 2025 Tholu Bommalata and Burrakatha were flagged as near extinction, for lack of patronage and youth interest.

b. Shaik Nazar

124.x: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu - Harikatha (Pitamaha); Shaik Nazar - Burrakatha (Pitamaha, Padma Shri 1986); Dalavai Chalapathi Rao - leather puppetry (Padma Shri 2020); Siddhendra Yogi - founder of Kuchipudi. Hence a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

124.s: Dalavai Chalapathi Rao, who received the Padma Shri in 2020, is an exponent of which art form?
124.x: Dalavai Chalapathi Rao is a leather puppeteer (Tholu Bommalata) from Anantapur district.

125.x: Kondapalli toys (NTR district, GI) are carved from wood – the soft, light Tella Poniki.

125.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019

125.s: In which area did the 'Panchanam varu' (professional artisans) emerge as a group?
125.x: The Panchanam varu – the five artisan castes of blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter and sculptor – were an Andhra group; NextGen lists Panchanam among the castes of Kakatiya Andhra.

125.s: Which of the following items is recently registered as a geographical indication from Andhra Pradesh?
125.x:
The key printed for this paper is Udayagiri wooden cutlery (GI registered 2016-17), the most recent registration when the paper was set. Banganapalle mango and Bandar laddu were also registered as GIs in 2017; Tapeswaram Kaja has no GI tag.
Unkeyed: three options are right. Udayagiri wooden cutlery (27 April 2017), Banganapalle mango (2017) and Bandar Laddu (2017) were all registered as GIs; only Tapeswaram Kaja has no GI tag.

125.s: Farishkhani' and 'Ashunkhani' were two designs of Exhibition of 1851. of Eluru in Andhra Pradesh which became centre of attraction during London
125.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
125.x: Eluru's hand-knotted carpets in the Farishkhani and Ashunkhani designs drew attention at the London Exhibition of 1851; Eluru was the carpet centre of 19th-century Andhra.

125.s: Etikoppaka is known for
125.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
125.x: Etikoppaka (Anakapalli district) is known for GI-tagged lacquered wooden toys – a wooden craft, not stone carving, painting or handloom.

125.s: Which of the following is not registered as a Geographical Indication in India as per details available till November, 2016?
125.x: Bandar Laddu got its GI only in 2017, so it was not registered by November 2016; Tirupati Laddu (2009), Uppada Jamdani (2009) and Guntur Sannam chilli (2011) were.

125.s: The wood of which of the following trees is used to make the large plucked string instrument used in Carnatic classical music known as Bobbili Veena/ Saraswati Veena?
125.x: The Bobbili (Saraswati) Veena is carved from a single block of jackfruit wood.

125.s: ‘Kalamkari painting refers to’
o: a hand-painted cotton textile in South India.
a handmade drawing on bamboo handicrafts in North-East India.
a block-painted woollen cloth in Western Himalayan region of India.
a hand-painted decorative silk cloth in North-Western India.
125.x: Kalamkari is a hand-painted (or block-printed) cotton textile of South India – Srikalahasti and Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

125.s: Which of the following is NOT the Traditional culture of Andhra Pradesh?
125.x:
Official key (2022): bamboo work. Strictly, after 2014 Bidri, Cherial and Nirmal are Telangana crafts and bamboo work is an AP craft, so the question has no single right answer.
The official key is bamboo work, following the undivided-AP framing in which Bidri, Cherial scrolls and Nirmal paintings are AP crafts. Since 2014 those three belong to Telangana and bamboo work is practised in AP's Agency areas.

b) Wooden Cutlery 2.Udayagiri

125.x: Eluru – hand-knotted carpets, Udayagiri – wooden cutlery, Narasapur – crochet lace, Etikoppaka – lacquerware toys: 1-2-3-4.

125.s: Kalamkari in the form of painting base is practiced by artisans at?
125.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
125.x: Kalamkari has two styles: the Srikalahasti style is free-hand painting with a pen (kalam), while the Machilipatnam-Pedana style uses block printing. 'Painting base' therefore means Srikalahasti.

125.s: Which is the state nodal agency for handicrafts in Andhra Pradesh, selling under the name 'Lepakshi'?
o: A.P. State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society (APCO)
125.x: Lepakshi, run by the A.P. Handicrafts Development Corporation (APHDC), is the state handicrafts nodal agency.

125.s: Where was a 90-foot installation of Etikoppaka toys unveiled in August 2026?
o: Visakhapatnam Beach Road near the RK Beach
Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
Tirupati Airport at Renigunta in Tirupati district

125.s: Which of the following crafts belongs to Telangana and not Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: Nirmal paintings, Bidri and Cherial scrolls are Telangana crafts.

126.s: ____ was the adventurous ruler of Vijayanagara who followed the policy of playing one Sultan against another which eventually led to their joining hands with each other.
126.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
126.x: Aliya Rama Raya, regent of Sadasiva, played one Deccan Sultan against another until they united against him at Talikota in 1565.

126.s: Who was the king of Vijayanagara during the Rakshasa Tangadi (Tallikota) battle of 1565?
126.x: Sadasiva Raya was the king at Talikota (1565); Aliya Rama Raya was only his regent, and Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu line afterwards.

126.s: ............ The Vijayanagara Empire came to an end in the Battle of Talikota.
126.x: Vijayanagara's power ended at Talikota (Rakshasa Tangadi) in 1565.

126.s: Son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya?
126.x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and the regent who led Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565). Achyuta Raya was Krishnadevaraya's half-brother.

126.s: In which year did the Talikota war take place?
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought in January 1565 (23 January in most books).

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought in –
126.x: Talikota was fought in 1565; 1526 is the First Battle of Panipat and 1576 Haldighati.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought between
o: Vijayanagara and combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda.
126.x: Vijayanagara fought the combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda (with Bidar). The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up, so option 2 is wrong.

126.s: In January 1565, the Battle of Talikota was fought between-

127.x: Babur came from Farghana (Ferghana) in Central Asia, which he ruled from 1494; Khiva, Khorasan and Seistan were not his home.

127.x: The Mughals were Chagatai Turks (Timurids); Turkish was their mother tongue. 'Mongols' is the tempting option, but Babur looked down on the Mongols.

127.x: The Mughals were Chagatai Turks, named after Chagatai, Genghis Khan's second son – not Persians or Afghans.

127.x: Babur founded Mughal rule in India by defeating Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

127.x: Babur descended from Timur on his father's side and from Chingiz Khan on his mother's side.

128.tq: Use the distinctive architectural feature to distinguish the monument from other Sur structures.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** at **Sasaram** (Bihar) is an **octagonal tomb in a tank** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; the **Purana Qila** is in **Delhi**.
xa: Sher Shah rebuilt the **Purana Qila** (Dinpanah), begun by **Humayun**.
He built the **Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** inside it.
**Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb**, with a **double dome**.

128.s: Who was the architect of Humayun's Tomb?
128.x: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas designed Humayun's Tomb, built 1565-72.

128.s: Where is Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, located?
128.x: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb.
xa: Balban's Tomb is the first in India in a **purely Indo-Islamic style**, with the **first true arch**.
Sher Shah's octagonal tomb in a tank at Sasaram was **completed** by **Islam Shah**.
Humayun's Tomb uses **red sandstone + white marble**.

Match List I with List II:
List I (Monument)
a. Sher Shah's Tomb, Sasaram (completed)
b. Citadel of Purana Qila (begun)
c. Humayun's Tomb
d. Sikandar Lodi's Tomb
List II (Builder)
i. Bega Begum
ii. Ibrahim Lodi

128.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram was completed by Islam Shah (1545); the Purana Qila (Dinpanah) citadel was begun by Humayun and given its present form by Sher Shah; Humayun's Tomb was built by Bega Begum; Sikandar Lodi's tomb by his son Ibrahim Lodi.

128.s: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, built by Sher Shah Suri, was constructed under the supervision of:
128.x: Rohtas Fort was begun in 1541 under Todar Mal; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

128.s: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located at:
128.x: Sher Shah's tomb is at Sasaram in Bihar.

128.s: From which place were Jayata and Kumpa associated who impressed Shershah with their valour?
128.x: Jaita and Kumpa were the generals of Maldeo Rathore of Marwar who fought Sher Shah at Samel (1544) with great valour.

128.s: Which of the following rulers at first assumed the title of ‘Hazrat-e-Ala’ and afterwards ‘Sultan’?
128.x: Sher Khan took the title Hazrat-e-Ala after defeating Nusrat Shah of Bengal, and became Sher Shah (Sultan) after Chausa (1539).

128.s: With which medieval ruler following statement is associated “I would have lost the empire just for a handful of millet’?
128.x: Sher Shah said it after the battle of Samel (1544), where Maldeo's generals Jaita and Kumpa nearly beat him: he had almost lost Hindustan for a handful of bajra (millet).

128.s:
Which among the following titles were assumed by the Sher Shah Suri?

I. Hazrat-e-Alam

II. Sultan

III. Zille-e-Ilahi

IV. Raiyat-e-Ala
Codes
128.x: Sher Shah took the titles Hazrat-e-Ala and then Sultan (Sher Shah) - I and II. Zill-e-Ilahi and Raiyat-e-Ala were not his titles.

128.s: With which medieval ruler would you associate the statement ‘I would have lost the empire just for a handful of millet’ ?
128.x: Sher Shah made the remark after the hard-won battle of Samel (1544) against Maldeo's Rajputs led by Jaita and Kumpa.

128.s: Death of Sher Shah Suri occurred in :-
128.x: Sher Shah died on 22 May 1545 during the siege of Kalinjar fort, wounded by a gunpowder explosion; he was buried at Sasaram.

128.s: From where did Fareed, who later on became Sher Shah Suri, get his education :
128.x: Farid (later Sher Shah) studied Arabic and Persian at Jaunpur, then called the 'Siraj-i-Hind'.

128.s: Last expedition of Sher Shah Suri was against which of the following States?
128.x: Sher Shah's last expedition was against Kalinjar (Kalanjar), where he died in May 1545 in a gunpowder accident.

128.s:
With reference to Sher Shah Suri, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. He was the architect of a brilliant administrative system.
2. However his qualities as a ruler were not more remarkable than his victories on the field of battle.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
128.x: Sher Shah was the architect of a brilliant administrative system (1 true), and his qualities as a ruler were MORE remarkable than his victories, so 2 is false.

128.s: From whom did Farid receive the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger?
128.x: The title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar, not Babur.
xa: He studied at **Jaunpur** and managed his father's jagir from **1511**.
⚠ **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s: Sher Shah fought the battle of Samel in 1544 against:
128.x: Sher Shah defeated Maldeo Rathore of Marwar at Samel in 1544.

128.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement of Sher Shah?
o: Capture of Raisen from Puran Mal
Victory at the First Battle of Panipat
128.x: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was won by Babur; Sher Shah defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540).

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding administration during Sher Shah Suri?

I. He divided his empire into Sarkars, which in turn was divided into Pargana.

II. He administered Sarkar and Paragana directly without using any other officials.
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
128.x: Sher Shah divided the empire into 47 sarkars, each split into parganas (I is correct), but ran them through officers such as the chief shiqdar, chief munsif, shiqdar, amin and fotedar, so II is wrong.

128.s:
Consider the following statements on Sher Shah's land revenue administration:
I. Land was classified into three categories on the basis of produce from the land.
II. Land was measured according to a uniform system.
III. 1/4 of the produce was collected as tax.
Which of the above statements are correct?
128.x: Sher Shah measured land by a uniform system (gaz-i-Sikandari) and classified it into three categories (good, middling, bad) by produce, so I and II are correct. The state's share was one-third, not one-fourth, so III is wrong.

128.s: Which medieval ruler introduced the system of “patta” and “qabuliyat” to help the peasants?
128.x: Sher Shah gave each peasant a patta (title deed stating the state's share) and took a qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) from him.

128.s: Kabuliyat and Patta was introduced by
128.x: Patta (title deed) and qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) were introduced by Sher Shah, not by Shivaji, Jahangir or Aurangzeb.

128.s: Kabuliyat and Patta as instruments of settlement were introduced by
128.x: Sher Shah introduced patta and qabuliyat as instruments of direct state-peasant settlement; Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah, Bahlul Lodi and Humayun did not.

128.s: In a Sur-era pargana, who were the Karkuns?
o: Writers keeping records in Hindi and Persian
Officers in charge of law and order in the pargana
Treasurers who kept the pargana's cash
Officers who assessed and collected revenue
128.x: Karkuns were writers who kept records in Hindi and Persian.

128.s: Which measure did Sher Shah's land survey use to measure land uniformly?
128.x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.
xa: State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **cash or grain**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "one-fourth" is false.
**Patta** = title deed given to the cultivator; **Qabuliyat** = deed of acceptance signed by the peasant.
The system became the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?
o: Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of average produce.
128.x: Sher Shah's rate was one-third of average produce, not one-fourth; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Sher Shah's classes: **good, middling, bad**.
His system was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024**: "one-fourth" for Sher Shah's share is false.

128.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Sur officer)
a. Chief Shiqdar (sarkar)
b. Chief Munsif (sarkar)
c. Amin (pargana)
d. Fotedar (pargana)
List II (Function)
i. Revenue and civil matters
ii. Assessment of revenue
iii. Treasurer
iv. Law and order
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
128.x: Correct code: a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii. In the Sur system the Chief Shiqdar of a sarkar kept law and order, the Chief Munsif dealt with revenue and civil matters, the pargana Amin assessed revenue and the Fotedar was the treasurer.

128.s: Under Sher Shah Suri, the term 'dagh' referred to:
128.x: Dagh was branding of horses and chehra the descriptive roll of soldiers; the silver coin was the rupiya.

128.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Sher Shah Suri's administration?
o: Local headmen made responsible for tracing crime
128.x: The mansabdari system was Akbar's; the other three were Sher Shah's measures.

128.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Term)
a. Patta
b. Qabuliyat
c. Jaribana
d. Muhasilana
List II (Meaning)
i. Collector's fee
ii. Deed of acceptance signed by the peasant
iii. Title deed stating the state's share
iv. Surveyor's fee
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
128.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i. The patta was the title deed stating the state's share; the qabuliyat the peasant's deed of acceptance; jaribana the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.

128.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Sher Shah's land revenue system was the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.
Reason (R): Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of the produce.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
128.x: A is true: Sher Shah's survey-based system was the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast. R is false: the state's share was one-third of the average produce, not one-fourth.

128.s: Hem Chandra Vikramaditya is famous in Indian history as –
128.x: Hem Chandra Vikramaditya is Hemu, Adil Shah Sur's Hindu general and prime minister, defeated at Panipat II (1556).

128.s: The successor of Sher Shah was
128.x: Sher Shah was succeeded by his second son Jalal Khan as Islam Shah (1545-53).

128.s: Who among the following was successor of Sher Shah?
128.x: Islam Shah (Jalal Khan), Sher Shah's second son, succeeded him and ruled 1545-53.

128.s: Who among the following rulers divided his troops into units of two hundred, two hundred fifty and five hundred?
128.x: Islam Shah Suri reorganised the army into units of 200, 250 and 500 troops; Sher Shah, Bahlul Lodi and Sikandar Shah did not.

128.s: Hemu was the army chief and Prime Minister of which Sur ruler?
128.x: Hemu served Muhammad Adil Shah and fought the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).

128.s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in:
128.x: 5 November 1556, between Akbar's forces (Bairam Khan) and Hemu.

128.s: The rate of land tax levied by Shershah was
128.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification Nos. 15/2011 & 18/2011) - General Studies & Mental Ability, Booklet Series A, held 27-05-2012 · Q83

128.src: APPSC Group-I Preliminary (Screening Test) 2023, Notification 28/2022, Paper I – General Studies (GS/1G/100), held 08-01-2023 · Q19
128.x: Sher Shah's Sarak-i-Azam (later the Grand Trunk Road) ran from the Indus to Sonargaon in Bengal and still exists.

128.s:
Consider the following statements on Sher Shah's land revenue administration :
I. Land was classified into three categories on the basis of produce from the land.
