Which of the above statements are correct ?
128.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test 2024 (Notification No. 12/2023), held 17-03-2024, Paper-I General Studies (GS/1G/100) · Q16
128.x: Sher Shah measured land uniformly and classified it as good, middling and bad by produce. The state's share was one-third of the produce, not one-fourth.

129.s: The first Indian ruler to organise Haj Pilgrimage from the state exchequer was
129.x: Akbar was the first Indian ruler to send Haj caravans at state expense (from 1576, under a Mir Haj); Alauddin, Firuz Tughlaq and Aurangzeb did not start it.

129.s: Which of one of the following factors is not conducive in establishing Akbar as a nationalist-
o: Administrative unity and unity in Law
129.x: Akbar never forsook Islam; his unity of law and administration, cultural synthesis and tolerant religious policy are what support calling him a nationalist.

129.s: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was
o: the mosque for the use of Royal Family
the hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions.
the room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs
129.x: The Ibadat Khana (1575) at Fatehpur Sikri was the hall where Akbar held religious discussions with scholars of various faiths.

129.s: Which ruler had promoted ‘’Din-i-Ilahi ?
129.x: Akbar promoted Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-Ilahi) in 1582.

129.s: Who constructed Ibadat Khana ?
129.x: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575.

129.s:
Reign of Akbar is known for :
(1) Annexation of regions
(2) Provincial administrative system
(3) Judicial administration
(4) His religious intolerance
Select the correct answer by using codes given below :
129.x: Akbar's reign is known for annexations, provincial administration and judicial administration; it was marked by tolerance (Sulh-i-Kul), not intolerance.

129.s: Who promulgated Din-i-Ilahi ?
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi was promulgated by Akbar in 1582.

129.s: The theory of ‘’Sulh-i-Kul’’ was promulgated by :-
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul (peace with all) was Akbar's principle; Nizamuddin Auliya and Nasiruddin Chirag were Sufis, Zainul Abidin a Kashmir sultan.

129.s: Akbar launched “Din-i-Ilahi” in the year_____
129.x: Akbar launched Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.

129.s: Who among the following rulers issued some coins with figures of Rama and Sita and Devanagari legend ‘Rama-Siya’ ?
129.x: Akbar issued coins with figures of Rama and Sita and the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'.

129.s: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was –
o: The mosque for the use of Royal Family
The hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars
The room in which the nobles belonging to different
129.x: The Ibadat Khana was the hall where Akbar held discussions with scholars of different religions.

129.s: The concept of ‘Sulh-i-Kul’ (universal peace and fraternity) adopted by Akbar was the result of :
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul grew out of Akbar's political generosity, religious tolerance and liberal cultural attitude - all three.

129.s: Who among the following emperors may be called “an enlightened despot” ?
129.x: Akbar, absolute yet liberal and reforming, is described as an enlightened despot.

129.s: Who of the following Muslim rulers abolished the pilgrimage tax?
129.x: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 (and jizya in 1564).

129.s: Who had led a deputation of Banaras pandits before the Mughal emperor to seek the abolition of pilgrim tax on Banaras and Allahabad ?
129.x: Kavindracharya Sarasvati led the Banaras pandits to Shah Jahan to seek the end of the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad.

129.s: ‘Din-i-Ilahi’ of Akbar was not a success because
o: after Akbar, it was not patronised.
the Muslims did not accept other religious practices.
it was not suitably projected to the masses.
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi failed for all three reasons: not patronised after Akbar, rejected by orthodox Muslims and never projected to the masses.

129.s: In which of the following years Akbar built Ibadatkhana?
129.x: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana in 1575 and opened it to all religions in 1578.

129.s: Among the following which Mughal Emperor introduced the policy of Sulh-i-Kul?
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul was Akbar's policy; the other three were not Mughal emperors.

129.s:
Causes of Akbar’s popularity were

I. Mansabdari customs

II. Religious policy

III. Land revenue system

IV. Social reforms
Select the correct answer by using codes given below.
129.x: Mansabdari, liberal religious policy, the Dahsala revenue system and social reforms all made Akbar popular.

129.s: The Mahzar or an attested statement signed by the seven leading Ulemas was issued by
129.x: The Mahzar (1579), drafted by Shaikh Mubarak and signed by leading Ulemas, made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes.

129.s: Which historian said ‘’Din-i-Ilahi’’ is a religion ?
129.x: None of these: Abul Fazl, Badauni and Nizamuddin did not call Din-i-Ilahi a religion - it was Mohsin Fani (Dabistan-i-Mazahib).

129.s:
What among the following is/are true about the priests who were sent to Akbar's court to resolve his curiosities toward Christianity in 1595 by Goa Church Authorities?
(i) This was the third mission of Goa Church Authorities which was sent to Akbar's court.
(ii) This session met Akbar in Lahore. (iii)Antonio Monserrate was included in this mission.
129.x: The 1595 mission (Jerome Xavier, Pinheiro, Bento de Goes) was the third and met Akbar at Lahore; Monserrate came with the first mission (1580): (i) and (ii).

129.s: Who among the following was conferred with the title of 'Jagat Guru' by Akbar?
129.x: Akbar honoured the Jain monk Hiravijaya Suri with the title Jagat Guru; Jinachandra Suri got 'Yuga Pradhan'.

129.s: Who was the renowned Jain Acharya, to be greatly honoured by Akbar?
129.x: Hiravijaya Suri was the Jain acharya most honoured by Akbar ('Jagat Guru').

129.s:
Arrange the following events of Akbar’s regime in their chronological order :
1. Abolition of Jizya
2. Construction of Ibadat Khana
3. Signing of Mahzar
4. Foundation of Din-i-Ilahi
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
129.x: Jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582: 1, 2, 3, 4.

129.s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.
129.tq: Discriminate the exact meaning of a Persian administrative-religious term.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** means **"peace with all"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **guiding principle** of Akbar's religious policy.
**Din-i-Ilahi** was **never forced** on anyone, so compulsory conversion is wrong.
xa: Measures: abolition of **jizya** (**1564**) and **pilgrimage tax** (**1563**), **Ibadat Khana**, **Mahzar**.
Shaikh Ahmad **Sirhindi** attacked Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi.
Akbar's coins showed **Rama and Sita** with the legend **'Rama-Siya'**.

129.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with Din-i-Ilahi?
o: Reverence for the sun and fire
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi included belief in one God, reverence for the sun and fire, and avoidance of meat-eating. It was never forcibly imposed on anyone.
129.tq: Reject the extreme compulsory feature that contradicts the voluntary character of the order.
xs: **Compulsory conversion of all subjects** was not a feature — Din-i-Ilahi was **never forced on anyone** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its features included **one God**, **reverence for sun and fire** and **avoiding meat**.
xa: Other features: greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, readiness to sacrifice wealth, high character.
Proclaimed in **1582**.
Orthodox critics: **Badauni** and Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.

129.s: Which of the following about Akbar's religious measures is NOT correct?
o: The pilgrim tax was remitted in 1563 and jizya abolished in 1564.
The Ibadat Khana was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575.
The Mahzar preceded the construction of the Ibadat Khana.
129.x: The Mahzar (1579) came after the Ibadat Khana (1575); the order is jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's religious measures:
1. He abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and the jizya in 1564.
2. The Ibadat Khana, built in 1575, was opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians only in 1578.
3. The Mahzar of 1579 was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: the pilgrimage tax and jizya went in 1563 and 1564, the Ibadat Khana (1575) was at first for Muslims and was thrown open to other faiths in 1578, and Shaikh Mubarak drafted the Mahzar.

129.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Tax)
a. Ushr
b. Zakat
c. Khums
d. Haqq-e-Sharb
List II (Meaning)
i. One-fifth of war booty
ii. Irrigation tax
iii. Alms tax on Muslims
iv. Land tax on Muslims
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Correct code: a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii. Ushr was the land tax on Muslims, zakat the alms tax on Muslims, khums one-fifth of war booty and haqq-e-sharb the irrigation tax.

129.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Measure)
a. Jizya reimposed (1679)
b. Grain tax ended
c. Jizya and cow slaughter ended
d. Privileges of Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis ended
List II (Ruler)
i. Sikandar Lodi
ii. Aurangzeb
iii. Zain-ul-Abidin
iv. Alauddin Khalji

129.x: Correct code: a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv. Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679; Sikandar Lodi (not Akbar) ended the grain tax; Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir ended the jizya and cow slaughter; Alauddin Khalji ended the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis.

129.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi is correct?
o: Todar Mal was its only Hindu member
It came to an end with Akbar's death
It had a mass following beyond Akbar's court
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi had only about 18 members; Abul Fazl was its chief exponent and Birbal its only Hindu member.

129.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass religion.
Reason (R): Akbar never forced it on anyone, and it remained a small voluntary circle.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
129.x: Both are true and R explains A: Din-i-Ilahi was never forced on anyone or projected to the masses; it stayed a voluntary circle of about 18 and so never became a mass religion.

129.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, called Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belonged to which Sufi order?
129.x: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi and criticised Akbar's religious ideas from an orthodox standpoint.

129.s: Which of the following did NOT criticise Akbar's religious ideas from an orthodox standpoint?
129.x: Abul Fazl was Akbar's admirer and chronicler.

129.s: The first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court (1580) included Antonio Monserrate and:
129.x: Acquaviva and Monserrate led the first mission from Goa; Jerome Xavier came with the third (1595).

129.s: The third Jesuit mission (1595), which included Jerome Xavier, met Akbar at:
129.x: Akbar was then holding court at Lahore; the second mission (1591) had come from Goa.

129.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Person)
a. Hiravijaya Suri
b. Jinachandra Suri
c. Guru Ram Das
d. Dastur Meherji Rana
List II (Honour or grant from Akbar)
i. Land grant to a Parsi priest
ii. Land on which Amritsar grew
iii. Title 'Jagat Guru'
iv. Title 'Yuga Pradhan'
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. Akbar gave the Jain Hiravijaya Suri the title Jagat Guru and Jinachandra Suri the title Yuga Pradhan; his land grant to Guru Ram Das let Amritsar grow; the Parsi Dastur Meherji Rana also received a land grant.

129.s: Who among the following was personally killed by Akbar?
129.x: Akbar personally killed Adham Khan, Maham Anaga's son, in 1562 for murdering the minister Atagh Khan.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bairam Khan:
1. Akbar gave the title of Khan-i-Khanan to Bairam Khan.
2. This title was not conferred upon Bairam Khan at the time of his appointment as wazir of the empire.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
129.x: Akbar made Bairam Khan his Wakil and gave him the title Khan-i-Khanan at that very time, so 1 is correct and 2 (not conferred at appointment) is wrong.

129.s: In which of the following place Akbar was enthroned on getting the information of Humayun’s death?
129.x: On news of Humayun's death, Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar in a garden at Kalanaur (Gurdaspur, Punjab) on 14 February 1556.

129.s: At the time of his coronation at Kalanaur the age Lat par The of Akbar was:
129.x:
Most books and keys: fourteen. Strictly, born 15 Oct 1542 and crowned 14 Feb 1556, he was 13 years 4 months (Rocket: 'age <14').
Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in February 1556 at about fourteen (NextGen: 'only fourteen years old'), so 'fourteen' is the intended answer; fifteen, eighteen and twenty are wrong.

129.s: Akbar ruled under the protection of Bairam Khan from
129.x: Bairam Khan was Akbar's regent from 1556 to 1560, when Akbar dismissed him; 1560-64 was the petticoat government.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Emperor Akbar marched towards Afghanistan in 1581 with a huge army.
2.
Reason (R): He was on his way to reclaim his ancestral country of Ferghana in Central Asia. Options:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

130.s: Under the Mughals, land whose revenue went directly to the imperial treasury was called:
130.x: Khalisa was crown land; a jagir gave only the right to collect revenue, and suyurghal was a charitable revenue-free grant.

130.s: Which of the following was NOT a category of land or grant under the Mughals?
130.x: Zabti was a system of revenue assessment (measurement), not a category of land; khalisa, jagir and suyurghal were.

Match List I with List II:

130.s:
Assertion (A) : During the time of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses.
Reason (R) : Horses had to be rested while on march and replacements were necessary in times of war.
o: Both (A) and (R) is true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
130.x: A mansabdar had to keep twenty horses for every ten cavalrymen because horses needed rest on the march and replacement in war, so R explains A.

130.s: In Akbar's mansabdari system, the term 'Sawar' denoted:
o: Number of horsemen to be maintained
130.x: Sawar indicated the cavalry to be maintained; zat denoted personal rank and pay.

130.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system is correct?
o: Mansabs were hereditary and passed to the son
Sawar denoted the personal rank of the noble
Zat denoted the personal rank and pay of the mansabdar
130.x: Zat was personal rank and pay; mansabs were not hereditary and lapsed to the state.

130.s: The mansabdari system had its origin in:
130.x: The decimal ranking of mansabs came from the Mongol military tradition.

130.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mughal mansabdari system?
o: It combined civil and military duties
Mansabdars were paid in cash or jagirs
Ranks were expressed as zat and sawar
130.x: Mansabs were not hereditary; they depended on the emperor's will.

130.s: The du-aspa sih-aspa system in the mansabdari was introduced by:
130.x: Jahangir introduced du-aspa sih-aspa, allowing a mansabdar to maintain extra horsemen.

130.s: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the 'sawar' rank indicated the:
o: Number of cavalrymen to be maintained
130.x: Zat fixed personal rank and pay; sawar fixed the number of horsemen.

130.s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left uncultivated for five years or more called?
130.x: Banjar was fallow 5+ years; Parauti 1-2 and Chachar 3-4 years.

a. Polaj
b. Parauti
c. Chachar
d. Banjar
List II (Status)
i. Fallow for 1-2 years
ii. Fallow for 3-4 years

130.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Akbar classified land into four categories for revenue.
Reason (R): Sher Shah classified land into three categories - good, middling and bad.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
130.x: Both are true: Akbar had four classes (polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar) and Sher Shah three (good, middling, bad). But Sher Shah's scheme does not explain Akbar's four-fold one, so R is not the explanation of A.

130.s: Which of the following about Mughal central ministers is NOT correct?
o: The Mir Saman was in charge of religious affairs.
The Wakil was the highest in rank.
The Wazir handled revenue, treasury and accounts.
130.x: The Mir Saman looked after the royal household and karkhanas; religious affairs were with the Sadr-us-sudur.

130.s: Which of the following pairs (Unit – Officials) is correctly matched?
130.x: The pargana had the shiqdar, amil and qanungo. The sarkar had the faujdar and amalguzar, the town the kotwal, and the village the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.
xa: The **Faujdar** handled law and order; the **amalguzar** handled revenue.
The **Kotwal** looked after police and municipal order.
**Suba** officials: Subedar, diwan, bakhshi, sadr, qazi.

130.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Jagir type)
a. Tankha
b. Watan
c. Mashrut
d. In'am
List II (Feature)
i. In lieu of salary; transferable every 3-4 years
ii. Reward with no service obligation
iii. Hereditary; not transferable
iv. Conditional, tied to specified duties
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
130.x: Correct code: a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii. Tankha jagirs were in lieu of salary and transferred every 3-4 years; watan jagirs were the zamindar's hereditary homeland; mashrut jagirs were conditional on duties; in'am jagirs were rewards without service.

130.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A jagirdari crisis developed under Aurangzeb.
Reason (R): There were too many mansabdars for too few jagirs.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
130.x: Both are true and R explains A: the jagirdari crisis of Aurangzeb's time arose because there were too many mansabdars for too few jagirs, which also raised pressure on the peasants.

130.s:
Match List I with List II:

a. Wakil
b. Mir Bakhshi

130.x: Correct code: a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii. The Wakil was highest in rank but lost his financial powers; the Mir Bakhshi handled military matters (dagh, chehra, promotions); the Sadr-us-sudur religious affairs and charitable grants; the Mir Saman the royal household and karkhanas.

130.s: In 1580, Akbar divided the Mughal empire into how many subas?
130.x: Akbar divided the empire into 12 subas in 1580; the number later rose to 15.

130.s: In the Mughal administration, the kotwal was responsible for:
130.x: The kotwal kept order in towns; villages had the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.

131.s: Which son of Shah Jahan was honored with the title 'Shah-i-Iqbal'?
131.x: Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir, was honoured by Shah Jahan with the titles Shah-i-Iqbal and Shah Buland Iqbal.

131.s: Mughal Prince who took refuge in Srinagar Garhwal –
131.x: Sulaiman Shikoh, Dara's son, took refuge with Prithvi Shah of Srinagar Garhwal; Medini Shah later handed him over to Aurangzeb.

131.s: Who among the following was given the title of ‘Shah Buland Iqbal’ by Shah Jahan?
131.x: Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir, bore the title Shah Buland Iqbal.

131.s: To whom Aurangzeb bestowed upon the title of ‘Sahibat-uz-Zamani’ ?
131.x: Aurangzeb gave Jahanara the title Sahibat-uz-Zamani; Roshanara was Padshah Begum. Shaista Khan and Amin Khan were nobles.

131.s: Name the title given by Shah Jahan to Dara Shikoh?
131.x: Dara Shikoh's title was Shah Buland Iqbal (Shahzada-e-Buland Iqbal); the other options are invented.

131.s: Taj Mahal was constructed in the memory of
131.x: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum), who died in 1631. Nur Jahan built Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb.

131.s: Who among the following was the daughter of Emperor Aurangzeb ?
131.x: Mehr-un-Nisa (b. 1661) was a daughter of Aurangzeb; Jahan Ara, Roshan Ara and Gauhar Ara were daughters of Shah Jahan.

131.s: Khusrau was the son of which Mughal emperor ?
131.x: Khusrau was the eldest son of Jahangir (mother Man Bai) and rebelled in 1606.

131.s: The actual name of Mumtaz Mahal was
131.x: Mumtaz Mahal was Arjumand Banu Begum, Asaf Khan's daughter, who married Khurram in 1612. Mehrunnisa is Nur Jahan's name.

131.s: Who among the following shifted the capital of the Empire from Agra to Delhi ?
131.x: Shah Jahan shifted the capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi), founded in 1638.

131.s: Who was the ‘Poet-Laureate’ of Shah Jahan’s reign?
131.x: Abu Talib Kalim (Kaleem) was Shah Jahan's poet laureate (malik-ush-shuara). Qudsi and Munir were other poets of the period.

131.s: In Indian history, who was Abdul Hamid Lahori?
o: An important military commander during Akbar’s reign
An official historian of the reign of Shah Jahan
An important noble and confidant of Aurangzeb
A chronicler and poet during the reign of Muhammad
131.x: Abdul Hamid Lahori was the official historian of Shah Jahan and wrote the Padshahnama, not a commander or a noble of Aurangzeb.

131.s: ……… was imprisoned for lifetime by Aurangzeb.
131.x: Aurangzeb kept Shah Jahan captive in Agra Fort from 1658 till his death in 1666.

131.s: Which Mughal Emperor abolished the Persian Court Custom of ‘Sijda’ which was begun by Balban?
131.x: Shah Jahan abolished the court custom of sijda (prostration) begun by Balban, replacing it with the chahar taslim.

131.s: Which Mughal Emperor Started Hijri Samvat in India by replacing Illahi samvat?
131.x: Shah Jahan gave up Akbar's solar Ilahi era and restored the Hijri (lunar) reckoning for regnal years.

131.s: During whose reign was the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri compiled?
131.x: The Fatawa-i-Alamgiri belongs to Aurangzeb's reign, not Shah Jahan's 'Golden Age'.
xa: Shah Jahan also annexed **Baglana** and **Bundelkhand**.
The **Peacock Throne** stood in the **Diwan-i-Khas**; **Nadir Shah** took it in **1739**.
⚠ Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox (some new temples destroyed) but kept many Hindu nobles.

131.s: In which field is Shah Jahan's reign called the Mughal 'golden age'?
131.x: Shah Jahan's reign is the golden age of Mughal architecture (Taj Mahal, Lal Qila, Jama Masjid).

131.s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Relation / fact):
List-I
a. Jagat Gosain
b. Jahanara
c. Roshanara
d. Sulaiman Shikoh
List-II
i. Eldest daughter of Shah Jahan; nursed him in captivity
ii. Dara's son; took refuge with Prithvi Shah of Srinagar Garhwal
iii. Jahangir's Rathor wife; mother of Shah Jahan
iv. Backed Aurangzeb; Padshah Begum
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
131.x: Jagat Gosain – Jahangir's Rathor wife, mother of Shah Jahan; Jahanara – eldest daughter who backed Dara and nursed the captive Shah Jahan; Roshanara – backed Aurangzeb, Padshah Begum; Sulaiman Shikoh – Dara's son, sheltered in Srinagar Garhwal and handed over by Medini Shah.

131.s: The Persian translation of the Upanishads made by Dara Shikoh is called:
131.x: Sirr-i-Akbar is the Persian translation of the Upanishads; Majma-ul-Bahrain compares Sufism and Vedanta.

131.s: Which of the following works is NOT associated with Dara Shikoh?
131.x: The Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl.

131.s: The Peacock Throne made for Shah Jahan was carried away in 1739 by:
131.x: Nadir Shah carried off the Peacock Throne after sacking Delhi in 1739.

131.s:
Assertion (A): Shah Jahan expelled the English from Hughli in 1632.
Reason (R): The Europeans at Hughli were punished for their trading abuses.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
131.x: A is false: it was the Portuguese whom Shah Jahan beat at Hughli in 1632. R is true: they were attacked for trading abuses. Hence A false, R true.

131.s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author / nature):
List-I
a. Padshahnama
b. Shahjahannama
c. Adab-i-Alamgiri
d. Sirr-i-Akbar
List-II
i. Dara Shikoh
ii. Abdul Hamid Lahori
iii. Inayat Khan
iv. Letters of Aurangzeb, incl. the father-son money dispute
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
131.x: Padshahnama – Abdul Hamid Lahori, Shah Jahan's official historian; Shahjahannama – Inayat Khan; Adab-i-Alamgiri – Aurangzeb's letters (including the father-son money dispute); Sirr-i-Akbar – Dara Shikoh's Persian Upanishads.

131.s: Shah Jahan shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to:
131.x: Shah Jahan built Shahjahanabad at Delhi (1638-48) and moved the capital there.

131.s: After his deposition in 1658, Shah Jahan was confined in Agra Fort and nursed by his daughter:
131.x: Jahanara stayed with Shah Jahan in Agra Fort till his death in 1666; Roshanara sided with Aurangzeb.

131.s: Who among the following wives of Jahangir committed suicide?
131.x: Shah Begum (Man Bai), Jahangir's Rajput wife and Khusrau's mother, took an overdose of opium in 1605, distressed by the quarrels between her husband and son. Nur-un-Nissa, Karamsi and Malika-e-Jahan were other wives.

131.s: Which among the following is not correctly matched? Emperor Amir
131.x: Sawai Jai Singh of Amber rose under Aurangzeb and the later Mughals (Muhammad Shah), not Jahangir, so that pair is wrong. Tardi Beg served Babur and Humayun, Bairam Khan was Humayun's (and Akbar's) noble, and Jaswant Singh served Aurangzeb.

131.s: Jahangir took shelter at which of the following fort?
131.x: Orchha's Bundela chief Bir Singh Deo was Prince Salim's ally (he killed Abul Fazl for him in 1602) and built the Jahangir Mahal for him, which is why the printed key is Orchha. Gwalior was a state prison, and Dhar and Narwar have no such link.

131.s:
Of the following who had rebelled against the Mughal Emperor Jahangir?

I. Asif Khan

II. Khurram

III. Mahabat Khan

IV. Khusrau
Codes
131.x: Khusrau (1606), Khurram (1622-26) and Mahabat Khan (1626 coup) all rebelled against Jahangir. Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and a junta member, not a rebel.

131.s: In whose reign was the ‘Treaty of Chittor’ signed between Mughal and the Rana of Mewar ?
131.x: Rana Amar Singh of Mewar submitted to Jahangir in 1615 (Treaty of Chittor); Mewar and Chittor were restored and his son Karan Singh became a mansabdar. Akbar never got Mewar's submission.

131.s:
Which of the following incidents took place during the reign of Jahangir?
I. The fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev was sentenced to death.
II. Victory over Rajputs of Mewar.
III. Annexation of Kabul and Kandahar.
IV. Arrival of English East India Company to India.
131.x: Guru Arjan Dev's execution (1606), Mewar's submission (1615) and the English arrival (Hawkins 1608, Roe 1615) all fall in Jahangir's reign. Kandahar was lost by Jahangir in 1622, not annexed, so III is wrong.

131.s: What was the childhood name of Nur Jahan?
131.x:
Printed APPSC key: Bahu Begam. Verified: Mehr-un-Nisa (NextGen, PMF, Britannica).
Nur Jahan was born Mehr-un-Nisa (Mehrunnisa; 'Maharul Nisa' here), daughter of Mirza Ghiyas Beg. 'Bahu Begam' in the printed APPSC key is not her name in any standard source, and Mumtaz was Arjumand Banu's title.

131.s: Who of the following was not a member of Noorjahan’s Junta?
131.x: The junta was Nur Jahan, her mother Asmat Begum, her father Ghiyas Beg, her brother Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram. Jahangir himself was not a member.

131.s: Who among the following was not a member of 'Nurjahan's Junta'?
131.x: Mahabat Khan was not in the junta; he was its rival who seized Jahangir in 1626. Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg), Asaf Khan and Khurram were members.

131.s: Mehrunnisa who was known as Nur Jahan was the wife of
131.x: Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Nur Jahan.

131.s: Who of the following was not a member of Nur Jahan’s Junta?
131.x: Jahangir himself was not a member of the junta, which was made up of Nur Jahan, her parents, Asaf Khan and Khurram.

131.s:
Consider the following statements. In the reign of Jahangir, Kandhar could not be recaptured due to

I. inefficiency of Mughal army.

II. refusal of Khurram to proceed to that place.

III. difficulties in organising an expedition.

IV. severe cold in Afghanistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
131.x: Kandahar was lost in 1622 while Khurram, ordered to march there, refused and revolted; the expedition could not be organised and winter made it harder. Inefficiency of the Mughal army is not the accepted cause.

131.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
131.x: Jahangir wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian; Babur's Tuzuk-i-Baburi was in Turki.

131.s: The Mughal Emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was
131.x: Jahangir banned tobacco smoking (1617), as he records in his memoirs; Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb did not.

131.s: With which place is Salim Chishti of Akbar's reign associated?
131.x: Salim Chishti lived at Sikri in Akbar's time.
n: Guru Arjan Dev was executed during the reign of Jahangir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed during the reign of Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Salim Chishti was associated with Sikri during the reign of Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
xa: **Fa-Hien** visited under **Chandragupta II**; **Hiuen-Tsang** under **Harsha**.
**Ibn Battuta** came under **Muhammad bin Tughluq**.
Arjan Dev was executed for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.

131.s: Under which pen name did Nur Jahan write poetry?
131.x:
Some books give Nur Jahan the pen name Makhfi; the best-known Makhfi is Aurangzeb's daughter Zeb-un-Nissa (Diwan-i-Makhfi), and several Mughal court women used it.
Nur Jahan was also a poet; some books give her pen name as Makhfi ("the hidden one").
131.tq: Identify the literary pseudonym associated with the political personality.
xs: Some books give Nur Jahan the pen name **"Makhfi"** — so option **(3)**; ⚠ the best-known Makhfi is Aurangzeb's daughter **Zeb-un-Nissa** (Diwan-i-Makhfi).
**Jahanara** was Shah Jahan's **daughter**; **Padshah** was a title, not her pen name.
xa: Her titles: **Nur Jahan** ("Light of the World"), later **Padshah Begum**.
She built the **tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah** (Agra), with marble inlay — a precursor of the Taj.
Born **Mehrunnisa** in **1577** at **Kandahar**.

131.s: Which member of Nur Jahan's junta was her brother and Shah Jahan's father-in-law?
131.x: Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and father of Mumtaz Mahal; Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg) was her father.

131.s: Which of the following describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance, with temple destruction ordered across the empire
Reimposition of the jizya on non-Muslims and of the pilgrim tax on Hindu shrines throughout his reign
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
Making the Din-i-Ilahi compulsory for all mansabdars and nobles attending the imperial court
131.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed in **1606** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
Jahangir imprisoned **Guru Hargobind** at **Gwalior**.
Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title **"Shah Jahan"**.

131.s: Which Mughal general seized Emperor Jahangir on the banks of the Jhelum in 1626?
131.x: Mahabat Khan's coup of 1626 took Jahangir captive on the Jhelum.

131.s: Which of the following statements about revolts in Jahangir's reign is correct?
o: Prince Khusrau rebelled in 1606 and was defeated near Lahore.
Prince Khurram rebelled in 1606 and was blinded.
Nur Jahan supported Khurram against Shahryar.
Mahabat Khan seized Jahangir at Agra in 1622.
131.x: Khusrau rebelled in 1606; Khurram revolted in 1622-26 while Nur Jahan backed Shahryar.

131.s: Which of the following events did NOT take place in the reign of Jahangir?
131.x: Samugarh (1658) was fought in Shah Jahan's war of succession; Kandahar was lost in 1622, Kangra taken in 1620 and Mewar submitted in 1615.

131.s: By the Treaty of 1615 with Jahangir, which Mewar ruler submitted to the Mughals?
131.x: Rana Amar Singh submitted in 1615 and his son Karan Singh was made a Mughal mansabdar.

131.s: Which of the following statements about Nur Jahan is correct?
o: She built her father's tomb at Lahore
She was the widow of Bairam Khan
Her name appeared on Mughal coins and farmans
131.x: Nur Jahan, widow of Sher Afghan, married Jahangir in 1611; she was the only Mughal consort named on coins, and built Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb at Agra.

131.s:
Match List-I (Emperor) with List-II (Diwan):
List-I
a. Akbar
b. Jahangir
c. Shah Jahan
d. Aurangzeb

i. Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg)
ii. Sa'adullah Khan
iii. Asad Khan
iv. Muzaffar Khan Turbati

131.x: Akbar – Muzaffar Khan (Turbati); Jahangir – Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg, Nur Jahan's father); Shah Jahan – Sa'adullah Khan; Aurangzeb – Asad Khan.

131.s: Who among the following witnessed the insult and humiliations faced by Dara Shikoh after loosing Battle of succession with Aurangzeb?
131.x: Francois Bernier, Dara Shikoh's French physician, was in Delhi in 1659 and described Dara's humiliating parade. Hawkins and Terry came under Jahangir, and Manucci was Dara's artilleryman.

131.s: Dara Shikoh was buried at?
131.x: Dara Shikoh was executed in 1659 and buried in Humayun's Tomb in Delhi.

131.s: The battle of Dharmat was fought between
o: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Marathas
131.x: The Battle of Dharmat (15 April 1658) was fought near Ujjain between Aurangzeb (with Murad) and Dara Shikoh's forces under Jaswant Singh.

131.s: The battle of Dharmat was fought between :
o: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Marathas
131.x: The Battle of Dharmat (15 April 1658) was fought between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh's forces under Jaswant Singh.

131.s: Aurangzeb defeated Jaswant Singh, the King of Jodhpur in the Battle of Dharmat in 1658. Dharmat situated in which state?
131.x: Dharmat lies near Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.

131.s:
Assertion(A) : Aurangzeb succeeded Shah Jahan to the Mughal throne.
Reason (R) : The law of primogeniture was followed.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
131.x: Aurangzeb did succeed Shah Jahan, but by the sword: the Mughals had no rule of primogeniture, so R is false.

131.s:
Battle of Deorai
2. Defeat of Shuja near Banaras
3. Battle of Samugarh
4. Victory at Dharmat Select the correct answer from the code given below. Code:
131.x: Order: Shuja beaten near Banaras (Bahadurgarh, Feb 1658), Dharmat (Apr 1658), Samugarh (May 1658), Deorai (Mar 1659), so 2, 4, 3, 1.

131.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal war of succession (1657-59) is correct?
o: Samugarh was the last battle of the war.
Dharmat was the first battle of the war.
Deorai was the last battle of the war.
131.x: The order was Bahadurgarh, Dharmat, Samugarh, Khajwa and Deorai (1659).

131.s: Whom did Aurangzeb and Murad decisively defeat at Samugarh (1658)?
131.x: Samugarh near Agra was the decisive defeat of Dara; Jaswant Singh was beaten at Dharmat and Shuja at Khajwa.
xa: **Deorai** (Mar **1659**, near **Ajmer**) was Dara's final defeat.
Dharmat was near **Ujjain**; Samugarh near **Agra**.
The war was triggered by Shah Jahan's illness in **1657**.

131.s: Whom did Aurangzeb and Murad defeat in the Battle of Dharmat (1658)?
131.x: At Dharmat near Ujjain, Aurangzeb and Murad beat Jaswant Singh, who led Dara's army.

131.s: Where was Dara Shikoh buried after his execution by Aurangzeb?
131.x: Dara Shikoh, betrayed by Malik Jiwan, was buried in Humayun's Tomb.

131.s: After his defeat in the War of Succession, Shah Shuja fled to:
131.x: Shah Shuja, governor of Bengal, fled to Arakan, where he perished.

131.s: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
131.x: Sir Thomas Roe was James I's ambassador to Jahangir (1615-19), not Akbar, so that pair is wrong. Hawkins-Jahangir, Tavernier-Shah Jahan and Manucci-Aurangzeb are correct.

131.x: Jahangir received Roe at Ajmer in January 1616; he stayed till 1619.

131.x: Sir Thomas Roe came as James I's ambassador to Jahangir's court (1615-19) and obtained trade concessions.

131.s: Who among the following was appointed as a physician in the Mughal service ?
131.x: Niccolao Manucci, who came in 1656 as Dara's artilleryman, later practised as a physician in Mughal service. Bernier was physician to Dara Shikoh too, but books key Manucci; Careri and Tavernier were not physicians.

131.s: Which British ambassador came behind Jahangir from Ajmer to Mandu ?
131.x: Sir Thomas Roe accompanied Jahangir from Ajmer to Mandu (1616-17). Clive and Clyde belong to later British India.

131.s: Sir Thomas Roe, an Ambassador of James I of England came to India in year
131.x: Roe landed at Surat in September 1615 and stayed till 1619, so 1615 is the year of arrival; he was received at Ajmer in January 1616.

131.x: Ibn Battuta came under Muhammad bin Tughluq. Fa-Hien came under Chandragupta II, Hiuen-Tsang under Harsha, and the Portuguese reached Vijayanagara under Krishnadeva Raya.

Hiuen-Tsang visited India during the reign of Harsha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Portuguese travellers had contacts with Vijayanagara during the reign of Krishnadeva Raya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]

**Salim Chishti** is associated with **Sikri** in Akbar's reign.
Jahangir received **William Hawkins** (**1608**) and **Sir Thomas Roe** (**1615-1619**).

131.s: Which European traveller described the Peacock Throne of Shah Jahan?
131.x: The French jeweller Tavernier described the Peacock Throne.

131.s: Which Englishman reached Surat in 1608 and was given the title 'English Khan' by Jahangir?
131.x: William Hawkins came on the Hector in 1608.

131.s: Sir Thomas Roe came to Jahangir's court as the ambassador of:
131.x: Roe (1615–19) was James I's ambassador.

131.s:

131.s: The motive behind Shahjahan's Balkh campaign was to:
o: secure a friendly ruler in Balkh and Badakhshan which bordered Kabul
conquer Samarqand and Farghana, the Mughal homelands
fix the Mughal frontier on the 'scientific line', the Amu Daria
expand the Mughal Empire beyond the sub‑continent
131.x: Shah Jahan's Balkh campaign (1646-47) aimed to set up a friendly ruler in Balkh and Badakhshan, which bordered Kabul; the idea of reconquering Samarqand and Farghana or of a 'scientific line' on the Amu Darya is the tempting but rejected view.

131.s: During Mughal Empire, which of the provinces was lost in 1622, recovered in 1638?
131.x: Kandahar was lost to Persia in 1622 under Jahangir and regained in 1638 when Ali Mardan Khan surrendered it to Shah Jahan.

131.s: The loss of Qandahar was a big blow to the Mughal empire from the view point of
131.x: Kandahar was the frontier fortress commanding the routes between India, Persia and Central Asia, so its loss was a blow to a strategic stronghold. It was not valued for resources.

131.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): During the reign of Shahjahan, Dara Sikoh was sent on expedition to Balkh, Badakhshan and Qandahar.
2.
Reason (R): The expedition sent by Shahjahan to the Middle East was a marvellous success.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
131.x:
Most keys: A true, R false. Strictly A is also inexact: Dara did not lead the Balkh-Badakhshan campaign (Murad 1646, Aurangzeb 1647).
The expeditions failed, so R is false. The printed key takes A as true, but Dara led only the 1653 Qandahar siege; Balkh and Badakhshan were Murad's and Aurangzeb's.

131.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
131.x: The Balkh-Badakhshan campaign was commanded first by Murad Bakhsh and later by Aurangzeb, not Dara Shikoh. Dara Shikoh commanded the 1653 Kandahar siege.
131.tq: Find the swapped commander in a campaign-person match.
xs: **Balkh-Badakhshan 1646-47 — Dara Shikoh** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
That campaign was led by **Murad Bakhsh**, then **Aurangzeb**.
The other pairs are right: **1649** and **1652** sieges — **Aurangzeb**; **1653** — **Dara Shikoh**.
xa: Balkh aim: secure the **Kabul frontier** and ancestral lands (**Samarkand** dream); withdrawn with heavy losses.
After **1653**, Kandahar was **lost for good**.
Kandahar had been recovered in **1638** through **Ali Mardan Khan**.

131.s: The Persian governor who surrendered Kandahar to Shah Jahan in 1638 was:
131.x: Ali Mardan Khan surrendered Kandahar in 1638; Persia took it back in 1649 and later Mughal sieges failed.

131.s: Which Mughal prince led the unsuccessful siege of Kandahar in 1653?
131.x: Aurangzeb's sieges (1649, 1652) and Dara Shikoh's siege (1653) all failed, and Kandahar was lost for good.

131.s: Who among the following was the governor of Deccan for the major part of Shah Jahan’s Reign ?
131.x: Aurangzeb was viceroy of the Deccan in 1636-44 and again in 1652/53-58, the greater part of Shah Jahan's reign.

131.s:
Assertion (A) Daulatabad fortress was besieged by the Mughal forces in the year 1631 and it had to be surrendered to them.
Reason (R) Malik Amber betrayed his sultan during the seige of Daulatabad fortress by Mughal forces.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
131.x:
Most keys: A true, R false. Strictly Daulatabad fell in June 1633, not 1631 (Satish Chandra), so A is also inexact.
Daulatabad did fall to the Mughals (Mahabat Khan) in Shah Jahan's early years, so the printed key takes A as true. R is false: Malik Ambar died in 1626; it was his son Fath Khan who surrendered the fort.

131.s: Which statement about Abul Hasan Tana Shah is correct?
o: He employed Madanna and Akkanna and helped Shivaji.
He led the Satnami revolt at Narnaul.
He founded the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
131.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, employed Madanna and Akkanna and helped Shivaji.
xa: He was Golconda's **last ruler**; Golconda annexed **1687** as the **21st suba**.
He was exiled to **Daulatabad** and died in **1699**.
General **Qamruddin Chin Qilich Khan** played a key role in the annexation.

131.s: In which year did the Mughals annex the Nizam Shahi state of Ahmadnagar?
131.x: Ahmadnagar was annexed under Shah Jahan in 1636; 1687 is the annexation of Golconda.
xa: **Mahabat Khan** was then made Deccan governor.
⚠ **1636** = Ahmadnagar + treaties; **1686** = Bijapur; **1687** = Golconda.
The Deccan was organised into four subas: **Khandesh, Berar, Telangana, Daulatabad**.

131.s: Who was Jahangir's envoy to Golconda?
131.x: Jahangir sent Mir Makki; Mir Jumla is linked with Aurangzeb's 1656 attack on Golconda.
xa: Golconda paid Mughal tribute from **1636** (**2 lakh hun**).
Annexation of Golconda (**1687**) brought **Andhra** under the Mughals.
**Abul Hasan Tana Shah** employed **Madanna and Akkanna**.

131.s: During which periods did Aurangzeb serve as viceroy of the Deccan?
131.x: Aurangzeb was Deccan viceroy in 1636-44 and 1652-58.

131.s: Aurangzeb, as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan, attacked Golconda in 1656 at the urging of:
131.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda noble who went over to the Mughals, urged Aurangzeb's 1656 attack on Golconda.

131.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four subas of the Mughal Deccan under Shah Jahan?
131.x: The four subas were Khandesh, Berar, Telangana and Daulatabad; Golconda was still a Qutb Shahi kingdom.

132.s: Which one of the following emperors had the highest number of Hindu Generals in the Mughal army:
132.x: The Hindu share in the nobility was highest under Aurangzeb (about 31.6%, mostly Marathas from the Deccan wars), against about 22.5% under Akbar.

132.s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
132.x: Aurangzeb, simple and orthodox in his personal life, was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint).

132.s: Who of the following Mughal Emperor was coronated twice?
132.x: Aurangzeb was crowned twice - at Delhi on 21 July 1658 and again on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

132.s: The Mughal Emperor who appointed the maximum number of Hindu officials was –
132.x: Aurangzeb had the largest number of Hindu officials (about 31.6% of the nobility), mainly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

132.s: Who among the following was called as a 'Zindapir'?
132.x: Aurangzeb was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint) for his simple, pious life.

132.s: The meaning of ‘Jihad’ carried on by Aurangzeb is
132.x:
Printed key: Dar-ul-Islam. Verified meaning: holy war.
Jihad means holy war – the war to turn dar-ul-harb (land of non-believers) into dar-ul-Islam. Dar-ul-Islam, printed in the key, is the aim of jihad, not its meaning; jizya is a tax.

132.s: Who re-imposed Jizya ?
132.x: Akbar abolished jizya in 1564; Aurangzeb re-imposed it in 1679.

132.s: During Aurangzeb’s reign, whose duty was to see that people lived their lives in accordance with the ‘shariat’?
132.x: The Muhtasib (censor of morals) saw that people lived by the shariat; Aurangzeb appointed them across the empire. Ahadis and Walashahis were troops and mansabdars were ranked officers.

132.s: Which royal woman received the title Padshah Begum under Aurangzeb?
132.x: Roshanara, who backed Aurangzeb in the succession war, was Padshah Begum; Jahanara was Sahibat-uz-Zamani.

132.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose the jizya?
132.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679; Akbar had abolished it in 1564.

132.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Aurangzeb?
132.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya (1679); Akbar had abolished it.

132.s: Which musical instrument did Aurangzeb play, though he banned music at his court?
132.x: Aurangzeb banned court music, yet he played the veena himself.

132.s: What was the regnal title of Aurangzeb?
132.x: Aurangzeb took the title Alamgir ('World Conqueror').

132.s: The 'Child's War' (1686–90), the first Mughal war with the English, took place during the reign of:
132.x: Josiah Child's East India Company fought Aurangzeb's Mughal empire in 1686–90.

132.s:

b. Order of 1669

ii. State-made secular regulations
iii. Demolition of the Kashi Vishwanath and Keshava Rai temples
iv. Officers who saw that people lived by the Sharia

132.x: Jizya – re-imposed 1679 (Akbar had abolished it in 1564); 1669 order – Kashi Vishwanath and Keshava Rai (Mathura) demolished; Muhtasibs – saw that people lived by the Sharia; Zawabit – state-made secular regulations.

132.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

132.x: Both are true and R explains A: Athar Ali finds Hindu nobles at about 31.6% in 1679-1707, many of them Marathas absorbed during the Deccan wars.

132.s: Who among the following changed the Rajput policy of the Mughals?
132.x: Aurangzeb broke with the Rajput policy of his predecessors by taking Marwar under direct control in 1679, which led to the Rajput war. Khurram, Shah Jahan and Dara did not change it.

132.s: Which son of Aurangzeb revolted against his father, weakening the latter’ position against the Rajputs?
132.x: Prince Akbar (called 'Akbar II' in the options) revolted in 1681 and joined the Rajputs, weakening Aurangzeb against them. Azam, Muazzam and Kam Bakhsh did not.

132.s: The Jat State of Bharatpur was established by?
132.x: Churaman built the Jat power after 1700 and Badan Singh formally founded the state of Bharatpur (1722); Suraj Mal later expanded it.

132.s: Who was known as the Plato of the Jat tribe?
132.x: Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur (r. 1755-63) was called 'the Plato of the Jat tribe' by a contemporary historian for his political wisdom.

132.s: The root of which among the following revolt lies in the problem faced by the farmers?
132.x: The Jat revolt (Gokula, 1669) was a peasant revolt against heavy revenue, and the Satnami revolt (1672) was by peasants and artisans, so both were agrarian. The Rajput, Sikh and Maratha conflicts were political.

132.s: The leaders of Jat who plundered Akbar’s tomb was
132.x: Jat leader Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra in the 1680s. Gokula led the 1669 revolt and Churaman came later.

132.s: The Satnami rebellion took place during the reign of Mughal emperor
132.x: The Satnami revolt broke out at Narnaul in 1672, under Aurangzeb (1658-1707).

132.s: Which tribes were involved in the Afghan revolt against Aurangzeb?
132.x: The Afghan revolt involved the Yusufzai and Afridi tribes of the north-west.
132.tq: Distinguish tribal groups from the regional and dynastic participants in other revolts.
xs: The Afghan revolt involved the **Yusufzai and Afridi** tribes of the north-west — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jats** (Mathura) and **Satnamis** (Narnaul) were separate revolts; **Marathas and Rajputs** were other opponents.
xa: Jats: under **Gokula** (**1669**).
Satnamis: **Narnaul** (**1672**).
Rajputs: **Marwar and Mewar**, under **Durgadas Rathore**.

132.s: What was the result of Aurangzeb's handling of the Marwar and Mewar resistance?
o: The Rajputs becoming the chief pillar of his empire
Peaceful acceptance of the Mughal succession in Marwar
The breaking of the Rajput alliance that had supported Akbar's empire
132.x: The clumsy handling of Marwar and Mewar broke the Rajput alliance that had been a pillar of Akbar's empire and cost the Mughals considerable influence.
xa: Marwar: **Durgadas Rathore** championed posthumous heir **Ajit Singh**.
Mewar: Rana **Raj Singh** joined Marwar.
**Prince Akbar** joined the Rajputs in **1681**.

b. Rajaram (Jat)
c. Churaman

ii. Jat revolt of 1669 in the Mathura (Tilpat) region

132.x: Gokula – Jat peasant revolt of 1669 around Mathura (Tilpat); Rajaram – plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra (1680s); Churaman – built the power that became Bharatpur (after 1700); Satnamis – 1672 revolt at Narnaul.

132.s: Suraj Mal, called 'the Plato of the Jat tribe', ruled the Jat state of:
132.x: Badan Singh founded the Jat state of Bharatpur; Suraj Mal (1755-63) was its greatest ruler.

132.s: The Satnami revolt of 1672 against Aurangzeb broke out at:
132.x: The Satnamis of Narnaul rose in 1672; Guru Ghasidas belongs to the 19th century.

132.s: During Aurangzeb's Rajput war of 1679-81, the claim of Ajit Singh of Marwar was championed by:
132.x: Durgadas Rathore championed Jaswant Singh's posthumous son Ajit Singh.

132.s: Which Mughal prince revolted against Aurangzeb, joined the Rajputs in 1681 and later fled to Sambhaji?
132.x: Prince Akbar, Aurangzeb's son, joined the Rajputs and later took refuge with Sambhaji.

132.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

132.x: Both are true. R explains A: the Zafarnama rebukes Aurangzeb for this broken promise.

132.s: Who was the ruler of Golconda when Aurangzeb seized the fort of Golkonda in 1687?
132.x: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was the ruler when Golconda fell in 1687. Sikandar Adil Shah ruled Bijapur, and Shaista Khan was a Mughal noble.

132.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors spent a greater part of his reign to overthrow the Deccan Kingdoms?
132.x: Aurangzeb spent the last 25-27 years of his reign in the Deccan, conquering Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687) and fighting the Marathas.

132.s: The Mughal Empire extended up to Tamil territory in the South under the reign of
132.x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached its greatest extent: after Bijapur and Golconda, Mughal armies pursued the Marathas to Jinji in Tamil country.

132.s: Which Mughal emperor captured the kingdom of Golconda in 1687?
132.x: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda in 1687.

132.s: When did Aurangzeb get the victory over Bijapur ?
132.x: Bijapur fell to Aurangzeb in September 1686 after a long siege.

132.s: The given map refers to the kingdom of :
o: Akbar at the time of capture of Khandesh in 1601
Akbar at the time of his death in 1605
Aurangzeb at the time of capture of Hyderabad
Aurangzeb at the time of his death in 1707
132.x: A map with Bijapur and Golconda inside the empire shows Aurangzeb's empire at his death in 1707; Akbar's empire never held them.

132.s: Who was the last ruler of Bijapur when Aurangzeb annexed it in 1686?
132.x: Sikandar Adil Shah was the last ruler of Bijapur; Tana Shah was Golconda's.

132.s: The fall of Golconda to Aurangzeb in 1687 ended the rule of which dynasty over Andhra?
132.x: Golconda fell in 1687 and Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was imprisoned, ending Qutb Shahi rule over Andhra; Golconda became a Mughal suba.
xa: **Bhakta Ramadasu** was the nephew of **Akkanna-Madanna**.
**Abdullah Pani** opened the gates; **Abdur Razzaq Lari** defended it.
Tana Shah died in **1699**; buried at **Khuldabad**.

132.s: Why was the prolonged 27-year Deccan war described as the 'Deccan Ulcer'?
o: prevented the annexation of Bijapur and Golconda
drained the Mughal treasury through prolonged warfare
strengthened the Mughal treasury through continuous tribute
132.x: The 27-year Deccan war drained the Mughal treasury and was therefore called the 'Deccan Ulcer', in comparison with Napoleon's Spanish Ulcer.
132.tq: Infer the consequence of a prolonged policy from the descriptive historical term.
xs: The **27-year** Deccan war **drained the treasury** — the **"Deccan Ulcer"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was compared to **Napoleon's Spanish Ulcer**.
Bijapur and Golconda were in fact annexed (**1686-87**), and the Maratha war went on till his death.
xa: Phase IV (**1687-1707**): war against the **Marathas** till death.
Aurangzeb spent **25-27** years camped in the Deccan.
He died in **1707** at **Ahmednagar**.

132.s: In which year did Aurangzeb annex Golconda as the 21st Mughal suba?
132.x: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda on 3 October 1687; 1679 is the year jizya was revived.

132.s: Who defended the Golconda fort against Aurangzeb in 1687?
132.x: Abdur Razzaq Lari held the fort; the traitor Abdullah Pani opened a gate.

132.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal conquest of Golconda (1687) is correct?
o: Mir Jumla defended the Golconda fort.
Abul Hasan Tana Shah was buried at Khuldabad.

Bhakta Ramadasu was the son of Madanna.
